news.head: Drake London quiet in loss to Panthers
news.body: Drake London caught four of five targets for 51 yards in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.impact: London had a better game than last week, but it still is nowhere near what you drafted him to do. The Falcons' quarterback play has been abysmal so far, which is the primary contributor to his struggles. But hopefully Michael Penix can fix things if he can return on Thursday.

news.head: Drake London held to two catches in Week 1 loss
news.body: Drake London caught two of his four targets for 29 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1. He also gained six yards on his lone carry in the game.
news.impact: London was quiet in the close loss, although his 29 receiving yards were good enough for him to finish second on the Falcons in that category. The Falcons were forced to play Cooper Rush, their third-string QB, thanks to injuries, so London should bounce back once either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is ready to return to the field. London sets up as a low-end WR1 heading into Week 2 against Carolina.

news.head: Drake London: Extension is 'on top of mind' per GM Ian Cunningham
news.body: Falcons GM Ian Cunningham said an extension for Drake London is “on top of mind.”
news.impact: It appears an extension could be agreed to after the NFL Draft. London is entering the final year of his rookie contract. There should be a new deal agreed to at some point later in the offseason.

news.head: Drake London finds the end zone in Week 18
news.body: Drake London caught 4-of-8 targets for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons 19-17 win over the Saints.
news.impact: Despite struggling with Kirk Cousins to end the season, London closed the year on a high note with a touchdown. He missed the 1,000 yard mark after missing five games. He is set to head into the final year of his rookie deal where he should remain a WR1 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Tyjae Spears not practicing Wednesday due to soreness
news.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Tyjae Spears will not practice on Wednesday due to soreness.
news.impact: Spears and Tony Pollard both aren't practicing due to what is being described as "soreness". They'll need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.head: Tyjae Spears runs for 41 yards in Week 2
news.body: Tyjae Spears carried the ball seven times for 41 yards and caught both of his targets for 29 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.impact: Spears was productive as a complement to starter Tony Pollard. The veteran running back is still looking for his first touchdown of the season but he has four catches for 41 yards through two games. He will be a low-end flex option for fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Giants.

news.head: Tyjae Spears finishes with 24 all-purpose yards in Week 1
news.body: Tyjae Spears carried the ball three times for 12 yards and caught two of his four targets for 12 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Spears operated behind Tony Pollard, who had eight touches. It was not a great day for the Tennessee run game, as the Titans were playing from behind for the entire game. Spears at least drew an encouraging number of targets in the passing attack. He will be a low-end flex option heading into Week 2 against the Eagles.

news.head: Tyjae Spears racks up seven receptions in loss
news.body: Tyjae Spears ran three times for 18 yards and caught all seven of his targets for nine yards in the Titans' 41-7 loss to the Jaguars.
news.impact: Spears made his fantasy day with his receiving in PPR leagues, but the yards certainly didn't come with it. His nine yards were the fewest yards on seven catches since at least 2010. Spears has some PPR appeal, but in a split backfield, it's tough to see him as much more than a flex play in 2026.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor scores twice in overtime loss Sunday
news.body: Jonathan Taylor rushed the ball 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding four receptions for 40 yards through the air in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Taylor was the engine for Indianapolis' offense on Sunday night. He totaled 132 yards over the course of the night and was able to score two touchdowns on the ground. He has been very strong to start the season and should continue to be considered an elite fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor rushes for two touchdowns in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jonathan Taylor carried the ball 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns while also catching three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Taylor was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Colts offense to begin the season, averaging 5.2 yards per carry in the loss. The superstar running back will look to remain an impactful backfield option in Week 2 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor agrees to two-year, $44 million extension with Colts
news.body: Jonathan Taylor has agreed to a two-year, $44 million deal with the Indianapolis Colts that could be worth up to $47 million.
news.impact: The 27 year old is coming off of back-to-back 1,400 yard rushing seasons with at least 11 rushing touchdowns in each, including a ridiculous 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Taylor should be viewed as a top tier running back in 2026, and his deal secures his dynasty value for the next several seasons.

news.head: Jonathan Taylor struggles in Week 18
news.body: Jonathan Taylor ran for 26 yards on 14 carries in the Colts 38-30 loss against the Texans. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards receiving.
news.impact: Taylor struggled to get anything going on the ground to close the season. It was a struggle over the second half of the year for him after he was the favorite to win Offensive Player of the Year during the first half of the season. He should remain a high-end RB1 heading into next season.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson held to one catch in Week 2
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught his lone target for a nine-yard gain in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.impact: Robinson was quiet in what was almost an upset win over the Eagles. The Titans only passed for 183 yards in the contest with Elic Ayomanor leading the way. Through two games in Tennessee, Robinson has caught six of his seven targets for 47 scoreless yards. He will need to see more frequent work moving forward to be trustworthy in fantasy. The Titans will face the Giants in Week 3.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robninson goes for 38 yards in Week 1
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught five of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Robinson tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while leading the way with his five catches. The entire Tennessee offense struggled to move the ball in Week 1, which cut into Robinson's final stats. He will look to bounce back as a decent flex option in PPR leagues heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson (head) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
news.impact: As expected, Robinson's head injury is no longer an issue and he carries no injury designation heading into Week 1. He should be a full go against the Jets and projects to be a worthwhile streaming option in PPR formats.

news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson expected to play on outside and in slot with Titans
news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson told reporters he expects to play on the outside as well as in the slot with the Titans.
news.impact: Robinson branched out from being a slot-only wide receiver last season. It resulted in him reaching 1,000 yards for the first time in his career. He should step in as the top target for Cam Ward and the Titans.

news.head: Jameson Williams underwhelming in loss Thursday
news.body: Jameson Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 33 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.impact: Williams had another disappointing performance on Thursday night. He caught just two passes in this matchup against the Bills and was only able to turn that into 33 scoreless yards, leaving him with a poor fantasy total on the night. Fantasy managers should recognize his low week-to-week floor when determining whether or not to start him in any given game moving forward.

news.head: Jameson Williams sees nine targets in Week 1 win
news.body: Jameson Williams caught four of his nine targets for 45 yards in the Lions' 31-30 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 1.
news.impact: Williams would have offered even more of an explosive impact if not for a couple of deep throw drops on passes from quarterback Jared Goff. The wideout remains a high-impact, explosive pass-catching option for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 road contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Jameson Williams (shoulder) returns to practice
news.body: Jameson Williams resumed practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Williams missed the Lions’ last two practices. He made his way back on Wednesday.

news.head: Jameson Williams catches six passes in Week 18
news.body: Jameson Williams hauled in six passes for 74 yards during Detroit's 19-16 win over Chicago in the final game of the year.
news.impact: It was the sixth time this season that Williams caught at least six balls in a game. The third-year wideout continues to improve production as he established career-highs in receptions (65) and receiving yards (1,117) while tying a career-best with seven receiving touchdowns.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. underwhelming in win Sunday
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. rushed the ball eight times for 25 yards and caught two passes for six yards in Sunday's 24-17 win over the Baltimore Ravems.
news.impact: Week 2 exposed some major concerns for Etienne. Not only did he have a bad game as far as efficiency and fantasy output go, but the return of Alvin Kamara is proving to be a big issue for his fantasy value, as the 31-year old saw one more carry and four more targets in his first game back from injury. Unless this distribution of work changes in the near future, it looks like Etienne is going to have a volatile week-to-week ceiling with the presence of Kamara eating into his workload that much.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. sees 16 touches in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. rushed nine times for a team-high 46 yards while also hauling in seven of his nine targets for 32 yards in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Etienne Jr. made the most of his carries out of the backfield for a New Orleans offense that had trailed 21-0 at one point, averaging 5.1 yards per carry in the loss. The running back offers fantasy managers more potential in PPR formats, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. splits first-team reps with Alvin Kamara Wednesday
news.body: Travis Etienne Jr. split first-team reps with Alvin Kamara in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Etienne is likely to be the 1A in the Saints backfield with the contract he got in free agency. This will be a situation to monitor throughout training camp.

news.head: Travis Etienne Jr. signing with Saints
news.body: The Saints are signing RB Travis Etienne Jr. to a four-year, $52 million deal.
news.impact: The future of Alvin Kamara in the Saints backfield is uncertain as Etienne joins the group. The status of Kamara will need to be monitored the rest of the offseason. Either way, Etienne should be stepping into the lead role. He'll be on the low-end RB1/high-end RB2 radar for fantasy managers.

news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson limited to six carries in Week 2
news.body: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson tallied 43 rushing yards on six carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers. He caught 1-of-2 targets for three yards.
news.impact: Stevenson saw the majority of the carries go to TreVeyon Henderson after Stevenson fumbled the ball in the first quarter. Stevenson struggled with fumbles in 2025 and that could impact his usage moving forward if he is unable to improve his ball security. Stevenson and the Patriots will take on the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson totals 95 yards Wednesday
news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball 18 times for 51 yards and caught five passes for 44 yards in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Stevenson was New England's workhorse running back on Wednesday night with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) out of the lineup. He ran at an inefficient clip of 2.8 yards per carry on the night, but his fantasy total was saved by the fact that he caught five passes. He will be more efficient than this in the future but will lose passing work to Henderson when he's back, so he will likely continue to be touchdown dependent on a week-to-week basis.

news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson (eye) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson is questionable to return to Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Texans.
news.impact: Stevenson left the game early with a eye injury. TreVeyon Henderson should see more snaps in the Patriots backfield while he is sidelined.

news.head: Rhamondre Stevenson dominant in Week 18 win
news.body: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed the ball seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and caught two passes for 22 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Stevenson saw just nine touches over the course of the afternoon on Sunday, but that was all that he needed. He logged 150+ total yards and three touchdowns against Miami, which left him with a dominant fantasy total in that matchup. He is set to return to New England next season and will continue to be featured in a two-headed backfield with TreVeyon Henderson.

news.head: Colston Loveland catches one pass in Week 2
news.body: Colston Loveland caught one of his three targets for three yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Loveland has struggled to make an impact to begin the season, recording one reception or less in each of the first two games. The tight end remains a risky pass-catching option ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.head: Colston Loveland sees two targets in Week 1
news.body: Colston Loveland failed to catch either of his two targets in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Loveland was non-existent in an explosive Chicago offense for head coach Ben Johnson in the season opener, operating as more of an afterthought in the win. The tight end will look to get back on track in a Week 2 divisional contest against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Colston Loveland catches 10 passes and scores TD in Week 18
news.body: Colston Loveland caught a team-high 10 passes, on 13 targets, for 91 yards and a score in the Bears' 19-16 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
news.impact: Loveland, the first-round pick out of Michigan, is starting to get hot at the right time for the Bears. Over the last two weeks, the tight end has caught 16 passes for 185 yards and two touchdowns. After a slow start to the season (11 catches in the first six weeks), Loveland has caught 47 passes over his last ten games. He will look to remain a focal point of the offense during the postseason.

news.head: Colston Loveland sees 10 targets in Week 17 loss to 49ers
news.body: Colston Loveland hauled in six of his team-leading 10 targets for 94 yards and one touchdown in the Bears' 42-38 Week 17 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Loveland has made the most of modest involvement in the Chicago passing attack of late, recording one touchdown in three of his last six games. The tight end remains a boom-or-bust tight end option in all formats for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 18 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II tosses three touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 32-of-47 passing attempts for 382 yards and three touchdowns while adding 17 yards on the ground in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Mahomes had an electric game on Sunday night, throwing three touchdowns and totaling nearly 400 yards en route to a narrow win over the Colts. He has been terrific since his return from injury and should be considered a worthwhile starter with week-to-week upside on any given week.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) listed as full participant Wednesday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) was listed as a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: As expected, Mahomes continues to carry on at full health, logging a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. Fantasy managers should have very few concerns with his premature return from injury at this point, since he demonstrated his health in Week 1 in Kansas City's big win over the Broncos.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II scores three touchdowns in return game Monday
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II completed 15-of-27 passing attempts for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception while adding 23 yards and a touchdown on the ground in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Monday night marked Mahomes' first game back after suffering a serious knee injury that ended his 2025 season prematurely. He looked good in his first game back, totaling over 200 yards and scoring three touchdowns on the night, including one impressive rushing touchdown from over ten yards out. He and Kansas City's offense as a whole are looking promising right now and may be primed for a big season if they can stay healthy this year.

news.head: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Patrick Mahomes II (knee) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Mahomes II cleared through every obstacle in his way in recovering from a late-season knee injury in 2025-26, as the dynamic signal-caller looks to lead a revamped Kansas City offense back to the postseason beginning with the Week 1 divisional matchup against a disruptive Denver defense Monday night.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. totals 46 yards Sunday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 3-of-3 targets for 46 yards in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.impact: Godwin was mostly quiet for the second straight week as Baker Mayfield has continued to struggle. He'll be on the WR3/WR4 radar next week against the Vikings.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. hauls in four passes Sunday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught 4-of-4 targets for 40 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Godwin totaled 30 of his 40 yards on one reception. The Bucs offense was unable to get in sync with four lost fumbles. He'll remain a WR3 heading into Week 2 against the Browns.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. (soreness) does not practice Tuesday
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. did not practice on Tuesday to manage injuries and soreness.
news.impact: Godwin, Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka all sat out on Tuesday. It doesn't appear to be anything serious with any of them.

news.head: Chris Godwin Jr. quiet in Week 18
news.body: Chris Godwin Jr. caught his lone target for eight yards in the Bucs 16-14 win over the Panthers.
news.impact: It was a quiet day for the entire Bucs wide receiver room. Godwin showed flashes after working his way back to full health, but he struggled to finish the season. He'll be a bounce back candidate next year.

news.head: Tyler Warren hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: Tyler Warren hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: The young tight end had an up-and-down night on Sunday. On one hand, he finished with a touchdown and six catches on the night, which led to good results in PPR leagues. On the other hand, he only totaled 21 yards on his seven targets, which is poor as far as efficiency goes. Fantasy managers should continue to expect high volume from him moving forward, especially with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time.

news.head: Tyler Warren finds end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Tyler Warren hauled in three of his five targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in a 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: Warren was mostly bottled up by a stiff Baltimore defense, averaging 4.3 yards per reception in the Week 1 loss. The tight end remains a primary pass-catching offense for head coach Shane Steichen ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) practices Tuesday
news.body: Tyler Warren was able to practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Warren has been working his way back from a minor groin issue. He should be good to go for Week 1 next week.

news.head: Tyler Warren (groin) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Tyler Warren did not practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Warren remains likely to miss practice all of this week as he recovers from a groin injury. His status for Week 1 is not in danger yet if he can return to practice by next week.

news.head: Dallas Goedert suffers MCL sprain, to miss a few weeks
news.body: Dallas Goedert suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday’s win over the Titans.
news.impact: The injury is expected to sideline Goedert for at least a few weeks. DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon should all step up even more in the passing game for Jalen Hurts.

news.head: Dallas Goedert held to one catch before knee injury
news.body: Dallas Goedert caught one of his two targets for four yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Goedert left the game with a knee injury and did not return. Look for the team to update his status heading into a Week 3 matchup against the Bears. The Eagles are all of a sudden very thin at tight end with Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra both on injured reserve already.

news.head: Dallas Goedert (ankle) questionable to return
news.body: Eagles TE Dallas Goedert (ankle) is officially listed as questionable to return Sunday.
news.impact: Goedert appeared to have suffered the injury blocking in the second quarter. Johnny Mundt will see an increase in snaps with Goedert sidelined.

news.head: Dallas Goedert hauls in two touchdowns in Week 1 win over Commanders
news.body: Dallas Goedert hauled in four of his five targets for 77 yards and two touchdowns in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Goedert made the most of his involvement in the Philadelphia passing attack in the season opener, leading the team in receiving yards in the win. The tight end offers fantasy managers a steady TE1 option entering a favorable Week 2 contest against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Denzel Boston snags another touchdown Sunday
news.body: Denzel Boston caught 5-of-7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: Boston connected with Deshaun Watson on a touchdown for the second straight week. He is seemingly emerging as the clear WR1 on the Browns offense. He'll hold some upside WR3 appeal next week for fantasy managers against the Panthers.

news.head: Denzel Boston snags bomb touchdown in loss
news.body: Denzel Boston caught two of four targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.impact: Boston had the Browns' only touchdown, though sadly it was in garbage time. His four targets tied with Jerry Jeudy for second on the team, an encouraging sign for his future usage as he gets further acclimated to the NFL game.

news.head: Denzel Boston to practice with first-team offense
news.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said rookie WR Denzel Boston will move into first-team offense.
news.impact: Boston continues to show out early on in training camp. He is slated to compete for an immediate starting role.

news.head: Denzel Boston selected No. 39 by Cleveland Browns
news.body: The Cleveland Browns have selected WR Denzel Boston with the No. 39 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
news.impact: Boston becomes the second wide receiver taken by the Browns in the first two rounds of the 2026 Draft as they double up after selecting KC Concepcion in the first round Thursday. Boston is a much larger receiver (6-3, 212) out of Washington and led the Huskies in receiving yards last season. He did not run a 40-yard dash at the combine and doesn't display top speed to create separation. But, he does have excellent hands and he was very tough to bring down at the collegiate level. It's a little surprising that the Browns took another receiver with a need for offensive line help. But, Cleveland is looking for playmakers to improve the offense in 2026 and Boston should help with that as part of the receiver rotation.

news.head: Andy Borregales connects on two field goals in Week 2 win
news.body: Patriots K Andy Borregales connected on 2-of-3 field goals and 2-of-2 extra points in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.impact: Borregales connected on field goal attempts from 30 and 45 yards out, while missing from 47-yards out. The second-year kicker should continue to see plenty of field goal opportunities until the passing attack can find consistency.

news.head: Andy Borregales scores four points Wednesday
news.body: Andy Borregales made his lone field-goal attempt and his lone extra-point attempt in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: The young kicker didn't get many opportunities on Wednesday night. He converted both of his attempts, however, leaving him with at least four points on the night. He doesn't project to be a strong option at the position moving forward.

news.head: Andy Borregales misses one kick Sunday
news.body: Andy Borregales went 5-for-5 on his extra-point attempts and went 1-for-2 on his field-goal attempts in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Borregales had an up-and-down game on Sunday. He missed one of his field-goal attempts against the Dolphins, but outside of that he made all of his kicks, including a field goal from 59 yards out. He has proven himself to be reliable overall and should remain their starter in 2026.

news.head: Andy Borregales misses lone field goal attempt
news.body: Andy Borregales went 0-for-1 on field goal attempts and 6-for-6 on extra points in the Patriots 42-10 win over the Jets.
news.impact: Borregales missed a 41-yard attempt late in the third quarter, his first missed field goal since Week 13. The rookie has been fairly consistent this season and will look to build upon a strong rookie campaign in Week 18.

news.head: Kyren Williams finds end zone Monday
news.body: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 85 yards and caught two passes for 12 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Williams had a productive night on Monday. He led the team in rushing and fell just three yards shy of the 100-total yards mark over the course of the game, and he was also able to haul in a touchdown to put the cherry on top. Concerns still exist for his season-long outlook, though, with Blake Corum seeing just one less touch on the night and seemingly only getting better and better.

news.head: Kyren Williams punches in score in loss to Niners
news.body: Kyren Williams ran 11 times for 41 yards and the Rams' only touchdown. He also caught all three of his targets for 24 receiving yards.
news.impact: Williams' day was saved by the touchdown; otherwise it was fairly miserable. Blake Corum showed out in his opportunities, but he was limited to ground work only. Kyren appears to be in a committee now, but he at least has the edge in passing situations, giving him more appeal.

news.head: Kyren Williams sees 15 touches in Week 18 win
news.body: Kyren Williams rushed for 60 yards on 12 carries in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals. He caught 3-of-5 targets for 21 yards.
news.impact: Williams and Blake Corum continued to split time in the backfield to close out the regular season. Both running backs have been effective in that role this season, so the Rams will likely continue that throughout their playoff run.

news.head: Kyren Williams (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Rams RB Kyren Williams (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: Williams was limited in practice this week, but is healthy enough to suit up against the Cardinals. Despite having a playoff spot locked up, the Rams are playing their starters in the final regular season game.

news.head: Breece Hall bottled up in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.body: Breece Hall carried the ball 16 times for 29 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.impact: Hall begins the season as one of the few bright spots in an inconsistent offense, totaling over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains one of the few reliable options for fantasy managers ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

news.head: Breece Hall finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Breece Hall carried the ball 22 times for 102 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 16 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Hall dealt with a groin issue during camp, but he appeared to be at full health in the Week 1 win. The veteran running back handled the majority of the backfield carries, with Braelon Allen mixing in for 10 totes. Hall found the end zone for the first time of the season on a four-yard rush in the third quarter. He will slot in as a solid RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.head: Breece Hall (groin) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Breece Hall (groin) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.
news.impact: Hall is heading into the weekend entirely free of any injury designation ahead of the team's season opener against the Titans on Sunday. He shouldn't have any substantial limitations to his workload in this matchup, and he projects to be a high-quality fantasy asset in this game and beyond if he can stay healthy.

news.head: Breece Hall (groin) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Breece Hall (groin) logged another full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: Hall has been a full participant in two-straight practices to start the week. He told reporters earlier that will be good to go for Week 1, so fantasy managers shouldn't have any real hesitations with starting him ahead of the first game of the season.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson finds the end zone in season debut
news.body: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson tallied 76 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.impact: Henderson missed Week 1 with an ankle injury, but made an immediate impact with a 39-yard touchdown early in the win over Pittsburgh. Rhamondre Stevenson lost a fumble and saw the bulk of the work go to Henderson after the turnover. Fantasy managers should expect both Stevenson and Henderson to have roles against the Jaguars in Week 3.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) officially good to go for Sunday
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is off of the injury report and officially good to go for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.impact: New England's offense is set to get a much-needed boost this week with their young running back off of the injury report and set to make his season debut on Sunday. Henderson projects to be something of a 'boom-or-bust' fantasy option on a week-to-week basis while he continues to split work with Rhamondre Stevenson in the Patriots' backfield.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) ready for season debut
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) has been practicing in full this week and will be ready for Sunday's game.
news.impact: Henderson was unable to go in Week 1, leaving the bulk of the backfield load to veteran Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson is in his second NFL season after totaling over 1,100 yards of offense and 10 touchdowns across 17 regular-season games as a rookie.

news.head: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: Henderson was able to log a second-straight full practice session on Thursday. He seems almost certain to play without any real limitations this week, as he also told reporters that he is ready to go for Sunday's game. His return to the lineup will mean less work for Rhamondre Stenson moving forward, but they could both be worthwhile starters on any given week.

news.head: Cameron Dicker misses kick in loss Sunday
news.body: Cameron Dicker went 2-for-2 on his extra-point attempts but missed his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: The Chargers didn't have much going for them on Sunday, including kicking. Dicker misses his lone field-goal against the Raiders, leaving three more points on the field for Los Angeles. Fantasy managers of the 26-year old should consider moving to a different fantasy option for the time being.

news.head: Cameron Dicker puts just two points on the board in Week 1
news.body: Cameron Dicker did not attempt a field goal and made 2-of-2 PATs in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Widely viewed as one of the best fantasy options among kickers, Dicker was not given much of an opportunity to contribute on Sunday. The Chargers drastically underperformed expectations, totaling only 268 yards of offense and being dominated in time of possession. Dicker will have better games, but this one was a huge disappointment for fantasy managers.

news.head: Cameron Dicker makes lone kick Sunday
news.body: Cameron Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Dicker was only given one opportunity on Sunday, but he was able to make it and finished with three points in the team's loss to the Broncos. That capped off what was another fantastic season for him, finishing as a top-four kicker in most fantasy league formats and distinguishing himself as one of the league's most consistent kickers in real life.

news.head: Cameron Dicker struggles in loss to Houston
news.body: Cameron Dicker connected on one of his two PATs as well as just one of his two FG attempts in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Texans.
news.impact: Dicker's misses were the difference between a Chargers loss and a potential overtime. But it was just not meant to be. He should bounce back next time out with the Chargers, as he's had 10+ kicking points in each of his last three games thanks to the offense that's been rolling.

news.head: Rashee Rice logs 83 yards in win Sunday
news.body: Rashee Rice caught 4-of-6 targets for 83 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Rice was able to bounce back a little bit in Week 2 after a very underwhelming performance to start the season last week. He was able to rack up 83 yards over the course of the night, but he didn't get into the end zone at all, which left him with a mediocre fantasy total. This was a better performance for him, but he was still fourth on the team in terms of targets in this matchup, so fantasy managers should continue to pay attention to his production over the next week or two to see how valuable he will be season-long.

news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) logs full practice Wednesday
news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
news.impact: Rice is still listed on Kansas City's injury report due to a knee injury, but it's nothing more than a minor issue for him at this point and he was able to log a full practice on Wednesday. He should play in Week 2 and will look to bounce back after an underwhelming performance to open the season last week.

news.head: Rashee Rice finds end zone in win Monday
news.body: Rashee Rice caught two passes for 19 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Rice had an underwhelming game on Monday night. He was held to just two catches for 19 yards against the Broncos, but he was able to get into the end zone on one of those receptions, which helped to salvage his fantasy total. QB Patrick Mahomes II didn't look his way very much in this game, but it seems like the team wanted Mahomes to drop back as little as possible given that it was his first game back from a major knee injury. Rice will likely improve going forward, but fantasy managers should keep a close eye on his production over the next few weeks to gauge whether this poor showing was a fluke or a sign of the things to come for the veteran wideout this season.

news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) active for Week 1
news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Rice will suit up after progressing throughout the practice week and not suffering any issues in pregame activities, providing quarterback Patrick Mahomes with all of his pass-catching weapons against the Broncos Monday night.

news.head: Jason Myers hits four PATs in win over Arizona
news.body: Jason Myers hit all four of his PATs and his lone field goal attempt in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.impact: Myers has had seven kicking points in each of his first two games, a solid total. He's going to continue to be productive thanks to the Seahawks offense being as potent as it is.

news.head: Jason Myers scores seven points in win Wednesday
news.body: Jason Myers went 2-for-2 on his field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point attempt in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Myers did his job on Wednesday, knocking in all three of his kicks en route to a win over the Patriots. He will likely be a decent fantasy option at the position over the course of the season, assuming QB Sam Darnold (hip) doesn't miss significant time and leave the offense weaker moving forward.

news.head: Jason Myers has rare off night Saturday
news.body: Jason Myers missed two field goal attempts on Saturday night but the Seahawks still managed a 13-3 win over San Francisco to clinch the top seed in the NFC.
news.impact: Myers had made 18 straight field goal attempts before his miss from 47 yards out early in the second quarter. He also missed on Seattle's last drive of the game when he hit the right upright from 26 yards away. Myers did have makes of 45 yards and 31 yards and also converted his only extra point attempt. Myers finishes with career highs in field goals made (41) and field goal attempts (48) while also converting a perfect 48-of-48 on PATs.

news.head: Jason Myers connects on five kicks Sunday
news.body: Jason Myers connected on both of his field goal attempts and all three extra point attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: Myers remains one of the top kickers in the NFL this season. He is 39-of-44 on field goals this year.

news.head: Courtland Sutton held to 25 yards in Week 2
news.body: Courtland Sutton caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Sutton posted a pedestrian stat line in the Broncos' exciting comeback win. It is becoming a concern after he caught just two passes for 11 yards back in Week 1. The Broncos don't seem to be prioritizing getting him the ball as they have in past years, leaving Sutton as a risky flex option in Week 3 against the Rams.

news.head: Courtland Sutton uninvolved in loss Monday
news.body: Courtland Sutton caught 2-of-5 targets for just 11 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily on Monday night, and Sutton was no exception to that. He caught just two of his five targets over the course of the game and was only able to turn that into a measly 11 yards. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future, even in more favorable matchups.

news.head: Courtland Sutton in full pads at practice Friday
news.body: Courtland Sutton was seen in full pads to begin practice on Friday.
news.impact: It is a positive sign after Sutton missed practice on Tuesday and Wednesday before he was limited in his return on Thursday. It appears he should be able to do more in practice on Friday.

news.head: Courtland Sutton being limited early in training camp
news.body: Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
news.impact: It explains why Sutton was not seen practicing on Tuesday or Wednesday. He returned to practice on Thursday, but he was still held out of team drills. He should continue to be ramped up as we get closer to the season.

news.head: Saquon Barkley held to nine yards while surviving injury scare
news.body: Saquon Barkley carried the ball four times for nine yards while catching one of his two targets for 11 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Barkley missed some time with a shoulder stinger but ultimately was able to return to the game, which explains his quiet afternoon at the office. The veteran running back has now run for 92 scoreless yards on the season as he looks to bounce back ahead of a Week 3 road matchup against the Bears. Assuming his shoulder is okay, Barkley will check in as a low-end RB1 in fantasy for that matchup.

news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) returns to the game
news.body: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (stinger) has returned to the game in the second half against the Titans.
news.impact: Barkley was seen on the sidelines holding his helmet after his first half injury and he did not return prior to halftime. Barkley took a carry in the third quarter and appears poised to return as the primary running back for the remainder of the game.

news.head: Saquon Barkley (stinger) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Tennessee Titans Sunday according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Barkley suffered the injury early in the first quarter for the Eagles, with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley taking over the backfield for head coach Nick Sirianni against the Titans.

news.head: Saquon Barkley heads to locker room Sunday
news.body: Saquon Barkley exited Sunday’s contest for the Philadelphia Eagles against the Tennessee Titans with an apparent arm injury according to Ari Meirov.
news.impact: Barkley carried the ball once for no gain prior to exiting Sunday. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley will take over the backfield touches for head coach Nick Sirianni.

news.head: Jalen Hurts throws two TDs in Week 2
news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 26 of his 37 passes for 264 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions while adding five rushes for 16 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Hurts saved the day for the Eagles, throwing a three-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper with 14 seconds left in regulation. The veteran quarterback also made some mistakes, tossing two interceptions and taking three sacks. Hurts now has five touchdown passes through two games, but he has yet to score any rushing TDs. He will be a high-end QB1 in Week 3 against the Bears on the road.

news.head: Jalen Hurts tosses three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Commanders
news.body: Jalen Hurts completed 14-of-25 pass attempts for 203 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing seven times for 46 yards in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Hurts made the most of an inconsistent season-opening performance behind center, averaging 14.5 yards per completion in the win. The quarterback will look to reward fantasy managers with more explosive dual-threat production in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Jalen Hurts expected to sit out season finale
news.body: The Eagles are expected to rest QB Jalen Hurts in Week 18 against the Commanders
news.impact: Philadelphia is expected to rest most of its starters in the season finale. Third-year QB Tanner McKee will get the start against a struggling Washington defense and could be a serviceable DFS option. Jalen Hurts will turn his focus to the postseason, while also looking ahead to 2026 as a high-end fantasy QB1.

news.head: Jalen Hurts: Eagles starters uncertain for Week 18
news.body: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said “we’re still thinking through” whether the team would play their starters in Week 18.
news.impact: The Eagles still have a chance to move up to the No. 2 seed in the NFC in the playoffs. There should be more clarity by Wednesday or Thursday on who will be starting for the Eagles.

news.head: Mike Evans to manage hip injury this week
news.body: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans' hip injury will have to be managed this week.
news.impact: Evans exited Sunday’s 35-13 victory over the Dolphins in the second half and did not return. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.head: Mike Evans catches three passes in Week 2 win
news.body: Mike Evans came down with all three of his targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: Evans gained half of his yards in Sunday's win on one catch, as he was limited overall in volume of targets due to Brock Purdy efficiently spreading the ball around. At this point in his career, Evans is not the top-tier WR he once was, but he is showing immediate rapport with Purdy. Evans has hauled in 9-of-10 targets for 103 yards and a score through two games.

news.head: Mike Evans snags touchdown in 49ers debut
news.body: Mike Evans caught six of seven targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 27-7 blowout win over the Rams on Thursday.
news.impact: Evans had a nice end zone fade touchdown over a Rams DB who was draped all over him, as well as plenty of third-down usage. He's looking like a potential draft-day steal if his momentum keeps up. This is especially true if De'Zhaun Stribling misses extended time with an ankle injury.

news.head: Mike Evans (adductor) returns to practice
news.body: Mike Evans returned to practice Wednesday.
news.impact: Evans was back on the field after being sidelined for most of training camp. He should be good to go for the season opener next week.

news.head: Quinshon Judkins sees 17 touches Sunday
news.body: Quinshon Judkins ran for 21 yards on 12 carries in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-5 targets for 27 yards receiving.
news.impact: Judkins was shut down on the ground, but somewhat salvaged his day in the passing game for fantasy managers in PPR leagues. His upside remains limited given his situation.

news.head: Quinshon Judkins quiet in blowout loss to Jaguars
news.body: Quinshon Judkins ran 12 times for 33 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also caught both of his targets for 17 yards.
news.impact: Judkins was held back by the Browns inept offensive showing, as everyone except Deshaun Watson and Denzel Boston was held under 10 PPR points, and those two got over that because of a bomb touchdown in garbage time. Judkins is the lead back, but his fantasy value is highly questionable unless something changes.

news.head: Quinshon Judkins returns to team drills
news.body: Quinshon Judkins returned to team drills during practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Judkins missed two practices last week and was limited to individual work on Monday. He was back full-go on Tuesday.

news.head: Quinshon Judkins not seen at practice Thursday
news.body: Browns RB Quinshon Judkins was not seen at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Judkins missed practice on Wednesday due to a "minor issue." He remains day-to-day.

news.head: Luther Burden III sees seven targets in Week 2 loss
news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in three of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.impact: Burden III has provided mixed results to begin the season, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in one of the first two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of an inconsistent Chicago offense early on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.head: Luther Burden III sees six touches in Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in all five of his targets for 63 yards while also rushing once for two yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden III saw steady involvement in the Chicago passing attack, finishing second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout offers head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catcher as part of an explosive Chicago offense ahead of a Week 2 divisional matchup with the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) good to go for Week 1
news.body: Luther Burden III (groin) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Burden was dealing with a groin injury earlier in the offseason, but he is fully healthy now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener. He should play without any restrictions and will be primed for a huge Week 1 if the Bears are without Rome Odunze (calf) for their matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Luther Burden III (groin) practices Tuesday
news.body: Luther Burden III was practicing on Tuesday.
news.impact: Burden had returned to practice last week. He is on track to be good to go for the start of the season next week.

news.head: Josh Jacobs has court appearance date moved up
news.body: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs had his initial court appearance moved up to Sept. 10 from Nov. 17 regarding Jacobs' misdemeanor charges.
news.impact: Jacobs was charged with battery and criminal destruction of property and is scheduled to appear at the Brown County courthouse on Sept. 10, multiple days before Green Bay's season opener against Minnesota. It is unclear how this will affect his return timeline; Jacobs is currently on the commissioner's exempt list, with a potential suspension looming.

news.head: Josh Jacobs expected to play for Packers in 2026 per GM
news.body: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said he expected Josh Jacobs to play for the team in 2026.
news.impact: Gutekunst said he wants to let the process play out when asked if there’s a scenario in which the Packers release Jacobs. He was placed on the Commissioners Exempt List on Sunday. This will remain a situation to monitor.

news.head: Josh Jacobs placed on commissioner of exempt list
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner exempt list by the National Football League according to Tom Pelissero.
news.impact: Jacobs is now ineligible to practice or play for the Packers while the league continues their investigation into alleged improper behavior while being charged with two misdemeanors related to his conduct earlier in the week. If the running back is forced to sit out for any period of the regular season, MarShawn Lloyd will be in line to receive the majority of backfield work while the recently acquired Kaleb Johnson gets up to speed on the offensive playbook with Week 1 approaching.

news.head: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors stemming from May incident
news.body: Josh Jacobs has been charged with two misdemeanors following an incident in May. His initial court date is set for mid-November. The NFL is conducting its own investigation, and a suspension could soon follow.
news.impact: It's important to remember that the NFL has the ability to either suspend Jacobs at the start of the season or wait until the legal process is over. If they wait, then Jacobs will likely not face suspension until next year. If not, we could be looking at a potential 6-8 game absence, though that is more of an educated guess at this point. For anyone taking Jacobs in drafts right now, Marshawn Lloyd is a must-have handcuff and is a great target for Zero-RB builds.

news.head: Brock Purdy turns in tremendous effort against Dolphins
news.body: Brock Purdy connected on 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on three carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: Purdy is off to an outstanding start this season, and he could hardly have been more prolific in Sunday's rout of the Dolphins. The fifth-year QB has completed a ridiculous 80.4% of his passes so far, averaging 246 yards with a 5-1 TD/INT ratio through two games. Purdy has also rushed for 59 yards on eight carries, including a two-yard scoring scramble on Sunday. He'll be a QB to start against the Cardinals in Week 3.

news.head: Brock Purdy dismantles Rams defense in statement win
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and a pick in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also ran five times for 29 yards.
news.impact: Purdy was great in this game aside from a couple of hiccups, namely the interception. However, he did what he needed to and got the Niners into scoring position and helped them take advantage of the several short fields they inherited. Purdy should be a solid asset moving forward for fantasy.

news.head: Brock Purdy shut down by Seattle defense Saturday
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-27 passes for just 127 yards and one interception in the 49ers 13-3 loss to the Seahawks.
news.impact: Purdy was held to a season-low 127 yards and failed to reach 200 yards through the air in a game for just the third time in his nine starts. It was also his only start of the year without throwing a touchdown pass. He carried the ball twice for 21 yards and had San Francisco's longest run of the night (11 yards).

news.head: Brock Purdy accounts for five touchdowns in Week 17 win over Bears
news.body: Brock Purdy completed 24-of-33 pass attempts for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception while also rushing six times for 28 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 42-38 Week 17 win over the Bears.
news.impact: Purdy continues an impactful stretch behind center, recording two or more touchdowns in each of his last four games (12 passing, three rushing) for the 49ers. The signal-caller remains a dynamic QB1 option despite a difficult Week 18 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: Sam LaPorta hauls in touchdown Thursday
news.body: Sam LaPorta hauled in 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.impact: LaPorta had a good showing on Thursday night. He caught all but one of his targets and turned that into 52 yards and a touchdown in a shootout loss against the Buffalo Bills. He might struggle with consistency moving forward but will continue to have as high of a TD upside as anyone for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Sam LaPorta catches five passes in Week 1 win
news.body: Sam LaPorta caught five of his eight targets for 48 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: LaPorta saw sizeable volume in his return to the lineup for head coach Dan Campbell, joining explosive wideouts Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown in finishing with eight or more targets in the win. The tight end remains a stable option in all formats as a primary pass-catching option in the Detroit offense ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Sam LaPorta (hip) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Sam LaPorta (hip) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: LaPorta is now off of the injury report after dealing with a hip injury for the latter part of the preseason. He should be a full go for Week 1 and will remain a startable fantasy option in this matchup and beyond.

news.head: Sam LaPorta (hip) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Sam Laporta returned to practice on Tuesday after suffering a hip injury last week.
news.impact: Laporta's hip injury has made his status for Week 1 murky, but his returning to practice this early is a good sign. The tight end will likely be limited as he builds back up, but he could be in line to start the season barring any setbacks.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid electric in win Thursday
news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 passing attempts for 95 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Kincaid's great start to the season continued on Thursday night. He was Buffalo's leading receiver against the Lions and was able to get into the end zone on one of his seven catches, which left him with a great fantasy total. It looks like he may be in the midst of a big breakout season right now, so long as he and QB Josh Allen stay healthy for the majority of the season.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid has breakout game against Texans
news.body: Dalton Kincaid caught five of six targets for 130 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Kincaid had arguably his best game as a pro, acheiving a career-high 130 receiving yards in what should have been tough sledding against Houston. He tied with Khalil Shakir for second in targets on the Bills, but vastly outproduced Shakir in yards. His downfield usage was encouraging, and it’s a promising start to his fourth season. Now to see if it keeps up.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid gets fifth-year option picked up
news.body: The Buffalo Bills have exercised the fifth-year option on TE Dalton Kincaid.
news.impact: Kincaid, a former first-round pick, is coming off his most efficient NFL season. The 26-year-old tight end hauled in 39 receptions for 571 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns. His contract is now guaranteed through 2027 as he continues to operate as one of Josh Allen’s top pass-catching options.

news.head: Dalton Kincaid (knee) not expected to require offseason surgery
news.body: Dalton Kincaid said “does not anticipate” undergoing surgery this offseason.
news.impact: It came out after the season that Kincaid played the 2025 season with a torn PCL. As of now, he should be healthy heading into the Bills offseason program.

news.head: Tucker Kraft quiet in Week 2 win
news.body: Tucker Kraft caught two of his three targets for 15 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.impact: Kraft was unable to make a significant impact as part of an underwhelming Green Bay passing attack, finishing with less than four receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end will look to get back on track for fantasy managers against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3.

news.head: Tucker Kraft totals 65 yards Sunday
news.body: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: Kraft was playing in his first game back from his torn ACL. He was on a snap count in his first game back. He remains a TE1 heading into next week against the Jets.

news.head: Tucker Kraft signs four year, $75 million deal with Packers
news.body: Tucker Kraft has agreed to a four-year, $75 million deal with the Green Bay Packers. The deal is worth up to $92 million.
news.impact: Kraft was on his way to a massive season in 2025 before going down with a torn ACL. He gets his payday as the Packers lock in their emergeing star for the long haul.

news.head: Tucker Kraft (knee) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Tucker Kraft (knee) is off of the injury report for Week 1's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Kraft has been rehabbing from a major knee injury all offseason, but it appears that he is finally close to full health again, as he carries no injury designation prior to the team's season opener on Sunday. He could be limited for his first few weeks back, but the team hasn't indicated that, meaning that he could be seeing a full workload in the very near future.

news.head: Eddy Pineiro makes five PATs in Sunday's win
news.body: Eddy Pineiro did not attempt a field goal but made all five of his PATs in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: The 49ers found the end zone with each of their first five drives Sunday afternoon, and did not give Pineiro any field-goal chances. That's obviously not going to be the case each week. The veteran should be a solid fantasy option for a squad that looks really strong so far.

news.head: Eddy Pineiro (illness) ready to go for Sunday's game
news.body: Eddy Pineiro (illness) will kick for the 49ers in Week 2's matchup with the Dolphins.
news.impact: Pineiro has missed practice all week due to being under the weather, but the veteran kicker will be ready to go Sunday. Pineiro hit 2-of-3 field goals and all three of his PATs in Week 1.

news.head: Eddy Pineiro (illness) uncertain to play Sunday
news.body: Eddy Pineiro (illness) is uncertain to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: The veteran kicker is officially considered questionable to play heading into the weekend. He is dealing with a mildly serious illness right now that has left him sidelined from practice all week, and it's unclear whether or not he will be ready to go in time for the team's matchup against the Dolphins, which would make them need to determine who will take his place prior to kickoff.

news.head: Eddy Pineiro (illness) absent from another practice Thursday
news.body: Eddy Pineiro (illness) was absent from another practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Pineiro is still recovering from an illness and was not at San Francisco's practice on Thursday as a result. He should be good to go for Sunday's game against Miami, however, as this illness is likely nothing more than a day-to-day issue.

news.head: Emeka Egbuka has touchdown salvage performance Sunday
news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 16 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns.
news.impact: It would have been a disastrous afternoon for Egbuka if it weren't for a touchdown he hauled in. He'll remain a WR2 play next week against the Vikings.

news.head: Emeka Egbuka totals 63 yards Sunday
news.body: Emeka Egbuka caught 5-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Egbuka entered Sunday fully healthy after coming off a toe injury. He got off to a strong start in the first half, but he was not targeted in the second half despite the Bucs trailing. He remains a WR2 heading into Week 2.

news.head: Emeka Egbuka (toe) cleared for Week 1
news.body: Emeka Egbuka (toe) is cleared to play in Week 1 for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cincinnati Bengals according to Greg Auman.

news.head: Emeka Egbuka (toe) practicing again Friday
news.body: Emeka Egbuka (toe) participates fully in Friday's practice session.
news.impact: It certainly seems that Egbuka will have no limitations for Sunday's season opener against the Bengals. The second-year wideout will lead the Buccaneers' receiving corps for quarterback Baker Mayfield.

news.head: Seattle Seahawks D/ST shuts down Cardinals defense on Sunday
news.body: The Seattle Seahawks D/ST shut down the Arizona Cardinals offense on Sunday 31-7, racking up an interception and two sacks in the big win.
news.impact: Seattle's defense has allowed a grand total of 17 points over two weeks. They're shaping up to be a formidable unit so far, and are a top defense to roster for fantasy moving forward.

news.head: Seahawks D/ST stellar in win Wednesday
news.body: The Seahawks' D/ST logged three sacks and three interceptions while allowing just ten points in Wednesday night's win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Seattle's defense put up a fantastic showing on Wednesday night. They not only held New England's strong offense to just ten points on the night, but they also recorded three interceptions, including one on the final drive of the game to seal the win. This unit is expected to be elite over the course of the season, assuming all of their key players remain healthy and on the field.

news.head: Seattle Seahawks D/ST shuts down 49ers offense Saturday
news.body: The Seattle Seahawks D/ST held the high-powered 49ers offense to just 173 total yards on Saturday night as Seattle clinched the NFC West and the top seed in the NFC with a 13-3 victory.
news.impact: The Seahawks' defense was swarming all night, limiting the 49ers to just nine first downs and 173 total yards for the game. Seattle sacked Brock Purdy three times and also got a huge interception from Drake Thomas at the Seahawks' three-yard line early in the fourth quarter. San Francisco was 2-of-9 on third downs and averaged only 4.1 yards per play on the night.

news.head: Seahawks D/ST dominates Panthers passing attack Sunday
news.body: The Seahawks D/ST allowed 10 points on 139 total yards with two sacks, one interception and one fumble recovery on Sunday.
news.impact: The Seahawks held Tetairoa McMillan to just one catch all game. They allowed one touchdown with the field goal coming on short yardage following a Sam Darnold fumble. They draw a 49ers offense on fire in Week 18 with the division and No. 1 seed on the line.

news.head: DeVonta Smith explodes for 117 yards, TD in Week 2
news.body: DeVonta Smith caught 10 of his 13 targets for 117 yards and a touchdown in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Smith bounced back in a big way after posting a pedestrian three catches for 53 yards in Week 1. He found the end zone on a 22-yard pass from Jalen Hurts in the second quarter to give the Eagles a 14-7 lead. Smith will be a rock-solid WR1 heading into a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Bears.

news.head: DeVonta Smith catches three passes in Week 1 win
news.body: DeVonta Smith caught three of his six targets for 53 yards in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: The wideout was mostly held in check despite leading the team in targets, finishing behind tight end Dallas Goedert and No. 2 wideout Dontayvion Wicks in receiving yards on the win. The wideout remains one of the more explosive options in the Philadelphia passing attack, with an opportunity to get back on track against the Tennessee Titans in Week 2 up next.

news.head: DeVonta Smith practicing fully on Monday
news.body: Devonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing fully on Monday for the first time in three weeks. He returned in a limited fashion recently, but he is back to fully participating.
news.impact: It’s great news for Smith as he works his way back from a hamstring injury. This should be the all the confidence boost fantasy managers needed to continue targeting him highly in drafts.

news.head: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) officially limited Thursday
news.body: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Smith is still in the process of recovering from a hamstring injury, but he was able to take part in Thursday's joint practice with New England in a limited capacity. It seems like his recover is going well, and unless there's a setback of some kind, it looks like he will be fully healthy in time for the season opener.

news.head: Javonte Williams sees 15 touches in Week 2
news.body: Javonte Williams rushed for 30 yards on 12 carries in the Cowboys 37-20 win over the Commanders. He caught 3-of-4 targets for 20 yards.
news.impact: Williams struggled to get anything consistent going against the Commanders' rush defense. Williams has logged 12 carries in both games this season, but has failed to get anything consistent going yardage wise. Williams and the Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.head: Javonte Williams scores twice in loss Sunday
news.body: Javonte Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught five passes for 31 yards and another touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Williams was arguably Dallas' most impactful offensive player on Sunday night. He scored two touchdowns and totaled 72 yards on a night where the entire offense struggled, leaving him with a surprisingly good fantasy total on the week. He is clearly the team's bellcow running back at this point and should be viewed as a high quality fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Javonte Williams remains Cowboys lead back in 2026
news.body: Javonte Williams remains as Dallas’ lead back by a comfortable margin headed into 2026 following a breakout campaign that ended with him signing a three year extension with the team.
news.impact: Williams has the bell-cow, or at least the lead role, on lockdown. However, what’s primarily in question is who will be backing him up, as Jaydon Blue, Malik Davis, and Phil Mafah are all vying for the role. It appears Dallas, while comfortable with Williams, doesn’t want to put the same sort of workload on him again this season as he had in 2025. That could hurt his upside unless he becomes more proficient in the passing game, but on volume alone he should maintain RB2 status.

news.head: Javonte Williams lands three year deal with Dallas
news.body: Javonte Williams has landed a three year deal with the Dallas Cowboys, with $16 million guaranteed.
news.impact: The former Bronco cashes in after a big season in Dallas. Expectations were fairly low for the veteran back, who was coming off of multiple injuries and disappointing seasons, but he crushed expectations to the tune of 1,200 rushing yards and 11 rushing touchdowns. He is a strong RB2 heading into 2026 with RB1 upside.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb finds the end zone twice in Week 2 win
news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Lamb turned in an excellent performance, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards. Lamb already has three touchdowns in the first two games and will look to continue his strong start to the season against the Ravens in Week 3.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb hauls in touchdown in loss Sunday
news.body: CeeDee Lamb hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Lamb was technically Dallas' leading receiver on Sunday night, but he did that with just 44 yards over the course of the game. He was able to haul in a touchdown at one point, however, which helped to salvage his fantasy total on the day. He will likely revert to being an elite producer at the position when Dallas' offense as a whole bounces back sometime within the next few weeks.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb has contract restructured by Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured the contract of WR CeeDee Lamb.
news.impact: Lamb was one of three players who had their contracts restructured to help create a significant amount of capital space for the Cowboys. They are now under the cap heading into free agency. Lamb and George Pickens are expected to run it back with Dak Prescott in the passing game for Dallas.

news.head: CeeDee Lamb catches just one pass in Week 18
news.body: CeeDee Lamb caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
news.impact: The Cowboys limited most of their starters' snaps in Week 18, and Lamb was no exception. The four-time Pro-Bowler made his 75th catch of the season Sunday, as he finished the campaign with 1,077 yards and three touchdowns over 14 games.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle bounces back in Week 2
news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught eight of his 10 targets for 138 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Waddle led the Broncos in all receiving categories in the close win. More importantly, he bounced back after catching just one pass for two yards in Week 1. Waddle will be a solid WR2 heading into Week 3 against the Rams.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle disappoints in Broncos debut Monday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle caught 1-of-3 targets for just two yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: There has been a lot of hype for the veteran wideout after the Broncos traded for him this offseason, but he got off to a poor start with his new team on Monday night. He caught one pass for just two yards over the course of the game, which burned any fantasy manager who risked starting him in this matchup. Denver's offense as a whole struggled heavily against Kansas City's defense, however, so there's a good chance that he and the rest of the offense bounce back and return to solid fantasy production in easier matchups moving forward.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) in full pads at practice Tuesday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle is in full pads at practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: It is another positive sign for Waddle following his return to practice on Monday. He remains on track to be good to go for the start of the regular season.

news.head: Jaylen Waddle (leg) returns to practice Monday
news.body: Jaylen Waddle returned to practice on Monday after dealing with a leg muscle strain.
news.impact: Waddle missed practice all of last week, but has now returned to action at the start of this week. The wideout should still be monitored throughout the week to see if an injury pops back up.

news.head: Bhayshul Tuten finds the end zone in Week 2
news.body: Bhayshul Tuten carried the ball 13 times for 65 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for minus-three yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Tuten punched in a one-yard touchdown in the second quarter to give the Jaguars an early 7-0 lead. The second-year back also vastly outproduced Chris Rodriguez Jr., who had just 13 yards on six carries. Tuten has now racked up 131 rushing yards through two games. He will be a solid RB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.head: Bhayshul Tuten racks up 66 yards on the ground in win
news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also caught his only target for 22 yards.
news.impact: Tuten led the Jags in rushing attempts in the win, but didn't have much to show in terms of fantasy scoring in half- or full-PPR formats. But to be fair, he was efficient in his touches, and it's likely that better days are ahead for the apparent Jags RB1.

news.head: Bhayshul Tuten expected to ‘have a big year’ per HC Coen
news.body: Bhayshul Tuten is expected to “have a big year” according to HC Liam Coen. Coen praised the second year back in an interview, noting his explosive ability and the growth in his game.
news.impact: Tuten is the favorite for RB1 duties in Jacksonville with his do-it-all skillset, while Chris Rodriguez dealing with an injury this offseason and LeQuint Allen is primarily a pass blocking and catching specialist. He’s still a bit of an unknown since Travis Etienne handled the majority of backfield work in 2025, but his upside should things work out is tantalizing.

news.head: Bhayshul Tuten gets five touches in return
news.body: Bhayshul Tuten ran five times for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans on Sunday.
news.impact: Tuten didn't touch the ball much in his return to play, but it's important to note that he was the RB2 of the offense, putting LeQuint Allen back in his special teams role.

news.head: Lamar Jackson held in check in Week 2 loss
news.body: Lamar Jackson completed 21-of-31 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He added 34 rushing yards on four carries.
news.impact: Jackson and the Ravens' offense appeared to feel the loss of Zay Flowers (hamstring) who was unavailable for this game. Jackson was intercepted on the final play of the game as the Ravens attempted a late comeback. The Ravens will take on the Cowboys in Week 3.

news.head: Lamar Jackson surpasses 300 passing yards in Week 1 win over Colts
news.body: Lamar Jackson completed 17-of-25 pass attempts for 324 yards and one touchdown while also rushing seven times for 40 yards, one touchdown, and one lost fumble in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Jackson took advantage of a more explosive offensive playbook from first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, accounting for touchdowns on the ground and through the air in the win. The superstar quarterback remains an elite QB1 option entering a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Lamar Jackson to play without contract extension to begin season
news.body: Lamar Jackson will play without a contract extension to begin the season for the Baltimore Ravens according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Jackson is focused on football entering the 2026-27 season under a new Baltimore Ravens coaching staff, as the superstar quarterback is poised for another elite season behind center barring injury while also offering fantasy managers explosive production as a high-level QB1 in all formats with an intriguing Week 1 contest against the Indianapolis Colts ahead.

news.head: Lamar Jackson will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson will not play in the preseason opener on Saturday against the Eagles.
news.impact: Minter said there will be some “established players” not playing Saturday. Jackson should see some reps in the second or third preseason game.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase hauls in two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 7-of-9 targets for 75 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Chase recorded both of the touchdowns scored by Cincinnati on Sunday, including an incredible catch where he just barely got both feet in. He remains a locked and loaded WR1 heading into next week against the Steelers.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase very quiet to open season
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: It was a Week 1 to forget for Chase fantasy managers to say the least. There shouldn't be too much of concern after one week, though he draws an even tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) cleared for Week 1
news.body: Ja’Marr Chase (knee) has been cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.

news.head: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) logged another full practice session on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, Chase was able to log yet another full practice session on Thursday. He is trending towards being a full go for the season opener on Sunday, assuming there are no unforeseen setbacks between now and then. He will be a top-tier fantasy option if active in Week 1 and beyond.

news.head: Davante Adams dominant in win Monday
news.body: Davante Adams hauled in 8-of-10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Adams had one of his best games as a Ram on Monday night. He put up nearly 200 receiving yards in this blowout win over the Giants, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He really stepped up in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip), so if he misses more time, fantasy managers should continue to view Adams as a can't-miss option any given week that he's the team's undisputed WR1.

news.head: Davante Adams quiet in loss to 49ers
news.body: Davante Adams caught just three of six targets for 26 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
