news.impact: Adams could just not get much going against the Niners. On the bright side, his six targets were second on the team, so he's still earning opportunities. It just wasn't his day, as was the story for most of the team. He will try to improve next time out.

news.head: Davante Adams expected to be back with Rams next season
news.body: Rams coach Sean McVay said he “absolutely” expects to have Davante Adams back next season.
news.impact: Adams has one more year left on his contract as he comes off a year where he led the league in receiving touchdowns. The Rams are expected to run it back with Adams, Puka Nacua and Matthew Stafford after falling just short of the Super Bowl this year.

news.head: Davante Adams (hamstring) off injury report
news.body: Davante Adams (hamstring) has been removed from the Rams' injury report.
news.impact: Adams has been fully active at Rams' practice this week and will be ready to go for Saturday's playoff matchup with the Panthers. Adams missed the final three weeks of the regular season after hauling in 60 passes, including a league-leading 14 touchdown grabs, over 14 games.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty inefficient in win Sunday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty rushed the ball 21 times for 48 yards and caught 4-of-7 targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Jeanty didn't look great on Sunday. He totaled just 63 on his 28 opportunities against the Chargers, and he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, which left him with an underwhelming fantasy total. The Raiders have a tough schedule coming up, so the young running back will need to step up his game if he wants to deliver for fantasy managers.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logs full practice Wednesday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
news.impact: Jeanty seems to be entirely over his ankle injury at this point, as he played through it in Week 1 and now logs a full practice session to start the week on Wednesday. He should be a full go and high-quality fantasy option moving forward, assuming he suffers no setbacks with his recovery.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty leads offense in Week 1 win over Dolphins
news.body: Ashton Jeanty carried the ball 23 times for 102 yards while also hauling in all six of his targets for a team-leading 45 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders' 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty was dynamic out of the backfield in the season opener, leading the team in rushing and receiving yards in the win. the running back remains an elite RB1 option with PPR upside for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers ahead.

news.head: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Ashton Jeanty is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
news.impact: Jeanty practiced in full all week. He should be good to go in his lead role to open the season.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. snags one pass in win
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. caught one of three targets for 15 yards in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.impact: With the Falcons' QB play being so abysmal, it's hard to take anything away from the last two weeks. Hopefully we will see Michael Penix on Thursday to help bring some clarity and stability to the passing game.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. held without a catch in Week 1
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. failed to catch his lone target in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: It was a rough day for the Atlanta passing attack as third-string QB Cooper Rush only passed for 143 yards. Pitts will hope to bounce back in Week 2 against the Panthers, although he will be tough to trust in fantasy as long as Rush is under center.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. agrees to 3-year, $54 million extension with Falcons
news.body: Kyle Pitts Sr. has agreed to a 3-year, $54 million extension with the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: After coming off arguably his best season as a pro, Pitts gets the bag. He will operate as the teams second target behind Drake London and TE1 in a tight end friendly Stefanski system. It’s wheels up for the still young Pitts.

news.head: Kyle Pitts Sr. could be moved if Falcons find trade partner
news.body: Adam Schefter said “he would watch to see if [the Falcons] could find a trade partner for Kyle Pitts, who they’re open to dealing.”
news.impact: Pitts had found himself in the midst of trade rumors earlier in the offseason, but they have quieted down since. He signed his franchise tender earlier in April. It still seems like Pitts will likely remain in Atlanta, but it is at least worth monitoring.

news.head: Travis Kelce dominant in overtime win Sunday
news.body: Travis Kelce hauled in 9-of-11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Kelce looked great on Sunday night. He led the team in receptions and racked up 101 receiving yards on the night, a number which he failed to hit at all last season. His touchdown was the cherry on top for fantasy managers, and he will likely continue to have good week-to-week value if Patrick Mahomes and KC's offense continues to look this good moving forward.

news.head: Travis Kelce solid in win Monday
news.body: Travis Kelce caught 3-of-5 targets for 71 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Kelce wasn't very involved for much of Monday night's game, but he was able to haul in a big catch at one point that helped to leave him with a solid 71 yards on the night. Fantasy managers should be pleased with his performance in this matchup but should not expect him to be a TE1 on a week-to-week basis for the foreseeable future, especially with Kansas City seemingly wanting to operate as a run-heavy team this season.

news.head: Travis Kelce officially re-signs with Chiefs on three-year deal
news.body: The Chiefs re-signed TE Travis Kelce to a three-year, $54.735 million contract.
news.impact: Kelce was reported to have signed a one-year contract, but it is now a three-year deal. He caught 76 passes for 851 yards and five touchdowns last season, and will remain in Kansas City for three more seasons.

news.head: Travis Kelce officially agrees to deal with Chiefs
news.body: Travis Kelce and the Chiefs have now officially agreed to terms on a new deal.
news.impact: It was reported Monday morning and it is now official. Kelce will be returning for a 14th season with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs.

news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) uncertain for Week 3
news.body: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua will play in Week 3.
news.impact: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua will be able to suit up against Denver next week. If he remains sidelined, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson would remain in bigger roles.

news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) inactive for Week 2
news.body: Puka Nacua (hip) is officially inactive for Week 2 for the Los Angeles Rams against the New York Giants according to Adam Schefter.

news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) questionable for Monday night
news.body: Puka Nacua (hip) did not practice on Saturday and is now labeled questionable for Monday night against the Giants.
news.impact: Nacua has now missed two practices in a row with a hip issue, and that does not bode well for his status on game day. Fantasy managers will need to have contingency plans ready in case he sits. Davante Adams is next up for targets, but Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson could see more looks. Konata Mumpfield is likely next up behind Puka with Jordan Whittington also questionable.

news.head: Puka Nacua (hip) doesn't practice Friday
news.body: Puka Nacua (hip) was added to the injury report as a non-participant at practice on Friday.
news.impact: Nacua is a new addition to the injury report, being listed with a hip injury of some kind that left him sidelined from practice on Friday. This is a situation that fantasy managers should be closely monitoring heading into the weekend because it could lead to him being limited or sidelined against the Giants on Monday night, which would be devastating for many managers relying on him for a big game at the end of the week.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs plays well in loss Thursday
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed the ball 16 times for 52 yards and caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.impact: Thursday's game wasn't great for Gibbs in terms of efficiency, but he was still able to accumulate over 100 yards and a touchdown on Thursday night, which left him with a great fantasy total in this shootout matchup against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option at the RB position for the remainder of the season, provided he remains healthy for most of it.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs leads backfield attack in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns while also hauling in all five of his targets for 30 yards in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: Gibbs was dynamic out of the backfield for head coach Dan Campbell, averaging 5.4 yards per carry in the win. The running back remains an explosive RB1 option in all formats, with a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills up next.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs agrees to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs has agreed to 3-year, $67.5 million deal with Lions that could be worth up to $75.75 million. Gibbs is now the NFL’s highest paid running back.
news.impact: Gibbs has done everything he needs to to earn this money. He’s a premier running back in the NFL, in the argument for the best. Now with David Montgomery gone, we will see how well he can shoulder a workhorse role, and fantasy managers are rightly expecting big things.

news.head: Jahmyr Gibbs does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Lions
news.body: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Lions.
news.impact: Gibbs has two years left on his rookie deal but is currently eligible for an extension. Gibbs could earn more than $20 million per year based on previous reports. This will remain a situation to monitor as Gibbs holds in to begin training camp.

news.head: Parker Washington goes for 98 yards in Week 2
news.body: Parker Washington caught seven of his 12 targets for 98 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Washington led the Jacksonville receivers in all receiving categories while nearly reaching 100 yards in a tough matchup against Denver. The veteran has been excellent through the first two games of the season, posting 12 catches for 181 yards and a touchdown. Clearly the alpha in the Jacksonville receiving room, Washington will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.head: Parker Washington snags touchdown in win
news.body: Parker Washington caught five of six targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns.
news.impact: Washington answered the call of all the offseason hype with flying colors. He scored on a 30-yard bomb from Trevor Lawrence early on in the game and kept showing up to make plays afterwards. Expect Washington to continue to be a focal point in the offense, especially if Brian Thomas Jr. were to miss any time.

news.head: Parker Washington, Jaguars remain in contract talks
news.body: The Jacksonville Jaguars are "not going to stop talking" to wide receiver Parker Washington as both sides iron out a potential contract extension, says general manager James Gladstone.
news.impact: Gladstone said the team would not hesitate to carry contract discussions into the regular season as they aim to finalize a deal with their breakout wideout. Washington had 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns last season and carries an expert consensus ranking of WR29, according to FantasPros, into his fourth NFL season.

news.head: Parker Washington (undisclosed) participating in practice Tuesday
news.body: Parker Washington (undisclosed) is participating in Jacksonville's practice on Tuesday.
news.impact: Washington has been battling an undisclosed injury of some kind for a little while now, but he was back and participating at practice on Tuesday. That's a good sign that he is close to full health, especially considering that it was a joint practice with the Buccaneers. He seems to be fully on track to play in Week 1 and remains an intriguing late-round dart throw if healthy.

news.head: Kenny Gainwell remains in limited role Sunday
news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 10 yards on two carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 3-of-4 targets for five yards receiving.
news.impact: Bucky Irving was the clear lead back for the second straight week. Gainwell remains a pure stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.head: Kenny Gainwell uninvolved Sunday
news.body: Kenny Gainwell ran for 15 yards on five carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught his line target for three yards receiving.
news.impact: This felt like the perfect time for Gainwell to make an impact with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early, but it was Bucky Irving in the passing game out of the backfield who caught seven passes. Gainwell is a risky flex play for now in PPR leagues until we see him more involved.

news.head: Kenny Gainwell (personal) not practicing Friday, expected back Sunday
news.body: Kenny Gainwell is not practicing on Friday due to personal reasons.
news.impact: It is an excused absence for Gainwell, who is expected to be back on Sunday. He is competing for a complimentary role alongside Bucky Irving.

news.head: Kenneth Gainwell referred to as '1B running back' by HC Todd Bowles
news.body: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles referred to Kenneth Gainwell as the team’s 1B running back.
news.impact: The hype on Gainwell has continued since early in the Bucs offseason program. He was also only more noticeable early on with Bucky Irving recovering from an offseason procedure. This will remain a situation to monitor heading into training camp.

news.head: Ravens D/ST struggles in Week 2 loss
news.body: The Ravens D/ST allowed 24 pints, 252 yards passing, and 65 rushing yards in the loss to the Saints.
news.impact: The Ravens' defense tallied three sacks but failed to force a turnover in the loss. The Ravens will need to get some of the issues with the pass defense together before taking on Dak Prescott and the Cowboys in Week 3.

news.head: Ravens D/ST stifles Colts in Week 1 win
news.body: The Ravens D/ST recorded two sacks, one fumble recovery, and one interception in a Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: The defense stood tall in the season opener for first-year head coach Jesse Minter, allowing less than 275 offensive yards in the win. The unit will look to take advantage of a favorable Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Baltimore Ravens hire Jesse Minter as Head Coach
news.body: The Baltimore Ravens are hiring former Los Angeles Chargers DC Jesse Minter as their new head coach.
news.impact: It was reported Minter turned down the Browns second interview as he saw better opportunity elsewhere, and this certainly fits the bill. He’ll look to take over the mantle of John Harbaugh and get the Ravens back into the playoff race in 2026 with Lamar Jackson at the helm of the offense and a talented defense to boot.

news.head: Baltimore Ravens parting ways with John Harbaugh
news.body: The Baltimore Ravens are reportedly parting ways with head coach John Harbaugh after 18 seasons. He was the second-longest-tenured head coach in the NFL.
news.impact: Harbaugh and the Ravens missed the playoffs this year, and there seemed to be some tension that was not present in recent seasons. Now, the Ravens are resetting with the coach in charge, a massive change for an organization that was 180-113 with Harbaugh at the helm. Harbaugh is a Super Bowl champion and should immediately be one of the top candidates for current vacancies.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) not practicing Wednesday
news.body: Ravens WR Zay Flowers is not practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Flowers continues to work his way back from a hamstring injury. His status remains uncertain for Week 3.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) out against Saints
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) has been downgraded to out against the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: With Flowers out, Mark Andrews will become the primary target for Lamar Jackson. Rashod Bateman will be the Ravens top receiver on the depth chart, but it would be extremely hard to start him, given the amount of routes he run for just one target last week. Rookie Elijah Sarratt could be an interesting watch if called up, but it’s best to start Andrews and move on.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) doubtful to play Sunday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: Flowers is officially going into the weekend with a doubtful tag, meaning that he is almost certainly going to be sidelined against the Saints thanks to the hamstring injury that he suffered in Week 1. It remains to be seen if he will have to miss more time beyond this game, and fantasy managers should look for Rashod Bateman and Devontez Walker to benefit from his absence and see more work on Sunday.

news.head: Zay Flowers (hamstring) returns to practice Friday
news.body: Zay Flowers (hamstring) returned to practice Friday for the Baltimore Ravens according to Jamison Hensley.
news.impact: Flowers was able to log his first practice session of the week for head coach Jesse Minter, taking a step in the right direction in hopes of suiting up for Week 2. If the wideout is unable to receive final clearance, Rashod Bateman would slide into a No. 1 wideout role against the New Orleans Saints Sunday.

news.head: Matthew Golden leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Jets
news.body: Matthew Golden hauled in four of his six targets for a team-high 58 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.impact: Golden has been one of the few bright spots in an underperforming Packers offense to begin the season, recording four or more receptions for over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two contests. The wideout will look for another impactful performance in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.head: Matthew Golden totals 95 yards Sunday
news.body: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 95 yards in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings.
news.impact: After a lost rookie season, Golden opened this year leading Green Bay receivers in targets on Sunday. He is in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 for fantasy managers.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: Matthew Golden was back at practice at Packers training camp on Tuesday.
news.impact: Golden makes his way back after missing a few days of practice. He was spotted running with the Green Bay first team offense on Tuesday.

news.head: Matthew Golden (toe) not expected to practice Monday
news.body: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said he does not expect WR Matthew Golden to practice on Monday.
news.impact: Golden also missed practice on Sunday. He remains day-to-day. It is unknown how serious his injury is.

news.head: Michael Wilson sees seven targets in loss
news.body: Michael Wilson caught two of seven targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.impact: Wilson failed to connect with QB Jacoby Brissett in this game, and fantasy managers will be wishing for more after such a bad showing. He wil look to bounce back against the Niners next Sunday.

news.head: Michael Wilson comes up with five catches in Week 1
news.body: Michael Wilson secured 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: With his next lucrative contract extension in hand, Wilson turned in a decent performance during Sunday's win. The fourth-year receiver finished third on the team in receptions, targets, and receiving yards, maintaining a solid rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett.

news.head: Michael Wilson agrees to three year, $75 million deal with Cardinals
news.body: Michael Wilson has agreed to a three year, $75 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals.
news.impact: Wilson was about to be playing on the final year of his rookie contract, but will now see himself attached to the team for the long haul. It will be interesting to see how his role changes, if at all, under a new coaching stafff and with Marvin Harrison Jr. back in the fold.

news.head: Michael Wilson expected to play role as Z-receiver
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson will play the Puka Nacua role, “closer to the core,” as the Z-receiver.
news.impact: LaFleur has spent the past three years as the Rams offensive coordinator and figures to bring a lot of what he learned under Sean McVay to the Cardinals offense. Wilson is expected to line up off the line of scrimmage which will allow him to move more freely. Wilson exploded last season when Marvin Harrison Jr. missed time. The question remains what his production will be heading into a full season with Harrison healthy, but he should be put in a more favorable situation.

news.head: 49ers D/ST records four sacks, stifles Dolphins offense
news.body: The 49ers' defense allowed just 13 points on 284 yards of offense while recording four sacks in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: For the second straight week, the 49ers' defense dominated. The unit has surrendered just 20 points in two games, holding both the Rams and Dolphins under 300 yards of total offense. The 49ers will remain a popular play in Week 3 against the Cardinals.

news.head: San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shuts down Rams in win
news.body: The San Fransisco 49ers D/ST shut down the Rams offense on Thursday, allowing just seven points in their 27-7 rout of the Super Bowl favorites.
news.impact: The Niners defensive totals were modest, with one interception and a fumble recovery, but were held without a sack. They just kept the Rams from moving the ball while not racking up much in the “counting stats” category. It’s a good showing for the team, and a date with the Dolphins is on tap. They are a great DST option this week if available.

news.head: San Francisco 49ers D/ST does nothing of note Saturday
news.body: The San Francisco 49ers D/ST could muster only two sacks and did not force a turnover during their 13-3 loss to Seattle on Saturday night.
news.impact: Yes, the 49ers only gave up 13 points. But, it could have been much worse as Jason Myers missed two field goals and the Seahawks failed to convert on fourth-and-goal on the game's first drive. Seattle had 361 net yards, including 180 on the ground, and did not turn the ball over against the 49ers defense. That's two straight weeks - and three of the last four - that San Francisco has not forced a turnover.

news.head: 49ers D/ST quiet in Week 17
news.body: The 49ers D/ST failed to register a sack or force a turnover in a 42-38 win over the Bears in Week 17.
news.impact: The unit struggled to keep the Bears from moving the ball, allowing multiple touchdowns on the ground as well as through the air in the win. The defense will look to get back on track in a Week 18 contest against the Seattle Seahawks.

news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) seeing specialist Wednesday
news.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jayden Daniels is seeing a specialist on Wednesday.
news.impact: Quinn did not have an update on Daniels. There should be an update later this week.

news.head: Jayden Daniels (elbow) undergoes imaging Monday
news.body: Jayden Daniels underwent imaging on his dislocated elbow on Monday.
news.impact: Daniels is now slated to consult with a variety of experts over the next few days. He remains without a clear timetable to return.

news.head: Jayden Daniels suffers dislocated elbow Sunday
news.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said QB Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow.
news.impact: Daniels will undergo additional testing Monday. The X-Rays on Sunday showed no fracture. Marcus Mariota closed out Sunday's game for Washington.

news.head: Jayden Daniels suffers elbow injury Sunday
news.body: Jayden Daniels suffered an elbow injury on the final play of the first half for the Washington Commanders against the Dallas Cowboys Sunday.
news.impact: Daniels completed 11-of-17 for 96 yards and one touchdown while also rushing seven times for a team-leading 69 yards prior to exiting. Backup Marcus Mariota is in line to take over behind center against the Cowboys for head coach Dan Quinn Sunday.

news.head: Bijan Robinson held in check in Week 2 loss
news.body: Bijan Robinson ran 16 times for 72 yards and caught three of four targets for nine yards in the Falcons' 34-3 blowout loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
news.impact: Robinson was fine on the ground, 4.5 yards per carry, but still largely held in check. The Panthers didn't allow the Falcons to move the ball, mostly thanks to Atlanta's lack of competent QB play. If Michael Penix returns on Thursday, that will hopefully be a huge boost to Bijan's value. If not, it's looking like another long night for Bijan managers.

news.head: Bijan Robinson hauls in touchdown catch in Week 1
news.body: Bijan Robinson carried the ball 21 times for 83 yards and caught eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1.
news.impact: Robinson was basically the entire offense for the Falcons in the close loss to Pittsburgh. He scored the team's only touchdown on a 23-yard catch at the end of the first quarter. It was an excellent start to the season for the star running back, who will slot in as a high-end RB1 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Panthers.

news.head: Bijan Robinson agrees to three-year extension with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $75 million contract extension with the Atlanta Falcons according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: The deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money while also making Robinson the highest-paid running back in the league. The third-year back finished with 2,298 total offensive yards and 11 total touchdowns in 2025 and remains in the argument as the 1.01 pick in upcoming fantasy drafts with offensive minded Kevin Stefanski being named the new head coach this offseason for the Falcons.

news.head: Bijan Robinson does not practice Wednesday amid contract talks with Falcons
news.body: Bijan Robinson did not practice on Wednesday amid contract talks with the Falcons.
news.impact: Jahmyr Gibbs did not practice either on Wednesday for the same reason. Both players are under contract for two more seasons and are looking for new contracts. They'll both be among the league's highest paid running backs with new deals and deservingly so. This will remain a situation to monitor, but it's too early in training camp to have any major concerns.

news.head: Bo Nix throws for 288 yards, one TD in Week 2
news.body: Bo Nix completed 22 of his 31 passes for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception while adding five rushes for six yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Nix and the Broncos got off to a very slow start on offense, scoring just two field goals heading into the fourth quarter. He then led two touchdown-scoring drives in the fourth quarter to complete the come-from-behind win. Nix has thrown for 419 yards and two touchdowns through the first two games of the season. He is looking like a QB2 in fantasy heading into Week 3's matchup against the Rams.

news.head: Bo Nix struggles in loss Monday
news.body: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passing attempts for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Nix had a poor performance on Monday night. He was held to just 131 passing yards on the night and wasn't able to get Denver's offense going, leading them to score just ten points en route to a blowout loss at the hands of their divisional rivals. He should improve and play better in more favorable matchups moving forward, but they will continue to have a tough schedule for the foreseeable future, so fantasy managers might be better off looking for another option for the time being.

news.head: Bo Nix will not play in preseason opener
news.body: Bo Nix will not play in the Broncos preseason opener against the Falcons.
news.impact: Nix is expected to play in the second and third preseason games. Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger will both play a half.

news.head: Bo Nix (ankle) practices without limitations Wednesday
news.body: Bo Nix practiced on Wednesday at Broncos training camp without any limitations.
news.impact: Nix was able to get 7-on-7 work in during OTAs. He appears to be well on track to be good to go for the start of the season.

news.head: James Cook III plays well in win Thursday
news.body: James Cook III rushed the ball 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Buffalo's offense was firing on all cylinders on Thursday night, and that included Cook. He rushed for 135 yards at an efficient clip of 6.5 yards per carry on the night and was able to get into the end zone on one of those carries. He wasn't very involved in the passing game, but he still dominated the backfield and was the only running back to receive even a single opportunity for the Bills.

news.head: James Cook III goes for 69 yards in big win over Texans
news.body: James Cook III ran 13 times for 57 yards and caught three of four targets for 12 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Cook was fine on his touches and was saved by his three receptions in PPR formats, but it fantasy managers will be hoping for more. He’s still a premium running back, and he will get his chance early this week as the Bills play the Lions on Thursday night.

news.head: James Cook will play in preseason opener
news.body: James Cook III and all Bills starters are set to play Saturday, per HC Joe Brady.
news.impact: Cook is reportedly expected to have a larger role as a pass catcher in 2026. Saturday's preseason opener against the Panthers could offer a preview of the Bills' plans for their RB1.

news.head: James Cook III nets two carries in Week 18 win
news.body: James Cook III rushed for 15 yards on two carries in the Bills 35-8 win over the Jets.
news.impact: Cook and the majority of the Bills' starters on offense were used sparingly in the win over the Jets. Cook turned in an excellent season, finishing with 1,621 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns on 309 carries this season. He will remain a highly sought after pick in fantasy drafts in 2026.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence throws for 189 yards in Week 2 loss
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 17 of his 29 passes for 189 yards and an interception while adding six yards on two rushes in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Lawrence got the Jaguars off to a fast start as they were leading 10-3 at halftime, but the Broncos came to life on defense starting in the third quarter. Lawrence has now thrown for 434 yards and four touchdowns through the first two games of the season. He will be a solid QB1 in fantasy in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence flawless in big win over Browns
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns. He also ran twice for three yards.
news.impact: Lawrence played on easy mode against a Browns defense that just couldn't create stops. He had only five incompletions to four touchdowns on the day, a great ratio to have. With their win over the Browns, the Jags are the only AFC South team to clinch a win on Sunday. He faces a much tougher test against the Broncos next week.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence: Jaguars starters 'trending' towards playing Friday
news.body: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.impact: The Jaguars starters did not see the field in last week's preseason opener. If they do play, it'll likely be in limited fashion.

news.head: Trevor Lawrence tosses three touchdowns in win
news.body: Trevor Lawrence completed 22-of-30 passes for 255 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars 41-7 win over the Titans. He also ran twice for 11 yards.
news.impact: Lawrence capped off a great season with a dominant performance against the lowly Titans. It wasn't always pretty, and there were plenty of struggles early on this season, but HC Liam Coen and Lawrence were able to get things rolling. The team is looking like they could be a tough out in the postseason, but time will tell.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard leads backfield in win over Falcons
news.body: Chuba Hubbard ran 12 times for 53 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons. He also caught both of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown.
news.impact: Hubbard has out-touched the younger Jonathon Brooks, who missed some time in this game due to a groin injury, by a solid margin yet again. He appears to be the back to own in Carolina moving forward. He'll get to play Cleveland next time out.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard scores two touchdowns in Week 1 loss to Bears
news.body: Chuba Hubbard carried the ball 10 times for 49 yards and one touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 38 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard took advantage of a primary ball-carrying option before the game script changed, leading the team in rushing yards in the loss. The running back remains a solid option out of the backfield for head coach Dave Canales, with a Week 2 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) off injury report for Week 1
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hubbard was battling a hamstring injury earlier this offseason, but it's no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 1. He will likely split work with Jonathan Brooks (groin) in the season opener, which hurts the fantasy outlook for both of them.

news.head: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) week-to-week with hamstring injury
news.body: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is week-to-week with a hamstring injury per HC Dave Canales. He is expected to play in Week 1.
news.impact: While it sounds like Hubbard should be good to go for the season opener, he could still be limited following a multi-week absence. With that said, it’s now wheels up for Jonathon Brooks, who’s now going to see his ADP rise yet again.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III totals 178 yards in OT win Sunday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 24 times for 117 yards and caught 6-of-10 targets for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Walker's hot start to the season continued on Sunday night. He totaled 178 yards from scrimmage in a big win over the Colts, and he was able to do that while maintaining terrific efficiency. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy asset for as long as he remains healthy and on the field moving forward.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III dominant in win Monday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III rushed the ball 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while catching 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards and an additional touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Walker was absolutely dominant in his debut with the Chiefs on Monday night. He totaled 191 yards and two touchdowns over the course of the game, which was especially impressive considering that he did it against one of the best defenses in the NFL in the Broncos. He looks great on his new offense and should be in line for a huge season if he can stay healthy with this increased workload.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III (foot) off injury report for Monday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III (foot) is off of the injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Walker was previously dealing with a foot injury of some kind, but he is over it now and is no longer listed on the team's injury report ahead of their Week 1 matchup against the Broncos. Fantasy managers should expect him to be highly involved on Monday night, although the tough matchup may hurt his ceiling from a fantasy perspective.

news.head: Kenneth Walker III (foot) not practicing Tuesday
news.body: Kenneth Walker III is not practicing on Tuesday due to a foot injury.
news.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Walker. His status will need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.head: Trey McBride snags touchdown in loss to Seattle
news.body: Trey McBride caught eight of 10 targets for 41 yards and a score in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.impact: McBride was the only thing working for the offense on Sunday, and even that only lasted but for so long. Seattle completely shut down the Cardinals in the second half, and McBride with them. But, it's doubtful any fantasy manager will complain about eight catches for 40+ yards and a score from their tight end.

news.head: Trey McBride (rest/back) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.body: Trey McBride (rest/back) did not take part in Arizona's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Arizona gave their star tight end the day off on Wednesday as a rest day. He was also listed with a back issue of some kind, but it seems to be nothing serious and isn't likely to play a factor on his availability for Week 2. He will remain a top-tier fantasy asset every time he's healthy and on the field for the Cardinals.

news.head: Trey McBride starts season with strong performance
news.body: Trey McBride hauled in 9-of-13 targets for 95 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: McBride is arguably the league's top fantasy asset at tight end, and he certainly looked the part in Week 1. Coming off back-to-back seasons with more than 100 receptions and 1,100 yards, McBride was QB Jacoby Brissett's favorite target on Sunday, getting five more looks than the next-closest Arizona pass catcher.

news.head: Trey McBride hauls in seven passes in Week 18 win
news.body: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 65 yards in the Cardinals 37-20 loss to the Rams.
news.impact: McBride was tied for the team lead in targets and led the team in receptions Sunday. Despite a shaky quarterback situation, McBride will be one of the top tight ends drafted by fantasy managers in 2026.

news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) in boot Wednesday
news.body: Rico Dowdle was wearing a boot on his right foot during practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Dowdle left last week's game early with what was reported as a toe injury. He remains day-to-day.

news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) day-to-day
news.body: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle is considered day-to-day with a toe injury.
news.impact: Dowdle was carted to the locker room on Sunday with the injury. He checked out "relatively OK" following tests.

news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) finishes with nine touches in Week 2 loss
news.body: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle rushed for 22 yards on seven carries and caught both of his targets for 22 yards in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: Dowdle suffered the toe injury in the second quarter but was cleared to return after the half. He was later ruled out with the same injury, so he may have reaggravated it in the second half. If Dowdle is unable to suit up in Week 3, Jaylen Warren will be the primary running back against the Bengals.

news.head: Rico Dowdle (toe) returns to the game Sunday
news.body: Steelers RB Rico Dowdle (toe) has returned to the game to start the second half against the Patriots.
news.impact: Dowdle was carted to the locker room in the second quarter but has returned and took the first carry of the second half. Dowdle and Jaylen Warren will continue to operate as the top two running backs for the Steelers.

news.head: George Pickens hauls in six passes in Week 2
news.body: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys in a win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Pickens had a much needed bounce back performance after tallying just three receptions. Although Pickens has not found the endzone yet this season, the increase in targets and receptions over the first week is a strong sign that Pickens will remain a factor in this offense. The Cowboys will take on the Ravens in Week 3.

news.head: George Pickens held to 28 yards Sunday
news.body: George Pickens caught 3-of-6 targets for just 28 yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Pickens had an extremely disappointing start to the season on Sunday night. He was held to just 28 yards on three catches in the team's first game of the season after being hyped up as an elite fantasy prospect throughout the preseason. He should bounce back and play better than this moving forward, but his week-to-week floor may be lower than some realize if Dallas' offense struggles with consistency this season.

news.head: George Pickens to play 2026 season on franchise tag with Cowboys
news.body: George Pickens will officially play the 2026 season on a $27.3 million franchise tag for the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Pickens and the Cowboys could not agree upon a long-term extension this summer, so he will head into the year effectively on a 1-year deal. The wideout is coming off a career year in which he hauled in 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He will head into this season with Dallas firmly in the WR1 conversation in fantasy.

news.head: George Pickens expected to move around formation more this season
news.body: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said he plans to move WR George Pickens around the formation more this season.
news.impact: Pickens has reported to mandatory minicamp after sitting out of voluntary OTAs. He is expected to play both on the outside and in the slot, adding to the versatility he will offer the Cowboys offense.

news.head: Garrett Wilson finds end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.body: Garrett Wilson hauled in five of his seven targets for 57 yards and one touchdown in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.impact: Wilson continues to make the most of sizeable involvement in an underperforming passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful options as part of a Jets offense filled with more questions than answers early on ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions.

news.head: Garrett Wilson goes for 79 yards in Week 1
news.body: Garrett Wilson caught six of his seven targets for 79 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Wilson led the Jets in all receiving categories in the easy win over an overmatched Tennessee team. Even though it wasn't a huge performance from Wilson, it was an encouraging debut for the receiver with Geno Smith at the helm. Wilson settles in as a high-end WR2 in a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

news.head: Garrett Wilson (illness) back at practice Tuesday
news.body: Garrett Wilson (illness) was back in action Tuesday after missing Monday's practice.
news.impact: Nothing much to see here for Wilson. The Jets' No. 1 receiver sat out Monday due to being under the weather, but he was back on the practice field Tuesday.

news.head: Garrett Wilson (illness) not at practice Monday
news.body: Garrett Wilson (illness) did not participate in practice on Monday due to an illness.
news.impact: Thankfully, this sort of practice absence is one where it raises little, if any, concern. Wilson will likely return to practice as normal within the next day or so.

news.head: Cam Little makes two FGs in Week 2
news.body: Cam Little made two of his three field goals and added an extra point in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Little hit field goals from 44 and 23 yards out in the game. The veteran kicker has hit four of his five field goals while going a perfect 5-for-5 on extra points through two games. He will take on the Patriots in Week 3.

news.head: Cam Little has nice day against Browns
news.body: Cam Little made both of his field goal attempts and all four of his PATs in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Little should be a nice kicker for those in need of one, or for those who have him, thanks to the firepower the Jags offense possesses. He will look to keep up his success next week against Denver.

news.head: Cam Little racks up 11 kicking points in win
news.body: Cam Little made all five of his PATs and both of his field goal attempts in the Jaguars' 41-7 win over the Titans.
news.impact: Little had a great game with the Jaguars putting up a scoring onslaught against the Titans. He's now put up 10+ kicking points in each of his last five games.

news.head: Cam Little makes all five kicks Sunday
news.body: Cam Little connected on 3-of-3 field goal attempts and 2-of-2 extra point attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: Little has connected on 28-of-32 field goals overall. He should be in line for plenty of opportunities in Week 18 against the Titans.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (core) officially on IR
news.body: Jonathon Brooks (core) was officially placed on IR on Wednesday.
news.impact: Brooks had core muscle surgery on Wednesday and will be out for at least four weeks on IR. The 23-year-old's timetable is actually projected to be around six weeks. Chuba Hubbard will continue to shoulder the load ouf of the backfield for the Panthers.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing surgery, will miss about 6 weeks
news.body: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to undergo surgery on his core to repair an injury he sustained on Sunday. His expected time to recover is six weeks and is expected to land on IR.
news.impact: It’s a tough blow for Brooks, who had just gotten back to the playing field after roughly two years away from it. When Brooks returns, he’ll still have time to make some noise before the season ends, but there’s no telling how much work he will get. Chuba Hubbard will carry the load in Carolina with Brooks out, so be expecting at least RB2 numbers from him thanks to volume.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks (groin) undergoing tests
news.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said RB Jonathon Brooks is undergoing tests on his groin injury.
news.impact: The team is still gathering information on the severity of the injury. There should be an update on Brooks this week.

news.head: Jonathon Brooks leaves Week 2 win early with groin injury
news.body: Jonathon Brooks (groin) left the Panthers' 34-3 blowout win over the Falcons with a groin injury. Before leaving, he ran five times for 16 yards and caught his only target for a loss of five.
news.impact: Brooks looked like he was firmly the Panthers' RB2 behind Chuba Hubbard before his injury, with Hubbard taking the majority of the rushing and red-zone work. Now, with this groin injury, Brooks could miss a week or two, depending on the severity.

news.head: Josh Allen scores five touchdowns in dominant showing Thursday
news.body: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passing attempts for 248 yards and three touchdowns while adding 69 yards and two touchdowns on the ground in Sunday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Allen had an insane showing on Thursday night. He totaled over 300 yards and scored five total touchdowns en route to a big win over the Lions in primetime, all while protecting the ball and committing zero turnovers. He has been absolutely dominant through the first two games of the season and is pacing to be one of, if not the most valuable individual player that anyone can roster at this point.

news.head: Josh Allen dismantles Houston defense in big win
news.body: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards with two touchdowns with an additional 23 yards and two scores on the ground on six carries in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Allen was in complete control on Sunday, carving up what should have been a difficult Texans defense on his way to a four touchdown performance. He will have another nice matchup against Detroit on Thursday who just allowed a 30-point game to the Saints.

news.head: Josh Allen won't play Thursday
news.body: Josh Allen won't play in Thursday night's preseason finale against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.impact: Allen saw some action earlier on in the preseason, but he is set to be sidelined for the team's final preseason game on Thursday night. He is fully healthy at this point and looks primed for another huge season from a fantasy perspective.

news.head: Josh Allen will play in preseason opener
news.body: Bills HC Joe Brady said starters will play against the Panthers in the preseason opener.
news.impact: Allen and the starters will have an opportunity to knock off any lingering rust while building momentum for the regular season.

news.head: Jalen Coker snags eight passes in win
news.body: Jalen Coker caught eight of nine targets for 66 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons.
news.impact: Coker had some great grabs in this game, including some toe-tapping plays along the sideline. He and Tet McMillan are forming a promising duo for the Panthers, and Coker is worth starting every week.

news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) logs full practice Friday
news.body: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Jalen Coker was a full participant in practice on Friday.
news.impact: Coker began the week in a precautionary boot after he injured his ankle last Sunday against the Bears. He'll remain an upside WR3/flex play for fantasy managers heading into Week 2.

news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) takes part in special teams drills to begin practice
news.body: Jalen Coker took part in special teams drills to begin practice on Friday.
news.impact: Coker was limited in practice to begin the week. He appears on track to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

news.head: Jalen Coker (ankle) officially limited Thursday
news.body: Jalen Coker (ankle) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Coker logged a second-straight limited practice session on Thursday. It seems like he is strongly trending towards playing at full health in Week 2, but it's worth keeping an eye on the team's final injury report after practice on Friday to see if he goes into the weekend with an injury designation.

news.head: Justin Jefferson leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Bears
news.body: Justin Jefferson hauled in three of his six targets for a team-high 55 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Jefferson has made the most of generous involvement in an inconsistent Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two games. The superstar wideout continues to fall victim to underwhelming quarterback play, with a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers up next.

news.head: Justin Jefferson scores two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Justin Jefferson caught 8-of-9 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Despite Kyler Murray leaving in the first quarter with a concussion, Jefferson was still able to produce in a big way with Carson Wentz. He remains a locked and loaded high-end WR1.

news.head: Justin Jefferson restructures contract with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of Justin Jefferson.
news.impact: Minnesota is making moves to clear salary cap space. Pelissero notes they still have work to do to get under the cap by Wednesday.

news.head: Justin Jefferson goes over 100 receiving yards in Week 18
news.body: Justin Jefferson ended the 2025 season on a high note, catching eight passes for 101 yards in the Vikings' 16-3 win over the Packers on Sunday.
news.impact: With the 101 yards, Jefferson joined Mike Evans and Randy Moss as the only players in NFL history to record at least 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six seasons. It was, however, a bit of a down year for Jefferson, who finished with a career-low 1,048 yards and just two touchdowns. The 100-yard effort on Sunday was just his third of the season and his first since October 5. Jefferson was hurt by inconsistent quarterback play this season, but he still remains one of the best receivers in the NFL and should be a favorite to rebound in 2026.

news.head: Jadarian Price sees 14 touches in win
news.body: Jadarian Price ran 13 times for 52 yards and caught one of two targets for eight yards in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over Arizona on Sunday.
news.impact: Price tied with Cooper Kupp for third in targets on the Seahawks, but with it being just two targets, that's not saying much. He was behind Emanuel Wilson this week in rushing as well, who had 21 carries of his own. Price has been involved, but not featured so far through two weeks, very reminiscent of his days at Notre Dame. It'll be tough to start him outside of a flex play until he either shows more or is fed more work.

news.head: Jadarian Price suffers shoulder injury Sunday
news.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury in Sunday's win against the Cardinals.
news.impact: It was originally reported to be a chest injury for Price, but Macdonald said Monday it was a shoulder injury. He said "it’s intact and nothing serious, it seems like." Emmanuel Wilson wound up seeing 21 carries. He would figure to see a big role in Week 3 against the Commanders if Price is sidelined.

news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) has X-rays return negative
news.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said X-rays returned negative on Jadarian Price's chest injury.
news.impact: Price left Sunday's game in the second half and did not return, but it is worth noting the game was out of hand. His status will need to be monitored in practice this upcoming week.

news.head: Jadarian Price (chest) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Jadarian Price (chest) is questionable to return for the Seattle Seahawks against the Arizona Cardinals Sunday according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: Price hauled in one of his two targets for eight yard while rushing 13 times for 52 yards prior to exiting. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani take over backfield duties in the fourth quarter against the Cardinals Sunday.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown scores twice in loss Thursday
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 6-of-8 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday night's 41-31 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
news.impact: St. Brown was on fire on Thursday night. He had a slow start, but he ended up finishing the game with a team high in receptions and receiving yards while finding the end zone twice against the Bills. He will continue to be a top-tier fantasy option moving forward, especially in PPR scoring formats.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauls in 10 receptions in Week 1 win over Saints
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown hauled in 10 of his team-leading 14 targets for 67 yards and two touchdowns in the Lions' 31-30 Week 1 win over the New Orleans Saints.
news.impact: St. Brown was dynamic in the season-opening contest for head coach Dan Campbell, hauling in both of quarterback Jared Goff's touchdown passes in the win. The wideout remains an elite WR1 option in all formats ahead of a Week 2 road matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown has contract restructured by Lions
news.body: The Lions restructured the contract of WR Amon-Ra St. Brown.
news.impact: LT Penei Sewell also had his contract restructured. The Lions created $35.68 million in cap space.

news.head: Amon-Ra St. Brown catches 11 passes in Week 18
news.body: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 11-of-15 targets for a game-high 139 yards in Detroit's Week 18 victory over the Bears.
news.impact: St. Brown closed out the year on a high note by registering his fifth 100-yard receiving effort of the season. It was also the second time this year that he caught more than 10 passes in a game. St. Brown remains one of the top receivers in the game and he closes out the year with 117 catches for 1,401 yards and 11 scores.

news.head: Harrison Mevis misses kick in win Monday
news.body: Harrison Mevis went 4-for-4 on his extra-point attempts but missed his lone field-goal attempt in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Mevis missed a field goal late in Monday night's game, but luckily for him, it wasn't very consequential with Los Angeles already being up several scores. He should return to being a solid fantasy option at the position somewhat soon.

news.head: Harrison Mevis kicks single PAT in loss to Niners
news.body: Harrison Mevis made his only PAT attempt in the Rams' 27-7 tough loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Mevis wasn't called upon much, the Rams offense was just never in scoring position for most of the game. He could have come in in the second half, but the Rams elected to go for it on 4th and goal at the 1 yard line, which was the correct choice, but their failure to convert meant Mevis was going to have an even bigger stinker. Brighter days are ahead for the Rams kicker.

news.head: Harrison Mevis returns to Rams after being tendered Monday
news.body: Harrison Mevis has been tendered by the Rams and will return to Los Angeles for the 2026 season.
news.impact: Undrafted out of Missouri in 2024, Mevis was a revelation for both the Rams and for fantasy owners last season. He replaced Joshua Karty as Los Angeles' kicker midway through they year and went 12-for-13 on field goal tries and a perfect 39-of-39 on extra point attempts in nine regular season games. He was also perfect in three postseason contests, going 6-for-6 on field goals and 9-for-9 on PATs. Mevis will open 2026 as the Rams' primary kicker and, given the potency of Los Angeles' offense, should be in line for a big year.

news.head: Harrison Mevis perfect in Week 18
news.body: Harrison Mevis connected on 3-of-3 field goals and 4-of-4 extra points in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Mevis connected on field goals from 34, 40, and 42 yards out in the win. Mevis will end his first season with the Rams 12-of-13 on field goal attempts and 39-of-39 on extra point attempts.

news.head: Terry McLaurin quiet in Week 2 loss
news.body: Terry McLaurin caught 2-of-9 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders loss to Dallas.
news.impact: McLaurin saw a major increase in targets from Week 1, but his production continued to be limited. With Jayden Daniels out, McLaurin could see an increase in targets considering his rapport with Marcus Maroita. McLaurin and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

news.head: Terry McLaurin quiet in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Terry McLaurin caught two of his four targets for 14 yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: McLaurin was one of the more underwhelming options as part of a disappointing Washington aerial attack in the season opener, averaging 7.0 yards per reception in the loss. The wideout will look to get back on track in Week 2 against a Dallas Cowboys that struggled to slow down the New York Giants in Week 1.

news.head: Terry McLaurin expected to play against Lions
news.body: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin is set to start against the Lions on Saturday.
news.impact: McLaurin enters the fantasy football season as a top-50 selection. He and Jayden Daniels will have an opportunity to build momentum ahead of the regular season.

news.head: Terry McLaurin catches four passes in season finale
news.body: Terry McLaurin caught all four of his targets for 57 yards in a 24-17 win over the Eagles in Week 18.
news.impact: McLaurin finished as the Commanders' receiving leader in the season-ender. The veteran did not live up to expectations in 2025, appearing in just 10 games due to injury. He wound up with just 38 catches for 582 yards and three touchdowns along the way. McLaurin is a candidate to post a bounce-back season for Washington in 2026.

news.head: David Montgomery sees just six carries Sunday
news.body: David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 2-of-2 targets for 14 yards receiving.
news.impact: After a huge Week 1 performance, it was a game to forget for Montgomery and the entire Texans run game. He'll look to bounce back next week against the Colts.

news.head: David Montgomery has big debut for Texans
news.body: David Montgomery rushed for 60 yards and two scores on 20 carries, adding three receptions for 19 yards and another touchdown in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Montgomery was given 23 touches in his debut with the Texans, as the veteran back was a focal point of the offense. Granted, he only averaged 3.0 yards per carry, but he found the end zone three times while being involved both on the ground and through the air.

news.head: David Montgomery traded to Houston Texans
news.body: David Montgomery has been traded to the Houston Texans. Houston is sending a fourth rounder, OL Juice Scruggs, and a seventh back to Detroit.
news.impact: Montgomery had made it known he wanted a new opportunity given his lack of usage last year, and the Texans came calling. Monty offers a big upgrade over Nick Chubb as the primary thumper, and his ability in the passing game could easily endanger Woody Marks value as well. For dynasty, it’s great for Montgomery and Jahmyr Gibbs managers, while Marks managers will have to deal with a much bigger threat to any potential volume. This also likely means Joe Mixon, who missed all of last season, is done in Houston.

news.head: David Montgomery gets eight carries in Week 18
news.body: David Montgomery carried the ball eight times for 42 yards and added one catch for 13 yards in Detroit's win over Chicago on Sunday.
news.impact: Montgomery has seen his production drop over the last couple of seasons as Jahmyr Gibbs has emerged as the lead back for the Lions. The seventh-year running back still had a solid campaign with 158 carries for 716 yards and eight scores. However, the carries and the rushing yards were new career-lows for Montgomery.

news.head: Broncos D/ST holds Jags to 13 points
news.body: The Broncos D/ST allowed 13 points while notching two sacks and forcing one turnover in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Denver's defense made life difficult for the Jacksonville offense, holding them to just three points after halftime. It was a needed bounce-back performance after the Broncos struggled on defense against the Chiefs in Week 1. They will look to keep it going in Week 3 against the Rams.

news.head: Broncos D/ST dismal in loss Monday
news.body: The Broncos' D/ST logged two sacks and one interception while allowing 31 points in Monday night's blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Denver's defense is supposed to be among the best in the entire NFL, but they didn't look the part on Monday night. They allowed Patrick Mahomes II to lead Kansas City to 31 points on the night, despite the fact that this was his first game back from a major injury and was missing one of his starting tackles. This unit should return to elite form at some point this season, but they have a rocky schedule coming up for the next 4-6 weeks and should not be considered an elite fantasy option at the position for that stretch of games.

news.head: Broncos D/ST scores touchdown in Week 18 win
news.body: The Broncos' D/ST logged four sacks, one interception, one fumble recovery, and a touchdown while allowing just three points in Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Denver's defense has been among the best in the league all season long, and they had a suitable performance to end the regular season on Sunday. They logged four sacks and two turnovers against the Chargers, one of which they were able to take to the house for a touchdown. This unit will make life hard for any team they end up playing in the postseason.

news.head: Denver defense dominates on Christmas Day
news.body: The Broncos defense surrendered 13 points on only 139 yards of total offense, registering one sack in Thursday's win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: This Christmas, the Broncos defense was given the gift of a struggling Chiefs offense led by a third-string QB making his first career start. The Denver unit took full advantage, shutting down the Chiefs on the ground and through the air. The Broncos feature a strong defense, but the task will be more difficult against the Chargers in Week 18.

news.head: Stefon Diggs hauls in two touchdowns in Week 2
news.body: Stefon Diggs caught 5-of-6 targets for 47 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
news.impact: Diggs caught touchdowns from both Jayden Daniels and Marcus Maroita to account for both of the team's touchdowns. Diggs has turned in two strong games in his first season in Washington. Diggs and the Commanders will take on the Seahawks in Week 3.

news.head: Stefon Diggs finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Eagles
news.body: Stefon Diggs hauled in four of his nine targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Diggs saw plenty of volume as part of a Washington passing attack held in check, leading the team in targets in a losing effort. The veteran wideout offers fantasy managers a stable WR2/3 option while the Commanders offense looks to get back on track in a Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

news.head: Stefon Diggs expected to play against Lions
news.body: Stefon Diggs is set to make his Commanders debut in the preseason on Saturday.
news.impact: Diggs will see his first action as a member of the Commanders. It will be worth tuning in to see what his exact role looks like.

news.head: Stefon Diggs signs with Commanders
news.body: The Washington Commanders have signed WR Stefon Diggs
news.impact: Diggs had been closely linked to Washington for a while. He should step into the immediate No. 2 wide receiver role behind Terry McLaurin. He is coming off a 1,000 yard season with the Patriots. This likely means they won't be signing Brandon Aiyuk.

news.head: DK Metcalf leads team in targets in Week 2 loss
news.body: Steelers WR DK Metcalf caught 4-of-9 targets for 27 yards in a 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: Metcalf was shadowed by Patriots DB Christian Gonzalez for the majority of the game, limiting his production and forcing Aaron Rodgers to look elsewhere. Metcalf has lead the team in targets in the first two games, so the target volume is encouraging, fantasy managers are just waiting for it to result in more production. Metcalf and the Steelers will take on the Bengals in Week 3.

news.head: DK Metcalf leads Steelers with 10 targets in Week 1
news.body: DK Metcalf caught four of his 10 targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Metcalf didn't do much damage but his usage was encouraging as he easily led the Steelers in targets while newcomer Michael Pittman Jr. saw just three looks from Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: DK Metcalf off injury report for Week 1
news.body: DK Metcalf is off of the injury report for Week 1's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.impact: Metcalf was dealing with an undisclosed injury earlier, but it's not an issue for him anymore and he is off of the injury report entirely ahead of Week 1. He goes into the season as the projected top target for the Steelers this season.

news.head: DK Metcalf practices Monday
news.body: DK Metcalf practiced on Monday.
news.impact: Metcalf missed time during training camp with an undisclosed injury. He remains on track to be good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Falcons.

news.head: Jaylen Warren not seen practicing Wednesday
news.body: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: It is unclear what Warren is dealing with. Rico Dowdle also did not practice and was seen in a boot on his right foot.

news.head: Jaylen Warren tallies 13 touches in Week 2 loss
news.body: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren rushed for 43 yards on 11 carries in the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the Patriots. He caught 2-of-4 targets for 34 yards.
news.impact: Warren saw the majority of the work after Rico Dowdle was ruled out with a toe injury. If Dowdle is unable to play in Week 3, Warren would be expected to handle the bulk of the work against a Bengals' defense that looked strong in a win over Houston.

news.head: Jaylen Warren leads Pittsburgh backfield in Week 1
news.body: Jaylen Warren carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards while catching five of his six targets for 27 yards and losing a fumble in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Warren and Rico Dowdle split first-team reps in the preseason, but it was Warren who emerged with the better game in Week 1, out-touching Dowdle 15 to 10 and out-gaining him 73 to 21. Warren will be a flex option for fantasy purposes heading into Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle both see first-team reps Thursday
news.body: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle split the first-team reps in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Warren and Dowdle continue to rotate who sees the first reps with the first-team. They are likely to both be involved in a committee in the Steelers backfield this season.

news.head: De'Von Achane grinds out 93 yards of offense in Week 2
news.body: De'Von Achane gained 74 yards on 20 carries and caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Achane's touches went up in Week 2, but his efficiency in the Dolphins' anemic offense was about the same. The dual-threat back has yet to find the end zone through two games while averaging just 3.5 yards per carry. He's best viewed as an RB2 for now, with his volume of touches being the main reason. Achane has a tough matchup coming against the Chiefs.

news.head: De'Von Achane sees 15 touches in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: De'Von Achane carried the ball 11 times for 36 yards while also hauling in four of his five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 Week 1 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Achane was unable to find much running room out of the backfield in the season opener, with the Las Vegas defense challenging new starting quarterback Malik Willis to beat it through the air. The running back remains a dynamic option in PPR formats, but fantasy managers may need to temper expectations in the short term, with a Week 2 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) cleared to practice
news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said De'Von Achane is ready to go after offseason shoulder surgery.
news.impact: Achane didn't participate in team drills this spring as he rehabbed, but he's good to go now that training camp's here. He'll be in line for his workhorse role as the focal point of the Dolphins offense.

news.head: De'Von Achane (shoulder) sees uptick in reps in minicamp Tuesday
news.body: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane reportedly saw an uptick in practice activity at Tuesday’s minicamp session.
news.impact: Achane is continuing to work his way back from an offseason procedure on his shoulder. He is expected to be good to go for training camp.

news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. sees one target in loss
news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. failed to catch his only target in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle on Sunday.
news.impact: This is a big development for Harrison. He only caught one pass in the season opener, and now that has escalated to just a single target in this game. It's unclear if the team has given up on him, or if it's more of a lack of effort on his part, QB Jacoby Brissett looking elsewhere when targeting receivers, or some combination of all three. Either way, the team needs to figure out a way to use their 2024 first-round investment. That, or trade him away to a new team and acquire assets while he gets a fresh start.

news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. finishes with one grab in season opener
news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught only 1-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Aside from one big play, Harrison did not make much of a mark for the Cardinals in Sunday's win. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett looked Harrison's way just three times, which was good for only fifth on the team. After finishing well behind fellow wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (8) and Michael Wilson (7) in targets, Harrison might be best viewed as a wait-and-see bench stash for now.

news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. dealing with cramps
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Marvin Harrison Jr. was dealing with cramps.
news.impact: Harrison had to stop practicing a couple times on Sunday. It is a positive sign it isn't a leg or hamstring injury he is dealing with.

news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. expected to play role as X-receiver
news.body: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Marvin Harrison Jr. will play the Davante Adams role as the team’s X-receiver.
news.impact: LaFleur has spent the past three years as the Rams offensive coordinator and figures to bring a lot of what he learned under Sean McVay to the Cardinals offense. This could benefit Harrison's involvement in the red zone the most as we saw from Adams last season in the same spot.

news.head: Derrick Henry finds the end zone in Week 2
news.body: Derrick Henry rushed for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints. He caught all three of his targets for 19 yards.
news.impact: Henry found the end zone on a one-yard rush in the first quarter. The veteran was held in check after that, unable to find any big gains on the ground. Henry and the Ravens will take on Dallas in Week 3.

news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for three touchdowns in Week 1 win over Colts
news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards and three touchdowns while also hauling in his lone target for 19 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Henry capitalized on a sizeable workload out of the Baltimore backfield, averaging an impressive 6.0 yards per carry in the Week 1 win. The superstar running back remains locked in as a reliable RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Derrick Henry rushes for 126 yards in Week 18
news.body: Derrick Henry carried the ball 20 times for 126 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Henry was unable to corral his lone target in the contest. With the loss, the Ravens will miss the playoffs in a disappointing ending to the season. Henry finishes the year with 1,595 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns while appearing in all 17 games. He will remain a solid RB1 for fantasy purposes heading into the 2026 season.

news.head: Derrick Henry has historic night against Packers
news.body: Derrick Henry ran 36 times for 216 yards and four touchdowns in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers on Saturday.
news.impact: Henry's performance could easily be what decides the title for many fantasy championships. His 36 rush attempts were a career high in a single game, and his four touchdowns tied his career high in touchdowns in a game. Henry now has over 1,400 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns this season, a great total. The King is still on the throne.

news.head: Kaelon Black gets seven carries in Week 2
news.body: Kaelon Black gained 25 yards on seven carries in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: After gaining 65 yards on 14 carries in Week 1, Black saw his attempts cut in half in Week 2. The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Sunday's win, but Brock Purdy more than made up for that with his passing prowess. Black has gained 90 yards on 21 carries through two games, and he maintains decent fantasy value as the backup to Christian McCaffrey.

news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) active for Week 2
news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is active for Week 2 for the San Francisco 49ers against the Miami Dolphins according to Nick Wagoner.
news.impact: Black is good to go after not experiencing any setbacks during pregame warmups for head coach Kyle Shanahan, offering another dynamic option alongside Christian McCaffrey out of the San Francisco backfield against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) expected to play on Sunday
news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is expected to play on Sunday against the Dolphins.
news.impact: If Black plays it seems unlikely he'll have the 50-50 split with Christian McCaffrey he had last time out, and likely will play a more complementary role. However, if the Niners do get up big, he could see a decent amount of touches, so he could be flex-worthy in deep formats.

news.head: Kaelon Black (groin) questionable to play Sunday
news.body: Kaelon Black (groin) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: The rookie was added to the injury report due to a groin issue on Thursday and will officially be questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Dolphins. He was quite involved in San Francisco's season opener last week, so his absence would likely lead to Christian McCaffrey seeing a supermajority of touches for the team in Week 2.

news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in five passes Monday
news.body: Isaiah Likely hauled in 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.impact: Likely didn't put up great numbers on Monday night, finishing with just 33 yards in a loss to the Rams. He was still the most targeted player on the team by far, however, which is a good sign that he will bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future. His bounce back may be delayed is Jaxson Dart (knee) has to miss time for the Giants.

news.head: Isaiah Likely hauls in two touchdowns in win Sunday
news.body: Isaiah Likely caught eight passes for 78 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Likely exceeded expectations in his first game as a Giant on Sunday. He led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns on the night, scoring twice in what turned out to be a huge win over the Cowboys. His involvement on this offense looks great right now and he will likely be one of the hot waiver additions this week in any league he's not already rostered in.

news.head: Isaiah Likely signs three-year deal with Giants
news.body: The Giants are signing Isaiah Likely to a three-year, $40 million contract.
news.impact: The deal is worth to $47.5 million as Likely reunites with John Harbaugh. He should take on a bigger role with the Giants than what he had in Baltimore. He will be on the TE1 radar for fantasy managers.

news.head: Isaiah Likely to draw interest from Giants
news.body: The Giants are expected to show interest in free agent TE Isaiah Likely.
