news.impact: Likely has history with new Giants head coach John Harbaugh. New York will be looking to bring in more offensive weapons to help the development of Jaxson Dart as they're likely losing Wan'Dale Robinson in free agency. Likely is one of the top tight ends available in free agency.

news.head: DJ Moore (shoulder) diagnosed with AC joint sprain, status day-to-day
news.body: DJ Moore (shoulder) has been diagnosed with an AC joint sprain and his status is day-to-day. A source said “He has a chance to play next week, but it’s not a lock.”
news.impact: Moore was injured while trying to catch a pass in the endzone, falling hard on his shoulder as a defensive back rolled over top of him. At first the injury looked serious, but he was able to sit up and walk off the field under his own power. More than likely Moore will miss at least a week, but if there’s any silver lining, the Bills get a mini-bye here thanks to the Thursday night game. Once he returns he will go back to being a featured target in the Bills passing attack. But if he misses time, Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir will be the primary targets for Josh Allen, but don’t sleep on Keon Coleman, who saw some sneaky good usage once, and even before, Moore was knocked out.

news.head: DJ Moore questionable to return with shoulder injury
news.body: DJ Moore is questionable to return with a shoulder injury.
news.impact: Viewers of the broadcast were able to see Moore get up and walk off under his own power after taking a big hit in the endzone. However, he is headed to the locker room for further x-ray examination and is questionable to return.

news.head: DJ Moore goes for 100 yards in win over Houston
news.body: DJ Moore caught 5 of 8 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans.
news.impact: Moore looked good and re-invigorated in this game, showing off some of his old self against a Houston defense that didn’t look like its normal self. His touchdown was a bit fluky, as the defensive back solely made a play on the ball and failed do to so, leaving no one around Moore while he walked in for a score. But, fantasy managers won’t be complaining. Next up for DJ are the Detroit Lions, who just allowed big days for Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele on Sunday.

news.head: DJ Moore avoids serious ankle injury Saturday
news.body: Bills coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore was “good to go” after suffering an ankle injury in Saturday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
news.impact: Moore appeared to have his ankle rolled up on after a catch and run. He hauled in 3-of-4 targets for 61 yards in his first official game with the Bills and Josh Allen.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) out at least six weeks
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least six weeks for the New England Patriots according to Ian Rapoport.
news.impact: Brown was placed on injured reserve after suffering the ankle injury in New England’s Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks Wednesday night, leaving head coach Mike Vrable without his top pass-catching option for the foreseeable future. In the wideout’s absence Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and DeMario Douglas will need to step up for quarterback Drake Maye early in the season.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) placed on injured reserve
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) has been placed on injured reserve by the New England Patriots according to Adam Schefter.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) expect to miss at least four weeks
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss at least four weeks with a high ankle sprain that he sustained early in the third quarter of the Patriots game against the Seahawks on Wednesday night.
news.impact: It’s a big blow to Brown’s Fantasy stock to start the season. In his absence, expect Hunter Henry and Romeo Doubs to see more work. However, with Doubs was struggling to find snaps and catch the ball, it’s possible that Demario Douglas could be a nice PPR sleeper.

news.head: A.J. Brown (ankle) believed to have suffered high-ankle sprain on Wednesday
news.body: A.J. Brown (ankle) is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in last nights game against the Seahawks. He will have an MRI today to determine the extent of the injury and how much time he will miss.
news.impact: It’s a tough start to Browns Patriot tenure. He went down early in the third quarter and did not return, leaving Drake Maye to lean on Hunter Henry, Demario Douglas, and Mack Hollins with fellow newcomer Romeo Doubs struggling to catch anything. Doubs should bounce back, and if Brown is out for any period of time, expect Doubs and Henry to have some more fantasy appeal, with Douglas as a PPR dart throw in deep formats.

news.head: Rome Odunze catches three passes in Week 2 loss
news.body: Rome Odunze caught three of his four targets for 43 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Odunze has struggled to make an impact in a slow-starting Chicago passing attack to begin the season, finishing with three receptions or less in each of the first two games. The pass-catcher remains difficult to trust with the potential absence of quarterback Caleb Williams ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) off injury report for Week 2
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Odunze has been recovering from a calf injury for a while, but it seems that he is fully over it at this point, as he isn't listed on Chicago's injury report at all heading into Week 2. It's likely that his workload will ramp up this week after he was limited in the season opener, which should help him to produce a fantasy finish better than his underwhelming performance in Week 1.

news.head: Rome Odunze quiet in Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze caught two of his three targets for 52 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers
news.impact: Odunze made the most of minimal usage in the Chicago passing attack in the season opener, averaging 26.0 yards per reception in the win. the wideout provides head coach Ben Johnson with one of many dynamic pass-catching options ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

news.head: Rome Odunze (calf) active for Week 1
news.body: Rome Odunze (calf) is officially active for Week 1 for the Chicago Bears against the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Odunze is good to go after passing through pregame testing without any setbacks from the calf injury, offering head coach Ben Johnson another dynamic pass-catching option for quarterback Caleb Williams against the Panthers Sunday.

news.head: Tee Higgins racks up 95 yards Sunday
news.body: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-10 targets for 95 yards in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Higgins recorded several big catch and runs in the first half against a strong Texans defense. He remains an upside WR2 heading into next week against the Steelers.

news.head: Tee Higgins totals 59 yards Sunday
news.body: Tee Higgins caught 3-of-6 targets for 59 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: It could have been worse. You could have Ja'Marr Chase catching two passes for 12 yards. It wasn't the most inspiring start to the season for Higgins, but he still had a couple of big catches. He'll remain an upside WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Tee Higgins (foot) cleared for Week 1
news.body: Tee Higgins (foot) is cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.

news.head: Tee Higgins (foot) practices in full again Thursday
news.body: Tee Higgins (foot) practiced in a full capacity again on Thursday.
news.impact: The Bengals will likely have Higgins for their season opener on Sunday, as he has been a full participant at two-straight practices to start the week. Fantasy managers should feel confident starting him if he's fully cleared to play prior to kickoff against the Buccaneers.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has hat trick of touchdowns in win
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 9 of 11 targets for 155 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
news.impact: JSN has been on an absolute tear to start the season, with 277 yards through the first two games. He's looking QB-proof at the moment, and as long as Drew Lock can continue to get him the ball with Sam Darnold still out, JSN is an auto start. Not that you were sitting him anyway. He gets a great matchup against the Commanders next week.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba electric in win Wednesday
news.body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 8-of-11 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown in Wednesday night's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: On Wednesday, Smith-Njigba picked up right where he left off last season, exploding for 122 yards and a touchdown in a big win over the Patriots. He did that with Drew Lock throwing him passes after starter Sam Darnold went down with a hip injury earlier in the game. Fantasy managers should be happy with his performance in this matchup but should keep a close eye on the health of Darnold, as the young wideout's week-to-week ceiling will certainly take a hit if their starting QB misses significant time.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba signs historic four-year extension with Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks signed WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to a four-year, $168.6 million contract extension.
news.impact: Smith-Njigba signs the richest contract extension for a receiver in NFL history with the deal including $120 million in guaranteed money. The 2025 NFL Offensive Player of the Year and Super Bowl Champion went for 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns on 119 receptions last season. He will remain under contract with the Seahawks through the 2031 season.

news.head: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has fifth-year team option exercised by Seahawks
news.body: The Seahawks exercised WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s fifth-year team option for 2027.
news.impact: Henderson added that Smith-Njigba’s 2027 salary is fully guaranteed and should make him roughly $23.85 million. This is expected to be a step towards the two sides agreeing to a long-term extension.

news.head: Rams D/ST plays well in win Monday
news.body: The Rams' D/ST logged two sacks and an interception while allowing just six points in Monday night's blowout win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Los Angeles' defense looked good on Monday night. They held the Giants' offense to just six points on the night, but that was also aided by the multiple key injuries that New York suffered over the course of the night. This unit can be started in a matchup against the Broncos next week, although that is by no means an easy game for them.

news.head: Los Angeles Rams D/ST run over by 49ers
news.body: The Los Angeles Rams' D/ST was completely destroyed by the 49ers' offense, and it didn't help that the Rams' offense was equally outmatched, making the final result all the more stark.
news.impact: The Rams still have plenty of star talent on this side of the ball, so don't overreact to one week of football. They should be just fine as the season rolls along once they find their footing.

news.head: Rams D/ST allows 20 points in Week 18 win
news.body: The Rams D/ST allowed 238 passing yards, 79 rushing yards, and 20 points in a 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: The Rams' defense tallied one interception, one fumble, and six sacks in the win. The Rams will head on the road to take on the NFC South champion Carolina Panthers in the first round of the playoffs.

news.head: Los Angeles Rams D/ST has huge touchdown in loss
news.body: The Los Angeles Rams D/ST allowed 27 points with no sacks or turnovers in the Rams 27-24 loss to the Falcons. They did however score a touchdown.
news.impact: The special teams unit came up big late in the loss to the Falcons thanks to a blocked field goal turned touchdown, getting the team back on the board and swinging momentum their way. But it wasn’t enough, as the offense still continued to have its struggles despite some success, and the defense struggled to stop Bijan Robinson all night. It’s a tough loss, but they will look to rebound next week and into the NFL playoffs.

news.head: D'Andre Swift leads quiet offense in Week 2 loss to Vikings
news.body: D'Andre Swift rushed 16 times for 45 yards while also hauling in each of his five targets for a team-high 54 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Swift continues a solid stretch out of the backfield to begin the season, finishing with over 90 offensive yards in each of the first two games. The running back will look to remain one of the more impactful options in the Chicago offense as the season moves on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) good to go for Sunday
news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Swift was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a couple of injuries that he was dealing with, but neither of them are serious and he carries no injury designation heading into the weekend. Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is also good to go, so Chicago's backfield should continue operating as usual in a divisional matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited again Thursday
news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice again on Thursday.
news.impact: The veteran running back was limited for another practice on Thursday, as he is still managing a pair of injuries that are bothering him right now. It doesn't seem likely to affect his availability for Week 2, and fantasy managers shouldn't read much into this issue unless he goes into the weekend with an injury designation.

news.head: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) limited at practice Wednesday
news.body: D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) was limited at Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Swift is a new addition to Chicago's injury report, being listed with a pair of injuries that left him limited at the team's first practice of the week. They may just be taking a cautious approach with his workload at this point, so it's worth keeping an eye on his status throughout the week, especially with backup Kyle Monangai (hamstring) also on the injury report currently.

news.head: Cam Skattebo inefficient in loss Monday
news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 12 times for 36 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.impact: Skattebo was pretty well bottled up on Monday night. He was only able to rush for 36 yards at an inefficient clip of 3.0 yards per carry, and he didn't add much in the passing game outside of four receptions. New York's offense as a whole was a mess with injuries in this game, but the young running back will have ample opportunities to bounce back with matchups against the Titans and Cardinals coming up over the next two weeks.

news.head: Cam Skattebo leads team in rushing Sunday
news.body: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
news.impact: Skattebo looked pretty solid in his first game back from an injury that ended his 2025 season early. He led the team in rushing yards and scored a touchdown against the Cowboys, and he was clearly the team's top RB in terms of carries, outnumbering the next closest back three to one in that area. He didn't see a single target or catch over the course of the night, however. If Devin Singletary and Tyrone Tracy Jr. continue to serve as the team's primary receiving backs, Skattebo's fantasy ceiling could be capped by that on a week-to-week basis.

news.head: Cam Skattebo practices Saturday
news.body: Cam Skattebo participated in Saturday’s practice.
news.impact: Raanan noted that Skattebo was limited, but seemed fine. He left practice early on Friday following a collision, but it had appeared to be precautionary.

news.head: Cam Skattebo suffers apparent injury during practice Friday
news.body: Cam Skattebo left practice early on Friday.
news.impact: Skattebo went down after a collision with LB Arvell Reese. He remained on the sideline, but didn't return to practice. The Giants will be cautious with him.

news.head: Caleb Williams (hamstring) labeled week-to-week with hamstring injury
news.body: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is "week-to-week", per HC Ben Johnson. Initial optimism about his status has given way to reality, and it now seems likely Williams will miss time.
news.impact: It's a bummer for Williams, who looked to be on his way to a great start to the year. Tyson Bagent is the next man up in Chicago, and he's shown promise in previous outings when taking over for Williams.

news.head: Caleb Williams (hamstring) avoids major injury, could play Monday
news.body: Caleb Williams (hamstring) has avoided any major injury to his hamstring, tests have confirmed. It’s well enough that the team isn’t even ruling him out for next week against the Eagles.
news.impact: Williams went down in a heap after scrambling on Sunday and had to be carted off the field. He was later seen walking aroundwithout a limp in the locker room, giving further optimism that he was ok. This confirms that initial assessment, but don’t be surprised if he does miss a week or two out of precaution for his long term health. If he misses time, Tyson Bagent will start in his place.

news.head: Caleb Williams (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.body: Caleb Williams (hamstring) has been ruled out for the Chicago Bears according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Williams was carted you the locker room late in the fourth quarter with the apparent hamstring injury, with backup Tyson Bagent taking over behind center for head coach Ben Johnson Sunday.

news.head: Caleb Williams exits early Sunday
news.body: Caleb Williams exited early with an apparent non-contact injury for the Chicago Bears against the Minnesota Vikings according to Adam Schefter.
news.impact: Williams went down without being touched late in the fourth quarter, completing 15-of-26 pass attempts for 138 yards and one interception while also rushing five times for 42 yards on the day. Tyson Bagent has taken over behind center for head coach Ben Johnson against the Vikings.

news.head: Drake Maye tosses fourth INT of the season in winning effort
news.body: Patriots QB Drake Maye completed 14-of-22 pass attempts for 208 yards and one interception in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers. He added 17 rushing yards on four carries.
news.impact: Maye completed passes to nine different pass catchers in the Patriots' first win of the season. The interceptions continue to plague the young quarterback, as he now has four on the season. Maye and the Patriots will take on the Jaguars in Jacksonville in Week 3.

news.head: Drake Maye throws three interceptions in loss Wednesday
news.body: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passing attempts for 178 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions while adding 47 yards on the ground in Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye started the season on the wrong foot on Wednesday night. He threw for under 200 yards and three interceptions against a tough Seattle defense, including one that cost the Patriots the game. He still showed lots of ability on the ground, however, and he's likely to return to being a good fantasy option against easier defenses. The loss of A.J. Brown (ankle) for at least a few games will severely hamper his short-term upside, however.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) off injury report for Super Bowl
news.body: Drake Maye is not on the injury report for the Super Bowl against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Maye was able to practice fully all week. He is officially good to go for the biggest game of the season on Sunday.

news.head: Drake Maye (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
news.body: Drake Maye was a full participant in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Maye has logged two straight full practices to begin the week. He remains on track to be a full-go on Sunday in the Super Bowl.

news.head: Buccaneers D/ST allows 23 points Sunday
news.body: The Buccaneers D/ST allowed 23 points on 267 total yards with two sacks.
news.impact: It was a prime matchup for Tampa Bay against Deshaun Watson and the Browns offense and they failed to come through. They draw the Vikings next week.

news.head: Buccaneers D/ST put in tough spot Sunday
news.body: The Buccaneers D/ST allowed 26 points on 351 total yards with one interception and one sack on Sunday against the Bengals.
news.impact: Cincinnati scored 33 points, but one of them was off a fumble by Baker Mayfield returned for a touchdown. The Bengals also scored 17 other points off Bucs fumbles. The Bucs will be on the streaming radar in Week 2 against the Browns.

news.head: Buccaneers D/ST recovers two fumbles in Week 18
news.body: The Buccaneers D/ST allowed 14 points on 285 total yards with one interception and two fumble recoveries in Week 18 against the Panthers.
news.impact: While the Bucs secondary struggled most of the season, they held their own to close the season while also completely shutting down the Panthers rushing attack. The Bucs also recovered a pair of fumbles and added an interception.

news.head: Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST struggles Sunday against Dolphins
news.body: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST failed to come up with any big plays on Sunday against Quinn Ewers and the Dolphins' offense on Sunday. Tampa Bay fell 20-17 to Miami, its seventh loss in the last eight games.
news.impact: The Buccaneers allowed only 298 yards of total offense and kept the Dolphins to just 4-of-12 on third-down conversions, but they failed to force a turnover and only sacked Ewers twice in the game. It's the second straight game the Buccaneers have not forced a turnover and they have only four in the last six games after registering 16 in their first 10 games. Tampa Bay has a chance for redemption when it hosts Carolina for the NFC South title on Saturday.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) 'expected' to return in Week 3
news.body: Brock Bowers is reportedly "expected" to return this week.
news.impact: It was previously reported that Bowers was expected to practice this week after he returned to practice last Friday. His status will need to be monitored in practice throughout the week.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) will practice this week
news.body: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers will practice this week.
news.impact: Bowers returned to a limited practice last Friday. His status will need to be monitored in practice this week as he hopes to return in Week 3 against the Saints.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) officially inactive for Week 2
news.body: Raiders TE Brock Bowers (knee) is officially inactive for a Week 2 matchup with the Chargers.
news.impact: Bowers was considered a long shot to play this week, but has a chance to return in Week 3. Fantasy managers should expect Michael Mayer to see increased playing time with Bowers out.

news.head: Brock Bowers (knee) not expected to play Sunday
news.body: Brock Bowers (knee) is not expected to play in Week 2 for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Los Angeles Chargers according to Ian Rapoport.
news.impact: Bowers could return as soon as Week 3 for the Raiders according to Rapoport, with Michael Mayer in line for increased touches again in Week 2 against the Chargers.

news.head: Bucky Irving totals 21 touches Sunday
news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 89 yards on 17 carries in the Buccaneers 23-19 loss against the Browns. He also caught 4-of-4 targets for one yard receiving.
news.impact: Irving had one long run of 38 yards, but was otherwise inefficient on the day. He did remain the clear lead back ahead of Kenneth Gainwell. He draws a tough matchup against the Vikings next week.

news.head: Bucky Irving active in passing game Sunday
news.body: Bucky Irving ran for 45 yards and a touchdown on eight carries in the Buccaneers 33-27 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 7-of-7 targets for 48 yards receiving.
news.impact: Irving took advantage of the gamescript in the passing game with Tampa Bay falling behind 21-3 early. He also lost a fumble, but otherwise performed well. He will be an RB2 play next week against the Browns.

news.head: Bucky Irving will be full-go to begin training camp
news.body: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving is “full-go” to begin training camp.
news.impact: Bowles said Irving looked good in practice on Wednesday. He is not being eased into anything. The question going into training camp will be what the split will be between him and Kenneth Gainwell.

news.head: Bucky Irving could see reduced workload to be more effective
news.body: Buccaneers beat reporter Scott Reynolds suggested the team may want to reduce Bucky Irving's workload to allow him to be more effective this season.
news.impact: Reynolds notes that there's a reason why Bucs head coach Todd Bowles has called Irving and Kenneth Gainwell 1A and 1B. The Bucs gave Gainwell a two-year, $14 million deal in free agency and he has reportedly impressed new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Gainwell emerged in a big way with the Steelers last season and it appears he could be in line for another similar role in the backfield for Tampa Bay. Irving is expected to be good to go in training camp, but he missed time earlier in the teams offseason program recovering from a shoulder injury.

news.head: Joe Burrow dealing with soreness
news.body: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Joe Burrow is dealing with soreness.
news.impact: It is unclear how much Burrow will practice on Wednesday. He is day-to-day for now.

news.head: Joe Burrow tosses two touchdowns Sunday
news.body: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Burrow took five sacks, but he was able to avoid any turnovers with a pair of touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase. He'll look to keep it going against the Steelers in a Divisional matchup next week.

news.head: Joe Burrow (back) will start Sunday
news.body: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) will start for the Bengals in their Week 2 matchup with the Texans.
news.impact: Head coach Zac Taylor stated that "he feels good" and is "ready to go." Fantasy managers should expect Burrow to not be limited in his play Sunday, barring him reaggravating his back injury.

news.head: Joe Burrow (back) questionable for Sunday
news.body: Joe Burrow (back) is questionable for the Bengals game against the Texans due to a back injury. Burrow has told the media he would play.
news.impact: The questionable tag is likely a formality given Burrows limited practice status throughout the week. He should be fine and good to go against a Texans defense that just got bulldozed by the Bills.

news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) uncertain for Week 3
news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans did not have an update on Nico Collins’ hamstring injury.
news.impact: Wilson noted that according to a source, Collins is currently not expected to play in Week 3 against the Colts. If he remains sidelined, Dalton Schultz will remain a TE1 with Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel also all seeing expanded roles.

news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.impact: Collins recently suffered a hamstring injury and will not be able to play in Sunday's game as a result. It may cause him to miss more time beyond this game as well, but we likely won't know more about his official recovery timeline until later this week or next. Look for Dalton Schultz, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel to see more work as a result of his absence against the Bengals in Week 2.

news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) not seen practicing Friday
news.body: Nico Collins was not seen at the start of practice on Friday.
news.impact: Collins will likely be ruled out when the injury report is officially released.

news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) officially doesn't practice Thursday
news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) officially did not take part in Houston's practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Collins did not take part in Houston's practice on Thursday, which is no surprise after he was recently diagnosed with a Grade 1 hamstring strain. It looks likely that he will miss Sunday's game against the Bengals, and he could miss another week or two beyond that depending on how his recovery goes. If he misses time, fantasy managers should expect Jaylin Noel, Kayshon Boutte, and Dalton Schultz to all see more work in his absence.

news.head: Christian Watson finds end zone in Week 2 win over Jets
news.body: Christian Watson hauled in four of his team-high 11 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.impact: Watson has been impactful as part of an inconsistent Green Bay offense to begin the season, catching one or more touchdowns on eight or more targets in each of the first two games. The wideout offers fantasy managers one of the few stable options in an underperforming Packer offense ahead of a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.head: Christian Watson scores two touchdowns in big day Sunday
news.body: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings on Sunday.
news.impact: Watson exploded for an 81-yard catch and run score early. He was later found in the end zone again by Jordan Love. He will be an upside WR2 next week against the Jets.

news.head: Christian Watson agrees to four-year, $110 million extension with Packers
news.body: Christian Watson has agreed to a four-year, $110 million extension with the Green Bay Packers. He is the second Green Bay receiver to sign an extension this offseason following Jayden Reed.
news.impact: Watson put together his best season on a per game basis in 2025 after coming back from an injury that forced him to miss the first seven weeks of the season. It’s quite a lot of money for a receiver who has been plagued with health issues and never had more than 620 receiving yards in a year. But to be fair to him, he averaged 13.2 PPR PPG in 2025 and he’s seen by many as a sleeper in 2026. This could certainly be the year he comes alive for the Packers offense.

news.head: Christian Watson does not see the field in Week 18
news.body: Christian Watson was dressed but did not see the field on Sunday during the Packers' 16-3 loss to Minnesota in the final week of the regular season.
news.impact: Watson, along with most of Green Bay's regular starters, did not play on Sunday. He finishes the regular season with 35 catches for 611 yards and six touchdowns in 10 games. He will be back in the starting lineup next weekend for the Wild Card round of the postseason.

news.head: Matthew Stafford tosses four touchdowns in win Monday
news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passing attempts for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: The reigning MVP had a great bounce-back game on Monday night after a disappointing season opener last week. He scored four touchdowns against the Giants and limited his mistakes overall, helping lead Los Angeles to a blowout win over New York. The only questions for him moving forward will be consistency and the health of his wideouts, with Puka Nacua (hip) currently out of the lineup for the Rams.

news.head: Matthew Stafford quiet in loss to Niners
news.body: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards and a pick in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers. He also ran twice for a loss of a yard.
news.impact: Stafford was not in his best form on Thursday, missing throws and looking a little rusty. It's a rough start for a team that was deemed Super Bowl-bound, but he will look to get back on track next week.

news.head: Matthew Stafford expected to have reps managed in training camp
news.body: The Rams are expected to limit the reps for Matthew Stafford in training camp.
news.impact: Stafford’s degenerative back issue cost him almost all of training camp last year, and he went on to have an MVP season. He is expected to have load managment once again throughout training camp as he enters another season.

news.head: Matthew Stafford agrees to one-year, $55 million extension
news.body: Matthew Stafford has agreed to a one-year, $55 million extension with the Rams. He is now under contract for LA for the next two seasons.
news.impact: The Rams are in a Super Bowl window, so this is hardly a surprising move. Stafford will give them the boost they need off of an MVP season to help them continue to compete for the next two years. As for Ty Simpson, it looks like he will be on the Jordan Love trajectory where we will need to wait at least two years to really get a shot as a starter.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) to get in some work Wednesday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) will get in some work during Wednesday's practice session.
news.impact: After making three grabs for 58 yards in Week 1, Pittman missed Week 2's loss to the Patriots due to a foot injury. He should still be viewed as questionable for this Sunday, but Pittman is at least moving in the right direction. Germie Bernard saw an uptick in playing time with Pittman sidelined.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) uncertain for Week 3
news.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he is unsure if Michael Pittman will play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
news.impact: Pittman was sidelined on Sunday with a foot injury he is still working his way back from. Germie Bernard went on to see an expanded role in his absence.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) ruled out Sunday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) has been ruled out for Week 2 for the Pittsburgh Steelers according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Pittman Jr. will be sidelined after struggling to reach the practice field for head coach Mike McCarthy, with Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard in line for increased roles behind No. 1 wideout DK Metcalf against the Patriots Sunday.

news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) questionable to play Sunday
news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
news.impact: Pittman recently suffered a foot injury and missed Pittsburgh's final two practices of the week because of it. He will still have a chance to play in Week 2, as he officially carries a questionable tag ahead of their matchup against the Patriots. DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth will both see an increase in work if the veteran is ruled out for that matchup.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love struggles in loss to Seattle
news.body: Jeremiyah Love ran nine times for 29 yards and caught three passes for 16 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to Seattle.
news.impact: Like the rest of the Cardinals' offense, Love struggled to move the ball against the Seahawks' stout defense. He will face yet another tough matchup next week, as Arizona takes on San Francisco.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) off injury report for Week 2
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is off of Arizona's injury report ahead of their Week 2 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: The rookie running back was dealing with an ankle injury prior to the team's season opener last week, but he was able to play through it against the Chargers and should be able to do the same in Week 2 now that he's off of the injury report entirely. His workload should continue to ramp up in the coming weeks if he can stay healthy.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love finds the end zone in debut
news.body: Jeremiyah Love picked up 41 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Love added a pair of grabs for nine yards to his NFL debut, and despite still being somewhat limited by the ankle sprain he sustained a month ago, the rookie certainly showed promise of things to come. Tyler Allgeier did get six more carries than Love, but that load share should begin to swing the other way as the season moves forward. The Cardinals have a tough matchup with the Seahawks on tap for Week 2.

news.head: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) active for Week 1
news.body: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is active for Week 1 for the Arizona Cardinals against the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Love is good to go after clearing through pregame activities without any setbacks from the injured ankle, with the rookie running back set to share the backfield with free agent Tyler Allgeier against the Chargers.

news.head: Steelers D/ST allows 14 points in Week 2 loss
news.body: The Steelers D/ST allowed 14 points, 208 passing yards, and 136 rushing yards in the 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: The Steelers' defense did tally an interception, a fumble recovery, and three sacks in the losing effort Sunday. The Steelers' defense will be at home against a strong Bengals' offense in Week 3.

news.head: Steelers D/ST scores TD in Week 1 win
news.body: The Steelers D/ST allowed 13 points while scoring a touchdown, forcing two turnovers, and notching four sacks in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Pittsburgh took advantage of the Falcons being forced to start their third-string QB in Cooper Rush. T.J. Watt dominated the whole afternoon as he sealed the game with a 35-yard pick-six in the fourth quarter while also logging two sacks. The Steelers will have a tougher test in Week 2 against the Patriots.

news.head: Steelers hiring Mike McCarthy as head coach
news.body: The Pittsburgh Steelers are working on a deal to sign Mike McCarthy as the organization's next head coach.
news.impact: McCarthy will succeed Mike Tomlin as the head man for the Steelers. Like Tomlin, McCarthy is one of the winningest coaches in NFL history, with a career record of 60.8% and 174 wins (15th). The Steelers value stability, and McCarthy brings that, along with ties to the city.

news.head: Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin stepping down
news.body: After 19 seasons at the helm of the Pittsburgh Steelers, head coach Mike Tomlin is stepping down as the Steel City’s head man.
news.impact: Tomlin was the longest-tenured active head coach in the NFL for one of the steadiest organizations in the league. The Steelers have had just three coaches since 1969, becoming a pillar of institutional stability. Tomlin never had a losing record as a head coach. However, after failing to win a playoff game since 2016, the Super Bowl champion head coach has informed the organization that he will step down, which will heavily impact Pittsburgh’s offseason plans.

news.head: Omarion Hampton scores once in loss Sunday
news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed the ball 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 21 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Hampton was one of the lone bright spots for the Chargers on Sunday. He logged 115 total yards and found the end zone once over the course of the afternoon, though he left something to be desired in the passing game. He should continue to be a good fantasy option moving forward, though the present struggles of Los Angeles' offense may cap his upside from a fantasy perspective.

news.head: Omarion Hampton finds the end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Omarion Hampton rushed for 43 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: A first-round pick in 2025, Hampton carried quite a bit of hype coming into his second NFL season, as did the Chargers' offense as a whole. At least some of that hype immediately died down after a disappointing season debut against a suspect Arizona defense, but it is only one game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Hampton found the end zone on an eight-yard run in the opening quarter, and this Chargers' attack will find its footing at some point. The Raiders are up next.

news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) will not practice Wednesday
news.body: Omarion Hampton is not practicing on Wednesday.
news.impact: Hampton is “working through it” and “doing everything he can” to get the ankle better that sidelined him in Week 18. He should still play in the Wild Card round against the Patriots, but it is possible he's still fighting through the injury.

news.head: Omarion Hampton (ankle) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: Omarion Hampton has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.impact: Hampton will be one of several starters sitting for the Chargers. Kimani Vidal could lead the backfield if he is cleared.

news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. catches five passes Sunday
news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. caught 5-of-6 targets for 54 yards in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: Fannin was able to bounce back after being held without a catch last week. He remains a low-end TE1 heading into next week against the Panthers.

news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. held in check on Sunday
news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. caught two of three targets for 21 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
news.impact: Fannin was held in check on Sunday, along with the rest of the Browns' offense. He will hope for better days next week against the Buccaneers.

news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. (personal) does not practice Friday
news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. missed practice on Friday for personal reasons.
news.impact: It is not an injury related absence for Fannin. He'll likely be back at practice soon.

news.head: Harold Fannin Jr. cleared for training camp activities
news.body: Harold Fannin Jr. (groin) has been cleared to participate in the Browns training camp after undergoing offseason surgery.
news.impact: It turns out Fannin was cleared two weeks ago, it’s just seemingly been kept under wraps. There is much to be decided among the Browns receivers pecking order sharing the field with him, but he should be a favorite to be the Browns top target in the passing game, ala Brock Bowers or Trey McBride-lite.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. goes for 40 yards in Week 2
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. caught three of his eight targets for 40 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Thomas seemed healthy after dealing with a shoulder injury in Week 1. He wound up finishing second on the Jags in all receiving categories while drawing an encouraging eight targets. Thomas is clearly behind Parker Washington in the pecking order, but he appears to be ahead of Jakobi Meyers, making him a solid WR3 in fantasy moving forward. He will face the Patriots in Week 3.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) cleared to play Sunday
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury during the team's season opener last week, but he was able to practice all week and won't miss any time because of it. He has been cleared to play on Sunday and should continue to contribute in his usual capacity for the Jaguars for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) limited again Thursday
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.impact: The young wideout remains banged up, still limited at practice due to a shoulder injury that he suffered in the season opener. It looks more likely than not that he will play in Week 2, but in the off-chance that he's sidelined, Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers will both benefit from his absence.

news.head: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) limited at practice Wednesday
news.body: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) was limited at Jacksonville's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Thomas suffered a shoulder injury in Week 1 which left him limited at practice on Wednesday. It doesn't seem to be a serious issue for the young wideout, but it still could affect his workload in Week 2's matchup against the Broncos. Fantasy managers should continue to pay attention to updates about his status moving forward.

news.head: Texans D/ST totals five sacks Sunday
news.body: The Texans D/ST allowed 20 points on 267 total yards with five sacks on Sunday against the Bengals.
news.impact: Houston was able to get pressure on Joe Burrow all afternoon, but Ja'Marr Chase burned them for a pair of touchdowns. They will face Daniel Jones and the Colts next week.

news.head: Texans defense struggles to contain Bills in Week 1
news.body: The Texans D/ST allowed 36 points on 409 yards of total offense while coming up with two sacks and no takeaways in Sunday's loss to the Bills.
news.impact: The Texans should feature a solid defensive unit this season, but they ran into a potent Bills' offense in Week 1. Powered by QB Josh Allen, the Bills shredded the Texans' pass defense, totaling 334 yards and a couple of scores through the air. Houston did come up with a couple of sacks, but Allen mostly had his way. The Texans will face another top-tier QB when Joe Burrow and the Bengals visit Houston in Week 2.

news.head: Texans D/ST recovers two fumbles in Week 18
news.body: The Texans D/ST allowed 30 points on 354 total yards with one interception, one sack and fumble recoveries on Sunday against the Colts.
news.impact: Houston sat its starters in the second half. They remain one of the top defenses in the NFL. They'll take on Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers in the Wild Card round.

news.head: Houston Texans D/ST force three turnovers in win
news.body: The Houston Texans D/ST forced two fumbles, an interception, and racked up five sacks in the Texans' 20-16 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: The Texans put up a dominant performance once again, showing why they are one of the best units in the league. Both star linemen Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson added sacks to their impressive season totals in the win. They're on a hot streak entering the final week of the NFL regular season.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan leads Panthers receivers in win
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5 of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
news.impact: McMillan's ten targets led the team, with Jalen Coker falling close behind with nine. It's a bummer he didn't connect on more than five, as he could have had a much bigger day. He and Coker are forming a formidable receiving duo in Carolina, and both are startable every week.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan (foot) practices Thursday
news.body: Tetairoa McMillan was at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The Panthers and Cardinals are the first teams to have veterans report to training camp. McMillan had missed most of the spring due to a foot injury.

news.head: Tetairoa McMillan expected to see more slot usage this season
news.body: Cameron Wolfe reports that Tetairoa McMillan is expected to see more usage in the slot this season.
news.impact: McMillan started to see more snaps in the slot during the second half of his rookie season last year. Wolfe notes that the Panthers believe Chris Brazzell II will be able to play on the outside that will allow McMillan the opportunity to play more in the slot. He should be able to take advantage of mismatches in the slot as he looks to take a step forward heading into his second season in the NFL.

news.head: Malik Nabers ends with one catch in loss Monday
news.body: Malik Nabers caught 1-of-4 targets for just one yard in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.impact: Nabers suffered a shoulder injury partway through Monday night's game and briefly left to be evaluated, but he ended up coming back and finishing out the game. He only ended with one catch for a single yard, however, which burned many fantasy managers who were relying on him. Managers should keep close tabs on his health and the health of Jaxson Dart (knee) throughout this week.

news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) returns to Monday Night Football
news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) has returned to the Giants game against the Rams on Monday.
news.impact: Nabers was initially questionable to return with a shoulder injury that appeared to put him in a lot of pain. However, it seems to be just a stinger, and he’s back on the field. It’s worth keeping an eye on though, as another hit could put him right back out.

news.head: Malik Nabers (shoulder) questionable to return to MNF
news.body: Malik Nabers (shoulder) is being checked out by the medical staff on the sideline with a possible shoulder injury. He is questionable to return.
news.impact: It didn't look like much on the field, but Nabers appeared to be in a lot of pain in the immediate aftermath. He is questionable to return.

news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) without injury designation for Week 2
news.body: Malik Nabers (knee) is without an injury designation heading into Week 2.
news.impact: Nabers told reporters that he is dealing with some minor soreness following his return to the field last week, but it doesn't seem to be anything to be concerned about, as he is not listed on the team's injury report at all heading into Week 2 and practiced in full on Thursday. He should be good to go this week and projects to be a great fantasy option for however long as he stays healthy and on the field this season.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd catches touchdown in quiet Week 2 performance
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd rushed six times for 20 yards while also hauling in both of his targets for six yards and one touchdown in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.impact: Lloyd has underwhelmed despite increased touches out of the Green Bay backfield to begin the season, finishing with less than 40 rushing yards in each of the first two games. The running back remains a risky option as part of a running back group leaving a lot to be desired, with a Week 3 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd sees 13 carries Sunday
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd ran for 37 yards on 13 carries in the Packers 39-22 loss against the Vikings. He did not catch his lone target.
news.impact: Lloyd was the lead back in the Packers backfield without Josh Jacobs. He was very inefficient as he averaged less than three yards per carry. He'll be a flex play next week against the Jets.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd will play in preseason
news.body: Packers OC Adam Stenavich confirmed that MarShawn Lloyd will play in the preseason.
news.impact: Stenavich said every day Lloyd is able to practice, he gets more confident his injury issues are fully behind him. He is competing the backup role in the Packers backfield.

news.head: MarShawn Lloyd to be ramped up in training camp
news.body: MarShawn Lloyd is expected to be ramped up early in training camp.
news.impact: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Lloyd doesn't necessarily have a rep count in camp, but learning from past the plan is to "gradually" ramp him up for season. He'll compete for the backup role in training camp.

news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes in Week 2 win
news.body: Patriots TE Hunter Henry caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.impact: Henry led the team in targets and was tied with Romeo Doubs for the team lead in receptions. Henry should continue to see a steady volume with A.J. Brown on injured reserve. The veteran tight end will head to Jacksonville for a Week 3 matchup with the Jaguars.

news.head: Hunter Henry hauls in three passes Wednesday
news.body: Hunter Henry caught three passes for 26 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: New England's offense wasn't very effective on Wednesday night, and Henry was no exception to that. He totaled just 26 scoreless yards against the Seahawks, which left him with a poor fantasy total. His value as a streaming option may be diminished this year with Eli Raridon seemingly primed to be more involved at the tight end position for the Patriots.

news.head: Hunter Henry agrees to two year extension with Patriots
news.body: Hunter Henry has agreed to a two year extension with the New England Patriots. He had one year left remaining on his contract, but is now locked in till the end of 2028.
news.impact: It’s great news for Henry managers, but bad news for Eli Raridon truthers. The rookie and promising young tight end could still break out as Henry ages out, but this certainly puts a damper on his prospects in the short term. But getting back to Henry, he should be a solid target later in fantasy drafts this year.

news.head: Hunter Henry (rest) listed as questionable for Super Bowl
news.body: Hunter Henry is listed as questionable for the Super Bowl next Sunday against the Seahawks.
news.impact: Henry closed the week with a full practice on Friday. He should be good to go heading into next week.

news.head: Chris Olave finds the end zone in Week 2 win
news.body: Chris Olave caught 8-of-10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.impact: Olave was considered questionable to play due to a hamstring injury, but that did not appear to impact him at all against the Ravens. Olave caught a 21-yard touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to tie the game and help pace the Saints to the upset win. Olave will look to continue his strong start to the season in Week 3 against Las Vegas.

news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) officially active for Week 2
news.body: Saints WR Chris Olave (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Ravens.
news.impact: Olave was a late addition to the injury report this week and was listed as questionable to play in Week 2. He immediately becomes the top pass catching option for QB Tyler Shough and the Saints.

news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) expected to play against Baltimore
news.body: Chris Olave (hamstring) is expected to play on Sunday against Baltimore.
news.impact: This is great news for the Saints, who are already down Jordyn Tyson. If Olave sits, Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson would be the primary options for Tyler Shough in the passing game. They're worth starting whether or not Olave plays, but the extra defensive attention given to them if he sits could cap their ceilings a little.

news.head: Chris Olave (hamstring) listed questionable for Week 2
news.body: Chris Olave has been listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Ravens.
news.impact: Olave was able to practice on Friday after he was a late addition to the injury report on Thursday. He should be on the favorable side of questionable, but he'll still need to be monitored on Sunday ahead of kickoff.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.body: Christian McCaffrey gained 23 yards on 10 carries and 43 yards on four catches, scoring twice on the ground in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: The 49ers' rushing attack was not very efficient in Week 2, but McCaffrey did score a pair of one-yard plunges. As usual, the dual-threat back was also active in the passing game. McCaffrey is up to 29 total touches through two games, averaging 4.6 yards per carry and 7.0 yards per reception. The 49ers appear to be capping the 30-year-old's usage a bit, but he's still a clear RB1, particularly in PPR formats, when healthy.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) returned to practice for the 49ers as a full participant on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, McCaffrey returns to being a full participant at practice on Thursday after being given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day. He should be good to go for Week 2 and is primed for a huge workload against the Dolphins, especially now that Kaelon Black (groin) has been added to the injury report for the 49ers.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey (rest) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.body: Christian McCaffrey (rest) did not take part in practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: McCaffrey was a non-participant at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday. The team gave him a routine rest day and he should be back on Thursday, so fantasy managers should have no concerns about him heading into a great Week 2 matchup against the Dolphins.

news.head: Christian McCaffrey racks up 88 scrimmage yards in win
news.body: Christian McCaffrey ran 10 times for 68 yards and caught five of eight targets for 20 yards in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday.
news.impact: McCaffrey surprisingly had a split backfield with Kaelon Black, at least much more than expected. The veteran tied Black in touches, 15 to 15, but had the edge in opportunities, 18 to 15, thanks to receiving. It will be interesting to see if this is a Week 1 fluke or a recurring theme, as Black was involved throughout the game, not just when the game was well in hand. Still, CMC is a top-tier asset, and while today was fine, bigger days are ahead.

news.head: Ladd McConkey underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.body: Ladd McConkey caught three passes for 35 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: McConkey was able to play on Sunday, despite being questionable coming into the week due to an injury he suffered in Week 1. He didn't look very good against the Raiders, however, totaling just 35 yards over the course of the afternoon. He will likely bounce back and return to being a good fantasy option in the near future, but his consistency may be frustrating if Los Angeles' offense continues to struggle.

news.head: Ladd McConkey (ribs) officially active for Week 2
news.body: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (ribs) is officially active for a Week 2 matchup with the Raiders.
news.impact: McConkey is dealing with a cracked rib but was pushing to play through the injury. With McConkey active, fantasy managers should expect him to operate as the top wide receiver for the Chargers in a divisional matchup with the Raiders.

news.head: Ladd McConkey (ribs) pushing to play Sunday
news.body: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is pushing to play on Sunday against the Raiders despite a cracked rib. There is optimism that he will play, as the team did not elevate a wide receiver from the practice squad this week. If he plays, he will be wearing a flak jacket.
news.impact: If Ladd goes, it's hard to imagine sitting him given how important he is to this offense. Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston could get some additional work, but Ladd will be the main man in town if active.

news.head: Ladd McConkey (ribs) questionable for Sunday
news.body: Ladd McConkey (ribs) is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Raiders due to a rib injury.
news.impact: McConkey was a DNP Wednesday and Thursday but got back on the practice field Friday. His chances to play are more on the slim side, but if he plays, you need to start him against this Raiders defense. If he sits, Quentin Johnston and Tre Harris are next in line for targets.

news.head: Brandon Aubrey perfect in Week 2 win
news.body: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three field goal attempts and all four of his extra point attempts in a win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Aubrey connected on field goals from 25, 44, and 60 yards out to help pace the Cowboys to their first win over the season. Aubrey remains one of the best kickers in the league and is a strong start against Baltimore in Week 3.

news.head: Brandon Aubrey misses one kick Sunday
news.body: Brandon Aubrey went 2-for-3 on his extra-point attempts in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Aubrey didn't have a good night on Sunday night. He scored just two points in the team's loss to New York, and he even missed one of his extra-point attempts late in the game. He should bounce back and return to being a good fantasy option sometime in the near future.

news.head: Brandon Aubrey signs four-year extension with Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys signed K Brandon Aubrey to a four-year, $28 million contract extension.
news.impact: Aubrey becomes the first kicker to ever earn $7 million per year and receive $20 million guaranteed. He has established himself as the top kicker in the NFL.

news.head: Brandon Aubrey has until Friday to sign offer sheet with another team
news.body: Cowboys restricted free agent kicker Brandon Aubrey has until Friday to sign an offer sheet with another team.
news.impact: If Aubrey does not sign an offer sheet with another team by Friday, Dallas retains his rights for the 2026 season. He appears likely to remain with the Cowboys.

news.head: Chase Brown sees 20 carries Sunday
news.body: Chase Brown ran for 80 yards on 20 carries in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also caught 3-of-5 targets for two yards receiving.
news.impact: Brown did not find the end zone. He ran well, but it was still a fairly quiet day for him overall for fantasy managers. He'll remain an RB1 against the Steelers next week.

news.head: Chase Brown finds the end zone Sunday
news.body: Chase Brown ran for 56 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 22 yards receiving.
news.impact: Brown did not have the most efficient afternoon, but it still got the job done for fantasy managers. He draws a tougher matchup in Week 2 against the Texans.

news.head: Chase Brown, Bengals in talks on extension
news.body: The Bengals and RB Chase Brown are reportedly in talks on an extension.
news.impact: Brown finished the season strong this past year after a rough first half. He is entering the final year of his rookie contract next season, which would make sense for both sides.

news.head: Chase Brown catches touchdown in loss
news.body: Chase Brown ran 13 times for 72 yards and caught four of six targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Brown closed the 2025 season with a nice fantasy day, totaling 90 scrimmage yards and a score. He struggled early on this season but rounded into form as time went on, and should be a low-end RB1, high-end RB2 for 2026.

news.head: George Kittle finds the end zone in Week 2
news.body: George Kittle secured all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: With his Achilles injury further behind him, Kittle's playmaking ability was on display Sunday. The veteran TE led the 49ers in receiving yards and had the longest gain of the day with a 40-yard pickup. Kittle also scored his first touchdown of the campaign on a 12-yard pass from Brock Purdy early in the third quarter. As long as he's healthy, Kittle is among the top TEs in the league.

news.head: George Kittle (Achilles) good to go for Sunday
news.body: George Kittle (Achilles) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.impact: As expected, Kittle carries no injury designation heading into the weekend and will be available to play against the Dolphins. It seems likely that he will continue to be limited in some capacity, though it looks like the 49ers are planning on ramping his workload up more and more each week moving forward.

news.head: George Kittle (Achilles) limited again Thursday
news.body: George Kittle (Achilles) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.impact: Kittle was limited for another practice on Thursday, which should come as no surprise given that the team is trying to be cautious while he ramps his workload back up after suffering a devastating Achilles injury at the end of last season. He should return to a full workload sometime within the next few weeks if his recovery continues to progress well, at which point he will likely return to being a great fantasy asset for the remainder of the season.

news.head: George Kittle (Achilles) limited at practice Wednesday
news.body: George Kittle (Achilles) was limited at San Francisco's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: San Francisco is still being careful with Kittle's workload at this point, so they left him as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday. He should be able to play on Sunday barring any unforeseen setbacks, however, and will likely continue to ramp up his workload over the next few weeks.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn makes two field goals Sunday
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on 2-of-3 field goal attempts on Sunday.
news.impact: Fairbairn connected on field goals from 37 and 45 yards out. He missed from 58 yards out in the third quarter.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn puts seven points on the board
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn made his only field-goal try and all four of his PATs in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Fairbairn showed off his powerful leg in Sunday's loss, nailing a 58-yard attempt to briefly give the Texans a one-point lead in the fourth quarter. The veteran has been kicking for the Texans since 2017 and remains one of the more reliable options in the league.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn re-signs with Texans
news.body: The Texans re-signed K Ka'imi Fairbairn to a two-year, $13 million deal.
news.impact: Fairbairn will remain in Houston for two more years. He remains one of the top kickers in the NFL and for fantasy managers.

news.head: Ka'imi Fairbairn connects on six field goals in Week 18
news.body: Ka'imi Fairbairn connected on 6-of-6 field goals in Week 18 against the Colts.
news.impact: Fairbairn finishes the season connecting on 44-of-48 field goals. He should continue to be needed heading into the playoffs.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. 'pretty sore' after Week 2
news.body: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Aaron Jones was “pretty sore” after Minnesota’s Week 2 win against the Bears.
news.impact: Jones led the backfield on Sunday with Jordan Mason on injured reserve. DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne are the current backups behind Jones. Jones will need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. leads ground attack in Week 2 win over Bears
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. carried the ball 23 times for 105 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Jones Sr. took advantage of his role as the primary ball-carrier as part of an inconsistent Minnesota offense, rushing for 40 or more yards in each of the first two games. The veteran running back will look for more success in a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) returns to field Sunday
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) returned to the field for the Minnesota Vikings against the Chicago Bears Sunday according to Kevin Seifert.
news.impact: Jones Sr. was back in the huddle after exiting briefly in the fourth quarter due to an apparent knee injury.

news.head: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) is questionable to return for the Minnesota Vikings against the Chicago Bears Sunday according to Mike Garafolo.
news.impact: Jones exited in the fourth quarter, rushing 18 times for 85 yards prior to the injury. DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne take over in the backfield against the Bears.

news.head: Carnell Tate catches three passes in Week 2
news.body: Carnell Tate caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.impact: Tate finished fourth on the team in receiving yards in the close loss to Philly. The rookie has caught seven of his 11 targets for 65 scoreless yards through the first two games of the season. Tennessee will now get ready to take on the Giants in Week 3. Tate will be tough to start in fantasy until Tennessee's passing attack starts to show more life.

news.head: Carnell Tate catches four passes in Week 1
news.body: Carnell Tate caught four of his six targets for 38 yards in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Tate tied for the team lead in targets and receiving yards while finishing second in receptions in his NFL debut. The rookie receiver will surely have bigger games going forward, as the entire Tennessee offense struggled in the season opener. Tate will be a low-end WR3 heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Carnell Tate (stiffness) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Carnell Tate (stiffness) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
news.impact: The rookie is no longer on Tennessee's injury report and is set to make his NFL debut on Sunday. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to his debut game to see if he has the talent and situation of a breakout fantasy player for this season.

news.head: Carnell Tate returns to practice Friday
news.body: Titans rookie WR Carnell Tate returned to practice on Friday.
news.impact: Tate missed practice time earlier this week due to "stiffness." The rookie could see some more reps in Sunday's preseason game against the Seahawks.

news.head: Dalton Schultz explodes for 12 catches Sunday
news.body: Dalton Schultz caught 12-of-14 targets for 140 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Schultz was the Texans pass catcher who stepped up big time in the absence of Nico Collins. He'll remain a strong TE1 play if Collins remains sidelined next week.

news.head: Dalton Schultz (rest) returns to practice Thursday
news.body: Dalton Schultz (rest) returned to practice as a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, the veteran was back at practice on Thursday after getting Wednesday off as a rest day. He should be fully good to go for Week 2 and may be primed for more work than usual with Nico Collins (hamstring) trending towards being sidelined against the Bengals.

news.head: Dalton Schultz (rest) misses practice Wednesday
news.body: Dalton Schultz (rest) missed Houston's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: The veteran tight end was given Wednesday off as a veteran rest day to start the week. He is likely to be back at practice on Thursday and should play in Week 2, barring anything unforeseen between now and then. He remains a fringe streaming option at the tight end position at this point.

news.head: Dalton Schultz hauls in four passes
news.body: Dalton Schultz secured 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Schultz caught a career-high 82 passes last season, and he remains a steady presence in the Texans' offense. The veteran tight end finished second on the team with eight targets, trailing only Nico Collins' 10. Schultz has a limited ceiling, but he's almost always on the TE streaming radar.

news.head: Jaxson Dart (knee) to miss the rest of the season
news.body: Jaxson Dart (knee) will undergo season-ending surgery.
news.impact: Dart had been getting multiple opinions on his ACL injury. Examination shows that the ligament is intact, but Dart will still require surgery that will end his second-season. Jameis Winston will take over as QB1 for the Giants.

news.head: Jaxson Dart (knee) testing reveals knee injury could be season-ending
news.body: Jaxson Dart (knee) has undergone further testing on his injured knee and they have revealed it could be a season-ending injury. What looked like a promising 2026 is quickly turning upside down for the Giants.
news.impact: Dart went down early in the first quarter with a knee injury, and did not return despite pushing to come back into the game. Now with testing revealing that his injuries could be season-ending, it’s a massive blow to fantasy managers. Jameis Winston looked shell shocked for the majority of his snaps, a far cry from the Jameis we’ve come to know and love over the past few seasons. There are a few comforts we can take from his performance, one is the fact that top WR Malik Nabers hurt his shoulder and was playing through pain. The other is that he will not have to face the Rams pass rush again this season. He could still be a streaming option if Dart is out, but don’t start him right away as we want to see a bit more promise of a bounce back first.

news.head: Jaxson Dart believed to have suffered sprained MCL
news.body: Giants QB Jaxson Dart is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL based on the initial exams.
news.impact: Dart underwent X-rays that returned negative. He will undergo an MRI on Tuesday. He is expected to miss some time, but it appears he avoided anything too serious.

news.head: Jaxson Dart (knee) ruled out for rest of Monday Night Football
news.body: Jaxson Dart (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of the Giants' contest against the Rams on Monday night.
news.impact: Dart went down early in the first quarter against the Rams after getting sandwiched between two defenders. From the information on the broadcast, it does sound like Dart is OK, but he is being held out as they do further testing on his knee.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. finished with three receptions in Week 2
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 31 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Dolphins.
news.impact: Samuel fell well short of the 60 total yards and a touchdown he contributed in Week 1, but he was still significantly involved in Week 2. That should remain the case as long as the veteran playmaker is healthy. Samuel has secured 9-of-11 targets for 79 yards through two games. He's also carried the ball once in each contest, gaining 16 yards.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. snags touchdown in win
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. caught six of seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers' 27-7 win over the Rams on Thursday. He also carried the ball once for 12 yards.
news.impact: Samuel looks to have come back to his old role on the 49ers, lining up everywhere and getting the ball put in his hands to make plays. He even had over 70 kick return yards. Samuel just might be a draft-day steal if they are going to use him like this throughout the season.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. starting against Chargers
news.body: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel Sr. will play against the Chargers in the preseason
news.impact: Thursday night's contest could offer a closer look at the type of role Samuel will have in the 49ers' offense this season.

news.head: Deebo Samuel Sr. participates in team drills Saturday
news.body: Deebo Samuel Sr. was participating in team drills at practice on Saturday.
news.impact: Samuel returns to the practice field two days after returning to the 49ers on a one-year deal. He will be a player to continue to monitor throughout training camp heading into the season.

news.head: Josh Downs leads team in receiving Sunday
news.body: Josh Downs hauled in 7-of-9 targets for 72 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: The Colts needed Downs to step up on Sunday night, and he did just that, delivering a team-high 72 yards in a narrow loss to the Chiefs. He seems primed to improve as a fantasy option in the near future with Alec Pierce (heel) seemingly set to miss some time after aggravating an injury.

news.head: Josh Downs catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Josh Downs caught two of his four targets for 37 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Downs saw modest involvement in an underperforming Indianapolis passing attack, finishing third on the team in targets in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more risky pass-catchers entering a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Josh Downs (calf) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens.
news.impact: Downs is not listed on Indianapolis' injury report heading into Week 1, meaning that his calf injury is no longer an issue and that he should be at full health at this point. Indianapolis' distribution of targets should be something fantasy managers keep a close eye on this weekend, but the 25-year old isn't projected to be a strong fantasy asset on his own to start the season.

news.head: Josh Downs (calf) practices Tuesday
news.body: Josh Downs practiced on Tuesday.
news.impact: Downs missed time last week with a calf issue. He is on track to be good to go for the season opener next week.

news.head: Romeo Doubs rebounds after a tough Week 1
news.body: Patriots WR Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 96 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.impact: Doubs had a rough Week 1 but bounced back to lead the Patriots' wide receivers in yardage in Week 2, including an impressive 63-yard reception. With A.J. Brown on injured reserve, Doubs has the opportunity to lead the Patriots' wide receiver room until he returns. Doubs and the Patriots will travel to Jacksonville in Week 3.

news.head: Romeo Doubs fails to log catch Wednesday
news.body: Romeo Doubs didn't haul in any of his three targets in Wednesday night's 10-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Doubs did not get off to a good start with his new team on Wednesday night. He failed to haul in even a single catch against a tough Seattle defense, and he had a costly drop on a very important play late in the game. He should bounce back in the near future and may be a worthwhile fantasy option short-term with A.J. Brown (ankle) expected to miss a bit of time due to injury.

news.head: Romeo Doubs (undisclosed) does not practice Thursday
news.body: Patriots WR Romeo Doubs did not practice on Thursday.
news.impact: It is unclear what Doubs is dealing with as he did not practice on Wednesday either. It should not be a concern this early in training camp.

news.head: Romeo Doubs signs with Patriots
news.body: The Patriots have signed WR Romeo Doubs.
news.impact: The Patriots had a huge hole at wide receiver, especially after releasing Stefon Diggs. They have been in trade talks for AJ Brown, but now land Doubs in free agency. He'll have a chance to potentially step into the No. 1 wide receiver role for Drake Maye and New England. He'll hold more upside for fantasy managers than what he had in a crowded Packers offense.

news.head: Devaughn Vele hauls in five passes in Week 2 win
news.body: Devaughn Vele caught 5-of-7 targets for 64 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.impact: Vele has put together two solid games to open the season, tallying 12 receptions on 16 targets. Vele is the clear WR2 in the Saints' offense and should be poised for another strong performance against the Raiders in Week 3.

news.head: Devaughn Vele finds end zone in Week 1 loss to Lions
news.body: Devaughn Vele hauled in seven of his nine targets for 69 yards and one touchdown in the Saints' 31-30 Week 1 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Vele capitalized on a sizeable role in the New Orleans passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in a losing effort. The wideout looks poised to offer head coach Kellen Moore another impactful pass-catching option in the New Orleans offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens up next.

news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) placed on IR
news.body: The Saints placed Devaughn Vele on injured reserve.
