news.impact: Vele will miss the rest of the season. He finishes the year having caught 25 passes for 293 yards and two touchdowns after being traded to the Saints mid-season.

news.head: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) out on Sunday against Jets
news.body: Devaughn Vele (shoulder) has been ruled out for the Saints game against the Jets on Sunday.
news.impact: Vele was having a bit of a breakout the last few weeks, but that is now on hold. Mason Tipton will likely fill the WR2 role in the offense, but the vacated targets will likely find their way to Chris Olave, Juwan Johnson, and the running backs than Tipton himself seeing a large bump in usage.

news.head: Juwan Johnson hauls in four passes in Week 2
news.body: Juwan Johnson caught 4-of-4 passes for 66 yards in the Saints 24-17 win over the Ravens.
news.impact: Johnson continues to serve as the primary passing option out of the Saints' tight end group. The 30-year-old veteran has topped 50+ receiving yards in the first two games of the season and appears poised to turn in solid performances in an improved Saints' offense. Johnson and the Saints will take on the Raiders in Week 3.

news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) off injury report Week 2
news.body: Juwan Johnson is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
news.impact: Johnson was a late addition to the injury report this week with an illness. He'll be on the TE1/TE2 radar for fantasy managers this week.

news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) returns to practice Thursday
news.body: Juwan Johnson (illness) returned to practice as a limited participant on Thursday.
news.impact: Johnson was back at practice on Thursday after being absent from practice on Wednesday due to an illness of some kind. He should be fully good to go for Sunday's game against the Ravens, and fantasy managers should continue to view him as a viable starter for the foreseeable future, especially with Chris Olave (hamstring) now popping up on the injury report and at risk of missing a bit of time.

news.head: Juwan Johnson (illness) doesn't practice Wednesday
news.body: Juwan Johnson (illness) did not take part in New Orleans' practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Johnson is a new addition to New Orleans' injury report, being listed with an illness of some kind that left him absent from practice on Wednesday. He's likely considered day-to-day at this point and seems to have a good chance to play in Week 2. If he's active he will be worth starting in a big matchup against the Ravens on Sunday.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks goes for 74 yards in Week 2
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks caught five of his six targets for 74 yards in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Wicks finished second on the Eagles in all receiving categories in the close win. The veteran wideout could stay involved as the Eagles lost Dallas Goedert to a knee injury in the game. Wicks is on the radar as a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Bears.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks finds end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks hauled in two of his four targets for 73 yards and one touchdown in the Eagles’ 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders.
news.impact: Wicks made the most of his modest target share in the season opener, averaging 36.5 yards per reception in the win. The wideout offers head coach Nick Sirianni another explosive pass-catching option moving forward, with a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans up next.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks on track to be Eagles WR2
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks is trending towards opening the season as the No. 2 wide receiver for the Eagles to open the season.
news.impact: Wicks continues to impress during training camp, while rookie Makai Lemon misses time with a hamstring injury. He was able to show flashes in Green Bay and could see more consistent opportunity with the Eagles. He'll remain a player to monitor for fantasy managers as well as the health of Lemon.

news.head: Dontayvion Wicks not at Eagles OTAs Wednesday
news.body: Dontayvion Wicks was absent Wednesday at Eagles OTAs.
news.impact: Wicks was acquired by the Eagles in a trade this offseason. He will figure to compete for an immediate role in the Eagles wide receiver room.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell sees 12 targets in Week 2 loss
news.body: Adonai Mitchell hauled in six of his team-high 12 targets for 63 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.impact: Mitchell has taken advantage of his increased role entering the season in the New York passing attack, recording 60 or more receiving yards in each of the first two games. The wideout looks poised to remain one of quarterback Geno Smith's primary pass-catching options as the season continues, with a Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions up next.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell goes for 60 yards in Week 1
news.body: Adonai Mitchell caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Mitchell finished second on the Jets in receiving yards, operating as the team's deep threat. He did most of his damage on a 40-yard pass from Geno Smith. While Mitchell will remain behind Garrett Wilson in the target pecking order, he has some boom/bust potential in a Jets offense that looked much improved from last year. Mitchell settles in as a flex option in Week 2 against Green Bay.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell held without a catch in Week 18
news.body: Adonai Mitchell did not record a reception on three targets in the Jets 35-8 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Mitchell appeared in seven games with the Jets since being acquired in the trade that sent Sauce Gardner to the Colts. This was the first time the 23-year-old was held without a reception since the trade. Mitchell should factor into the Jets' offensive plans for 2026 and should benefit from the return of Garrett Wilson.

news.head: Adonai Mitchell hauls in three passes in Week 17
news.body: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-9 targets for 22 yards in the Jets 42-10 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: Mitchell led the team in targets, seeing four more than the next option in the passing game. The 23-year-old has registered nine or more targets in three of his last six games as he clearly has worked himself into a prominent role in the Jets' offense. The Jets will take on Buffalo in Week 18.

news.head: Quentin Johnston struggles in loss Sunday
news.body: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-5 targets for just seven yards and rushed the ball one time for seven yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense as a while struggled on Sunday, and Johnston was no exception to that. He wasn't able to haul in all but one of his five targets against the Raiders, and he only ended up contributing 14 total yards over the course of the game. He isn't worth rostering in most league formats at this point in the season.

news.head: Quentin Johnston does little in Week 1 loss
news.body: Quentin Johnston came up with only 2-of-6 targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Johnston has finished each of the last two seasons with more than 50 grabs, over 700 yards, and exactly eight touchdowns. Some have him pegged to take the next big step up in his fourth season, but some of that hype will be quelled with this season-opening disappointment. The Chargers' offense just had a difficult time getting much going at all in their first game under new OC Mike McDaniel. Johnston should still produce some valuable stats, and he may have just become a nice buy-low option for fantasy purposes.

news.head: Quentin Johnston not expected to miss much time
news.body: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston is not expected to miss much, if any, practice time.
news.impact: Johnston limped off the field during practice on Tuesday. He is day-to-day for now.

news.head: Quentin Johnston suffers apparent lower body injury
news.body: Quentin Johnston left practice early on Tuesday with an apparent lower body injury.
news.impact: Johnston came up limping after an attempting to make a leaping catch on the sideline. There should be an update provided on his official status when available.

news.head: Rashod Bateman scores in Week 2 loss
news.body: Rashod Bateman caught 7-of-9 targets for 88 yards and a touchdown in the 24-17 loss to the Saints.
news.impact: Bateman found the end zone on a 22-yard touchdown to close out the second half. Bateman was the target of the interception late in the game that allowed the Saints to close out the game. If Zay Flowers (hamstring) is unavailable to play in Week 3, Bateman would serve as the primary wide receiver against Dallas.

news.head: Rashod Bateman sees one target in Week 1
news.body: Rashod Bateman failed to catch his lone target in the Ravens' 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1.
news.impact: Bateman operated as more of an afterthought in a Baltimore passing attack that lost both Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) to injury, but could be in line for increased usage if either of the pass-catchers misses time ahead of a Week 2 contest against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Rashod Bateman back at practice Thursday
news.body: Rashod Bateman returned to practice for Baltimore on Thursday.
news.impact: Bateman had missed the previous two days of practice for the Ravens.

news.head: Rashod Bateman (personal) has not been at Ravens OTAs
news.body: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman hasn't been at voluntary workouts since the first week of offseason program.
news.impact: "He's dealing with some personal things and so he hasn't been here for a little bit," OC Declan Doyle said. The Ravens don't seem to be too worried.

news.head: Tony Pollard not practicing Wednesday due to soreness
news.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Tony Pollard will not practice on Wednesday due to soreness.
news.impact: Pollard and Tyjae Spears both aren't practicing due to what is being described as "soreness". They'll need to be monitored in practice the rest of the week.

news.head: Tony Pollard runs for 64 yards in Week 2 loss
news.body: Tony Pollard carried the ball 14 times for 64 yards and caught his lone target for a one-yard gain in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.impact: Pollard was solid in a tough matchup, averaging 4.6 yards per carry. He has now run for 99 scoreless yards while catching just two passes through the first two games of the season. He will be an RB3 heading into Week 3 against the Giants.

news.head: Tony Pollard held to 35 rushing yards in Week 1
news.body: Tony Pollard carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and lost one yard on his lone catch in a 23-10 loss to the Jets in Week 1.
news.impact: Pollard was quiet with the Titans playing from behind for most of the game. On the bright side, the veteran running back led the backfield with Tyjae Spears getting just three carries. Pollard will look to bounce back as a high-end RB3 in Week 2 against the Eagles.

news.head: Tony Pollard (foot) returns to practice Wednesday
news.body: Tony Pollard returned to practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Pollard missed two practices with a foot issue. He saw four carries in the Titans preseason opener.

news.head: Jake Ferguson finds the end zone twice in Week 2
news.body: Jake Ferguson caught all four of his targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Ferguson was quiet in Week 1, so this was a much needed bounce back performance. The 27-year-old remains the primary pass catching option out of the tight end group. Ferguson will look to build on this performance in Week 3 against the Ravens.

news.head: Jake Ferguson quiet in loss Sunday
news.body: Jake Ferguson caught just two passes for six yards in Sunday night's 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: The veteran tight end didn't make an impact on Sunday night. He was held to just two catches and six total yards against the Giants, which was a symptom of Dallas' offensive struggles against their divisional rivals. Ferguson isn't expected to be fantasy relevant anytime in the foreseeable future.

news.head: Jake Ferguson restructures contract with Cowboys
news.body: The Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson’s contract.
news.impact: Ferguson’s $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. The Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space.

news.head: Jake Ferguson (personal) misses practice Saturday
news.body: Jake Ferguson missed practice on Saturday due to personal reasons.
news.impact: Ferguson was away from the team on Saturday.

news.head: Tre Tucker stellar in win Sunday
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The Raiders were able to pick up an upset win over the Chargers on Sunday, and Tucker played a big part in that. He led the team in receptions and yards over the course of the afternoon, and he also caught a touchdown, which further helped his fantasy total. He will likely have other big games moving forward, but they will be inconsistent and hard to predict, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to return to the lineup.

news.head: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 1
news.body: Tre Tucker caught two of his four targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.impact: Tucker was one of six to catch at least one pass from Kirk Cousins in the season opener, averaging a team-high 13.5 yards per reception. The wideout remains one of many pass-catching options as part of a revamped Las Vegas offense, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Tre Tucker catches two passes in Week 18
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Raiders 14-12 win over the Chiefs.
news.impact: Tucker led the team in targets, but was unable to do much with them Sunday. The 24-year-old will end the season with 696 yards and five touchdowns on 57 receptions.

news.head: Tre Tucker hauls in five passes Sunday
news.body: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-6 targets for 49 yards in the Raiders 34-10 loss against the Giants.
news.impact: Tucker was a safety blanket throughout the afternoon for Geno Smith. He'll be a WR4 in Week 18 against the Chiefs.

news.head: Jordan Addison sees five targets in Week 2 win
news.body: Jordan Addison hauled in two of his five targets for 21 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Addison has struggled to make an impact as part of an underwhelming Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, finishing with two receptions or less in each of the first two games. The wideout remains a high-risk pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.head: Jordan Addison fails to catch pass Sunday
news.body: Jordan Addison did not catch either of his two targets in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Justin Jefferson dominated the targets after Carson Wentz took over behind center. Addison will be in the WR3/WR4 mix heading into Week 2 against a vulnerable Bears defense.

news.head: Jordan Addison (thumb) to miss day or two of practice
news.body: Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said WR Jordan Addison will miss a day or two after jamming his thumb.
news.impact: Addison underwent tests that showed the injury will be short-term. He could return to practice by this weekend.

news.head: Jordan Addison officially has fifth-year option picked up by Vikings
news.body: The Vikings have officially exercised Jordan Addison's fifth-year option.
news.impact: It was reported over a month ago and it is now official. Addison has shown flashes of his potential across his first three seasons, while also being suspended three games for violating the league’s substance abuse policy. He was also arrested for misdemeanor trespassing charges earlier this offseason.

news.head: Khalil Shakir totals 38 yards in win Thursday
news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very impactful on Thursday night, catching just three passes for 38 yards on a night where Buffalo's offense couldn't be stopped. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, although he may be primed for more work than usual for a week or two if DJ Moore (shoulder) has to miss time.

news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 50 yards in win
news.body: Khalil Shakir caught four of six targets for 50 yards in the Bills’ 36-31 win over Houston on Sunday.
news.impact: Shakir operated as Josh Allen’s safety valve underneath with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid working over the top. That’s been Shakir’s role in the past, so don’t expect it to stop any time soon. His upside is capped because of it, but he’s a decent flex play in PPR formats if you need a solid floor.

news.head: Khalil Shakir good to go for Sunday
news.body: Khalil Shakir will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Shakir was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and is expected to be fully good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans. He is not worth starting for fantasy purposes at this point, however, especially with DJ Moore now in town for the Bills.

news.head: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) seen practicing Wednesday
news.body: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) was seen practicing for the Bills on Wednesday.
news.impact: Shakir's availability for Week 1 is currently up in the air due to an undisclosed injury that he's dealing with. He was spotted at practice on Wednesday, however, which bodes well for his availability for the season opener. It remains unclear if he was a limited or full participant.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers held to one catch in Week 2
news.body: Jakobi Meyers caught his lone target for a 28-yard gain in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Meyers didn't record his lone catch of the game until the fourth quarter as he took a backseat to both Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. Meyers has now caught all three of his targets for 68 yards and a touchdown through two games this season. He will be a flex consideration heading into Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) good to go for Sunday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Meyers was on the injury report all week due to a lingering wrist issue, but he is going to be good to go and will play in Sunday's game against the Broncos. Fantasy managers shouldn't trust in his week-to-week consistency at this point in the season, however, especially in what projects to be a tough matchup.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) limited participant Thursday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (wrist) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The veteran was again a limited participant on Thursday, which was to be expected, as the team has left him limited at all of their official practices so far in the regular season. He should be good to go for Week 2 and will see more work than usual if Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is sidelined against the Broncos.

news.head: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) listed as limited Wednesday
news.body: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: The veteran wideout was able to play through his thumb injury last week, but he's not fully over it and it left him limited at practice on Wednesday. He should play through it again this week but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy asset for the foreseeable future, unless Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) misses time for Jacksonville.

news.head: Mark Andrews hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
news.body: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 targets for 49 yards in the Ravens 24-17 loss to the Saints.
news.impact: Andrews ranked second on the team in targets, receptions, and yardage in the loss Sunday. With Zay Flowers (hamstring) out, Andrews should continue to see an increase in targets behind Rashod Bateman. Andrews and the Ravens will take on the Cowboys in Week 3.

news.head: Mark Andrews sees six targets in Week 1 win
news.body: Mark Andrews hauled in four of his six targets for 49 yards in the Ravens' 41-23 Week 1 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Andrews received sizeable volume in the Baltimore passing attack, finishing tied for first in targets in the win. The veteran tight end remains a reliable option ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.

news.head: Mark Andrews catches two passes in Week 18
news.body: Mark Andrews caught two of his three targets for 14 yards in a 26-24 loss to the Steelers in Week 18.
news.impact: Andrews was quiet as the Ravens lost the AFC North and will miss the playoffs. The veteran tight end wraps up his 2025 season with 48 catches for 422 yards and five touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Ravens' games. Andrews' days as an elite tight end appear to be over as the team did not prioritize getting him the ball in 2025.

news.head: Mark Andrews snags four passes in win
news.body: Mark Andrews caught all four of his targets for 28 yards in the Ravens' 41-24 win over the Packers.
news.impact: You would think Andrews would have a better game given the number of points the Ravens put up, but it was almost all done on the ground. He's tough to trust for fantasy at this point.

news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. catches six passes Sunday
news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. caught 6-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Browns 23-19 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
news.impact: Concepcion caught all six targets he saw, but they only resulted in 28 yards. Denzel Boston has appeared to emerge as the WR1 on the Browns offense.

news.head: KC Concepcion snags four passes in loss to Jags
news.body: KC Concepcion caught four of five targets for 43 yards in the Browns' 34-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran the ball three times for 15 yards.
news.impact: While it wasn't a massive day, it was encouraging that Concepcion got touches as both a receiver and out of the backfield, showing the team wanted to get the ball in his hands. A loss is a loss, but brighter days should be ahead for Concepcion.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) returns to practice Tuesday
news.body: KC Concepcion was back at practice on Tuesday at Browns training camp.
news.impact: Concepcion landed hard on his shoulder that forced him out of Monday's practice early. He is back one day later.

news.head: KC Concepcion (shoulder) avoids serious injury
news.body: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion is believed to have avoided a serious shoulder injury on Monday.
news.impact: Concepcion left practice on Monday with a shoulder injury after a hard fall. The team expects him to be fine.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in four passes in Week 2
news.body: Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards and rushed once for two yards in the Steelers 20-3 loss to the Patriots.
news.impact: Freiermuth has logged five targets in both games this season and appears to have built a rapport with Aaron Rodgers. With Michael Pittman dealing with an ankle injury, the veteran tight end could be a solid option heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Bengals.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth finds the end zone in Week 1 win
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in a 20-13 win over the Falcons in Week 1.
news.impact: Freiermuth kicked off the season with a promising outing in the win over Atlanta. He hauled in Aaron Rodgers' lone touchdown pass on a six-yard catch in the second quarter while tying for second on the team in receptions. Freiermuth will settle in as a TE2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 matchup against the Patriots.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth goes for 51 yards in Week 18
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught three of his five targets for 51 yards in a 26-24 win over the Ravens in Week 18.
news.impact: Freiermuth finished third on the Steelers in receiving in the win. The veteran tight end wraps the regular season with 41 catches for 486 yards and four touchdowns while appearing in all 17 of the Steelers' games. He will now prepare to take on the Texans at home in the Wild-Card round of the playoffs.

news.head: Pat Freiermuth hauls in three passes in Week 17
news.body: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 63 yards in the Steelers 13-6 loss to the Browns.
news.impact: Freiermuth saw an increase in targets after Darnell Washington exited the game with a broken arm. With Washington out next week, Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith should see the bulk of the snaps at tight end against the Ravens in a matchup with the Ravens to decide the AFC North.

news.head: Kyle Monangai leads backfield in Week 2 loss
news.body: Kyle Monangai rushed 10 times for 47 yards while also catching both of his targets for 11 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Monangai struggled to make an impact against a strong Minnesota rushing defense, finishing with less than 50 rushing yards in the loss. The running back will look to get back on track in Week 3 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
news.impact: Monangai is going to be good to go for Sunday's game, despite being limited at practice earlier in the week due to a hamstring injury. He shouldn't have any limitations and will likely continue to be an involved backup behind D'Andre Swift in this game and beyond.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
news.body: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) was limited at Chicago's practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Monangai was again limited at practice due to a hamstring injury on Thursday. It doesn't seem like more than a minor issue at this point, however, so fantasy managers should expect Chicago's backfield splits to look normal in Week 2, assuming him and D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) are both cleared to play before game time.

news.head: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) listed as limited Wednesday
news.body: Kyle Monangai (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Monangai is currently listed on Chicago's injury report due to a hamstring and was only able to participate in Wednesday's practice in a limited fashion. It seems more likely than not that this is more precautionary than anything else, but fantasy managers should keep an eye on the team's injury reports throughout the week with both him and starter D'Andre Swift (ankle/knee) dealing with injuries right now.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught two passes for 18 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Gadsden didn't see a lot of opportunities on Sunday, but he was able to capitalize on one of them by scoring Los Angeles' lone touchdown through the air against the Raiders. He still didn't have a great fantasy total, but he may see an increase in work moving forward with David Njoku (knee) possibly needing to miss time.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II hauls in two passes Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Gadsden was clearly the second option at TE behind newly acquired veteran David Njoku on Sunday. However, Gadsden did show off his big-play ability with a 26-yard gain in the second quarter. The hype was real around Gadsden for a time last season, but his fantasy value is capped with Njoku now firmly in the mix. Gadsden is a boom-or-bust option at the moment.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II catches two passes Sunday
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught two passes for 23 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: The rookie was active on Sunday but wasn't able to rack up a good fantasy total against the Broncos. He showed a lot of potential over the course of the regular season, however, which will likely make him an interesting upside option at the tight end position for the 2026 fantasy football season.

news.head: Oronde Gadsden II snags touchdown in loss
news.body: Oronde Gadsden II caught three of six targets for 32 yards and a score in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to Houston.
news.impact: Gadsden saved his fantasy day thanks to a one-yard touchdown pass from Justin Herbert as the Chargers were in comeback mode. He's now rotated between good games and single catch performances for the last month, showing some inconsistency, but that's not abnormal for a rookie tight end.

news.head: Xavier Worthy finds end zone in overtime win Sunday
news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: Worthy saw good involvement with seven targets on Sunday night, although he was only able to turn that into five catches for 25 yards against the Colts. He was able to score on one of those catches, however, which salvaged his night from a fantasy perspective. He should not be considered a strong option at the wide receiver position until we see some more consistent production from him.

news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in win Monday
news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Worthy was Kansas City's most targeted player on Monday night, but he wasn't able to do much with his opportunities, finishing with just three catches for 18 yards against the Broncos. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.head: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) active for Week 1
news.body: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is active for Week 1 for the Kansas City Chiefs against the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Worthy will suit up after being able to practice throughout the week for head coach Andy Reid, joining fellow wideout Rashee Rice (knee) in offering quarterback Patrick Mahomes a full complement of weapons against a strong Denver defense Monday night.

news.head: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) listed as full participant Thursday
news.body: Xavier Worthy (shoulder) was listed as a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: To no surprise, Worthy seems to be over his shoulder injury and was able to practice in full on Thursday. He should be a full go for Week 1 but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy option in a matchup against the Broncos.

news.head: Malik Washington grabs four passes in Week 2 loss
news.body: Malik Washington secured 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Washington has now hauled in seven combined passes over the first two weeks for an average of 13.7 yards. His production to this point is likely an indicator of what to expect for the duration of the season in the Dolphins' anemic offensive attack.

news.head: Malik Washington catches three passes in Week 1 loss
news.body: Malik Washington caught three of his eight targets for 53 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Washington made a modest impact despite leading the team in targets, finishing third on the team in receptions in the loss. The wideout remains another high-risk pass-catching option as part of a Miami offense searching to establish their identity as the season continues, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Malik Washington scores touchdown in loss
news.body: Malik Washington caught three of four targets for six yards and a touchdown while also running twice for 22 yards in the Dolphins’ 38-10 loss to New England on Sunday.
news.impact: Washington failed to get much going as the de facto top target in the Miami offense. He’s did at least score a touchdown, but six yards on three receptions leaves a lot to be desired. He’s a depth option in deep dynasty leagues at best at this point, having failed to take advantage of his opportunities in 2025.

news.head: Malik Washington quiet despite Waddle injury
news.body: Malik Washington was limited to just one reception for four yards on three targets during Sunday's win over the Buccaneers. The wide receiver also added a single carry for one yard but failed to see increased involvement in the passing attack even as Jaylen Waddle missed time with a rib injury.
news.impact: Washington's most notable contribution came on special teams, where he delivered a 47-yard kick return late in the third quarter. He will look to build better chemistry with quarterback Quinn Ewers in the Week 18 regular-season finale against the Patriots.

news.head: Keenan Allen held to one catch Sunday
news.body: Keenan Allen caught 1-of-5 targets for just five yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: The veteran saw five opportunities on Sunday night, but he was only able to haul in one catch for five yards over the course of the night. He hasn't looked very good over the first two games of the season, which mitigates a lot of the optimism surrounding him now that Alec Pierce (heel) seems set to miss time.

news.head: Keenan Allen (rest) full participant Thursday
news.body: Keenan Allen (rest) was a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.impact: As expected, the veteran was a full participant at practice on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. The team was simply limiting his workload as a load management tactic, and he should be fully good to go for Week 2. He may see more work than usual if Alec Pierce (heel) or Ashton Dulin (ankle) are sidelined against Kansas City.

news.head: Keenan Allen (rest) officially limited Wednesday
news.body: Keenan Allen (rest) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: The veteran wideout was limited at Wednesday's practice. The team is intentionally limiting his workload at the start of the practice week, however, so it's nothing that fantasy managers should be concerned with. He should play in Week 2 but projects to be a weaker fantasy option in a tough matchup against the Chiefs this week.

news.head: Keenan Allen hauls in six receptions in Week 1 loss
news.body: Keenan Allen hauled in all of his team-high six targets for 32 yards in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
news.impact: Allen was unable to find much room despite leading the team in receptions, averaging 5.3 yards per reception in the Week 1 loss. The veteran wideout will look to offer head coach Shane Steichem more sizeable impact against a difficult Kansas City Chiefs defense in Week 2.

news.head: Kalif Raymond catches five passes in Week 2 loss
news.body: Kalif Raymond caught all five of his targets for 40 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.impact: Raymond continues to make the most of solid involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout continues to take advantage of his familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's offense, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.head: Kalif Raymond leads pass-catchers in Week 1 win over Panthers
news.body: Kalif Raymond hauled in eight of his team-leading nine targets for 84 yards in the Bears' 59-37 Week 1 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.impact: Raymond made an immediate impact after rejoining his former offensive coordinator in the offseason, finishing first in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the win. The wideout remains one of many dynamic options in a crowded wide receiver room, with a Week 2 contest against the Minnesota Vikings up next.

news.head: Kalif Raymond signs with Bears
news.body: The Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond.
news.impact: Raymond remains in the NFC North after five seasons with the Lions. He will remain in a depth role in the Bears wide receiver room.

news.head: Kalif Raymond catches three passes in Week 18
news.body: Kalif Raymond caught three passes for 52 yards and added three punt returns for 33 yards in the Lions' win over the Bears in the final game of the season.
news.impact: Raymond established himself as another target for Jared Goff over the last five weeks of the regular season. After catching just 13 passes over his first 10 games of the year, Raymond caught at least one pass in each of his last five games and totaled 11 receptions during the stretch.

news.head: Blake Corum totals 92 yards in win Monday
news.body: Blake Corum rushed the ball 12 times for 79 yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Los Angeles' offense looked great on Monday night, and Corum was no exception to that. He put up 92 total yards on just 13 opportunities, although he wasn't able to get into the endzone to put the capstone on that. The Rams' backfield is a situation to continue monitoring, with Corum and Kyren Williams each seeing the same amount of carries in this blowout win.

news.head: Blake Corum totals 54 yards in loss
news.body: Blake Corum ran 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
news.impact: Corum was solid on the ground at 5.4 a carry, but that was about all he had going for him. Without a touchdown or receiving work to go along with his yardage, it was a disappointing fantasy performance. However, his usage is encouraging; the Rams at least trust him enough that they will split Kyren Williams' workload with Corum. It makes him a top-tier handcuff RB, and one that should be rostered in case anything happens to Kyren.

news.head: Blake Corum sees 14 touches in Week 18 win
news.body: Blake Corum rushed for 59 yards on 13 carries and caught his lone target for 10 yards in the Rams 37-20 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Corum and Kyren Williams continue to split time in the backfield for the Rams. With the Rams success this season in getting both running backs involved, it should be expected that the rotation continues throughout the team's playoff run.

news.head: Blake Corum (ankle) officially active for Week 18
news.body: Blake Corum (ankle) is officially active for Week 18.
news.impact: Corum exited Monday's game with an ankle injury and was considered questionable to play against Arizona. Corum will continue to work in a rotation with Kyren Williams in the final game of the regular season.

news.head: AJ Barner runs in touchdown in win over Cardinals
news.body: AJ Barner caught his only target for eight yards and ran in a one-yard touchdown on his only carry in Seattle's 31-7 win over Arizona.
news.impact: Barner's fantasy day was saved by the touchdown, as he hasn't gotten much volume to start the season. He's touchdown-or-bust right now and is best left on the bench or on waivers.

news.head: AJ Barner catches two passes Wednesday
news.body: AJ Barner caught two passes for 13 yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: The Seahawks were able to pick up a win over the Patriots on Wednesday, but they didn't need to get Barner very involved in order to do so. He finished the game with just two catches for 13 yards, and there's not much reason to believe that he will bounce back and become a quality week-to-week option anytime soon.

news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) off injury report Wednesday
news.body: AJ Barner is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Barner practiced all week in full. He'll be a TE2 for fantasy managers going into the season.

news.head: AJ Barner (oblique) logs full practice Monday
news.body: AJ Barner was a full participant in practice on Monday.
news.impact: Barner remains on track to be a full-go for Wednesday’s season opener against the Patriots.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: Boutte continues to learn the playback in his second game with the Texans. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role as an upside WR4/WR5.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte makes only catch in Texans debut
news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired from New England late in the preseason to shore up the Texans' wide receiver corps. His big-play potential is known from the last couple of years with the Patriots, but his targets were predictably limited in an offense that is still relatively new to him. Boutte is a wait-and-see bench stash in standard fantasy leagues.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1
news.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Kayshon Boutte will play in Week 1 against the Bills.
news.impact: Boutte was acquired in a trade with the Patriots back on August 24. Ryans said he has been “picking up the playbook really well.” He'll be a deep threat on the outside for CJ Stroud.

news.head: Kayshon Boutte traded to Texans
news.body: The Patriots are sending WR Kayshon Boutte to the Texans in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick.
news.impact: Boutte has had his name in trade rumors for most of the offseason following the Patriots offseason additions of AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs. Boutte will get a fresh start in a wide open wide receiver room with Houston. He should compete for a role as a field stretcher for the Texans.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson sees nine targets Sunday
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.impact: With Nico Collins sidelined, Hutchinson led Houston in targets. It did not lead to much production. He could be in the streaming conversation in deeper leagues next week if Collins remains sidelined.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson finishes with three grabs in Week 1
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Hutchinson saw the third-most targets from C.J. Stroud on Sunday. The Texans are looking for a No. 2 wide receiver to emerge behind Nico Collins, and though Hutchinson's upside may be limited, he might be the guy at the moment. The fourth-year pro hauled in 35 passes for 428 yards and three scores over 17 games last season.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson totals 84 yards in Week 18
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 5-of-9 targets for 84 yards in the Texans 38-30 win over the Colts.
news.impact: Hutchinson led the Texans in receiving on the day with the starters sitting in the second half. He is unlikely to make a big impact in the playoffs.

news.head: Xavier Hutchinson shut out in Week 12
news.body: Xavier Hutchinson was not targeted in Thursday's 23-19 win over the Bills.
news.impact: Hutchinson was on the field for 21 offensive snaps and had a nine-yard run in the game, but he was not targeted in the passing game for the second time in the last three weeks. The third-year wide receiver has also turned in three games with at least three receptions during the last five weeks. Hutchinson has potential, but he is quite difficult to project for fantasy purposes due to this inconsistency. Notably, starting QB C.J. Stroud (concussion) is expected back for in Week 13, so do not close the door on Hutchinson completely.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed goes for 39 yards in win
news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught three of six targets for 35 yards and ran once for four yards in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Shaheed was second on the team in targets, but it all amounted to less than a quarter of the yards teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba had on his 11 targets. Shaheed can have some spike performances, but especially with Drew Lock being more conservative and locked onto JSN, he's more of a flex play at best right now.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed quiet in win Wednesday
news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for just four yards in Wednesday's 13-10 win over the New England Patriots.
news.impact: The speedy wideout wasn't able to do much on Wednesday, catching just one pass for four yards in the team's win over New England. The injury to starter Sam Darnold (hip) may have played a large role in his lack of production, however, so this isn't a good game to look at in order to discern his true involvement in this offense.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed agrees to three-year deal with Seattle
news.body: Rashid Shaheed has agreed to return to the Seahawks on a three-year, $51 million deal.
news.impact: Shaheed wasn’t what fantasy players hoped he would be in Seattle, managing only 15 receptions for 188 yards after being traded to Seattle despite his deep threat skillset and QB Sam Darnold’s deep throwing ability. However, Shaheed proved his worth in the return game, returning both a punt and kickoff for a touchdown for Seattle. Hopefully in 2026 he sees more work in the receiving game, as his price tag would imply. This likely means Tory Horton’s breakout is at best delayed, if not completely out of the cards with Cooper Kupp also still on the roster with Shaheed and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

news.head: Rashid Shaheed testing free agency
news.body: WR Rashid Shaheed is expected to test free agency after failing to agree on an extension with the Seahawks.
news.impact: Shaheed’s value to the Seahawks largely came from his returning ability. If he signs elsewhere, he could become fantasy-relevant again.

news.head: Woody Marks active in receiving game Sunday
news.body: Woody Marks ran for eight yards on eight carries in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday. He also caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards receiving.
news.impact: Marks and David Montgomery were both completely shut down on the ground. Marks salvaged his afternoon with five receptions. He will be on the flex radar in deeper leagues next week against the Colts.

news.head: Woody Marks gets 10 touches in Week 1
news.body: Woody Marks rushed for 42 yards on nine carries and caught his only target for a two-yard loss in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills.
news.impact: Marks was certainly involved in the offense behind new workhorse back David Montgomery on Sunday. Marks averaged close to 5.0 yards per carry on his nine attempts. He'll remain a useful handcuff to Montgomery for now.

news.head: Woody Marks: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans seeing year two jump
news.body: Texans coach Demeco Ryans said he is seeing a “year two jump” from Woody Marks.
news.impact: Ryans noted specifically that Marks is looking faster and making better decisions compared to his rookie season. The Texans traded for David Montgomery who is expected to lead the backfield, but Marks should play a role behind him.

news.head: Woody Marks (shoulder) questionable to return Sunday
news.body: Woody Marks is questionable to return to Sunday's Divisional Round game on Sunday against the Patriots.
news.impact: The Texans offense is dropping like flies. Nico Collins was ruled out before Sunday's game with Dalton Schultz ruled out during the game. Nick Chubb will be among the players to see more run in the backfield for Houston.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 for the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles according to Ian Rapoport.

news.head: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited participant Wednesday
news.body: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: Croskey-Merritt is managing a groin injury right now and was unable to log a full practice session on Wednesday as a result. There's an off-chance that it will leave him sidelined for Week 1, which would lead to more work for Rachaad White against the Eagles.

news.head: Jonah Coleman finds the end zone in Week 2
news.body: Jonah Coleman carried the ball 10 times for 39 yards and a touchdown while catching all three of his targets for 19 yards in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Coleman got extra work after J.K. Dobbins left early with a hamstring injury. The rookie found the end zone for his first career touchdown on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. If Dobbins is unable to play in Week 3 against the Rams, Coleman will be an RB2 consideration in fantasy leagues. He's a priority waiver add in all formats this week if he's available.

news.head: Jonah Coleman without attempt in NFL debut Monday
news.body: Jonah Coleman did not see a single opportunity in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: There has been a lot of hype about the potential of the rookie over the course of the offseason, but he didn't see even a single opportunity in the three snaps he played in his NFL debut on Monday night. He will likely see involvement in more favorable matchups moving forward, but this start is very discouraging and indicates that he is squarely behind both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey in the pecking order at this point.

news.head: Jonah Coleman could earn immediate role in Broncos backfield
news.body: The belief in Broncos camp is Jonah Coleman could earn an immediate role.
news.impact: Coleman would most likely hold a short-yardage and/or goal line role if he is to play right away. This could end up being a three-man committee with J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

news.head: Jonah Coleman signs rookie deal with Broncos
news.body: The Broncos signed RB Jonah Coleman to a four-year contract.
news.impact: Coleman is likely to open the season as the RB3 in the Broncos backfield behind RJ Harvey and JK Dobbins, though he could hold an immediate short-yardage role. He'll remain a rookie to monitor heading into OTAs and training camp.

news.head: Tre' Harris leads team in receiving Sunday
news.body: Tre' Harris caught 1-of-3 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
news.impact: Harris was the leading receiver for the Chargers on Sunday, and he was able to earn that title with just one 53-yard catch on the afternoon. Fantasy managers shouldn't have high hopes for him moving forward after two underwhelming games to start the season.

news.head: Tre' Harris finishes with three receptions in Week 1
news.body: Tre' Harris caught 3-of-6 targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
news.impact: Harris was at least significantly involved in the passing game Sunday, as the second-year wideout tied a career high in targets set in Week 18 of last season. Harris did not do much with those targets, however, totaling only 20 yards with a long of 11. The second-round pick from 2025 is a fringe redraft option at present.

news.head: Tre Harris inefficient in loss Sunday
news.body: Tre Harris caught 2-of-6 targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 19-3 loss to the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: Harris saw plenty of opportunities on Sunday with six targets, but he wasn't able to take advantage of them and ended up with just two catches for 28 yards. He has had a disappointing rookie campaign and will likely remain a non-factor for the Chargers heading into the postseason.

news.head: Tre Harris quiet in loss to Houston
news.body: Tre Harris caught his only target for eight yards in the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Houston Texans.
news.impact: After back-to-back weeks of at least 49 receiving yards, Harris went back to being the WR4 of the offense and came up with a single reception. In fact, of all the Chargers receivers, only Quentin Johnston had more than a single catch. Harris is off the board for fantasy for now, but is a worthwhile stash in dynasty.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne quiet in loss Sunday
news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for just 11 yards in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.impact: Bourne came back down to earth in Week 2 after a stellar performance in Arizona's season opener a week before. He only caught two passes for 11 yards on Sunday, but Arizona's offense as a whole struggled in this matchup against Seattle, so there's a good chance that he will bounce back and have relevance as a depth piece in most leagues sometime in the near future.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne hauls in eight passes Sunday
news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
news.impact: Well, this was surprising. Bourne outpaced both Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in Sunday's season opener, finishing just one reception behind TE Trey McBride for the team lead. This effort should make Bourne a popular waiver claim for Week 2, but the Cardinals are headed into a tough matchup against the defending Super Bowl champs.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne expected to see more snaps in slot
news.body: Kendrick Bourne is expected to see more playing time in the slot with the Cardinals.
news.impact: Bourne signed with Arizona in free agency this offseason. He is unlikely to hold much fantasy upside outside of a bye week fill-in behind Trey McBride, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson in the passing game.

news.head: Kendrick Bourne signs two-year deal with Cardinals
news.body: The Cardinals agreed to terms with WR Kendrick Bourne on a two-year, $11.47 million contract.
news.impact: Bourne remains in the NFC West with Arizona. The deal has a max value of $16.47 million. He figures to step into a depth role in the Cardinals wide receiver room behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson.

news.head: Rachaad White hauls in six passes in Week 2 loss
news.body: Rachaad White rushed for 43 yards on seven carries in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys. He caught 6-of-6 targets for 40 yards.
news.impact: White saw six targets to Jacory Croskey-Merritt's one target, but both contributed the same amount of yards on the ground. With Jayden Daniels (elbow) out for the foreseeable future, the running game should get more of a focus heading into a Week 3 matchup with Seattle.

news.head: Rachaad White sees nine touches in Week 1
news.body: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 22 yards while also catching both of his targets for five yards in the Commanders’ 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: White made the most of modest touches in the season-opening contest, finishing second to Jacory Croskey-Merritt in touches in the loss. The running back offers more value in PPR formats as the No. 2 backfield option for the Commanders, with a Week 2 contest against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.impact: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

news.head: Rachaad White (hamstring) set to practice Wednesday
news.body: Rachaad White (hamstring) is set to take part in Washington's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: White's status for Week 1 is still unclear right now thanks to a hamstring injury that he's still dealing with. He is taking part in Wednesday's practice, however, which is a step in the right direction for him. Fantasy managers should pay attention to updates about his health throughout the week, as Jacory Croskey-Merritt will be a significantly better fantasy option if the veteran is sidelined this week.

news.head: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won't practice Wednesday
news.body: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won't take part in Miami's practice on Wednesday.
news.impact: The rookie recently suffered an ankle injury and will not be able to practice on Wednesday because of it. That's not a good sign for his availability for Week 3, but fantasy managers should continue to keep tabs on updates about his health throughout the week to see whether or not he will suit up against the Chiefs.

news.head: Caleb Douglas dealing with ankle injury
news.body: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said it's "too early to tell" at this point on WR Caleb Douglas with his ankle.
news.impact: Douglas will need to be monitored in practice this week for his ankle injury.

news.head: Caleb Douglas does little on three targets in Week 2
news.body: Caleb Douglas caught 2-of-3 targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: Douglas had a nice NFL debut, grabbing five passes for 94 yards in Week 1. He came well short of that production against a tougher San Francisco defense in Week 2. Douglas saw 51 snaps for the second straight week, but his output is likely to be volatile all season.

news.head: Caleb Douglas leads pass-catchers in Week 1 loss to Raiders
news.body: Caleb Douglas caught five of his team-high seven targets for 94 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
news.impact: Douglas was the lone bright spot in an underwhelming Miami passing attack, leading the team in receptions and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout will look to provide quarterback Malik Willis with a reliable pass-catching option moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.head: Makai Lemon sees one target in Week 2
news.body: Makai Lemon caught his lone target for a 14-yard gain while losing five yards on his only carry in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.impact: Lemon was quiet in the close win as Philly leaned on DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in the passing attack. Lemon now has just four catches for nine yards through two games as he looks to carve out a larger role in the Eagles' offense. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 3 against the Bears.

news.head: Makai Lemon quiet in Week 1
news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for a loss of five yards on the Eagles’ 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1.
news.impact: Lemon struggled to find any success in the season opener, as the pass-catcher was bottled up by the Commanders defense in the win. The wideout will look for more impactful output in a favorable Week 2 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) practicing in full on Monday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) is back to practicing fully for the first time in weeks. He returned to practice in a limited fashion last week, and is now practicing in full.
news.impact: This is huge for Lemon’s development and integration into the offense. The more reps he gets, especially as a rookie, the better. He’s looking like a potential draft steal if he can continue to stay healthy and improve his game.

news.head: Makai Lemon (hamstring) limited at practice Thursday
news.body: Makai Lemon (hamstring) was limited at Philadelphia's practice on Thursday.
news.impact: The rookie was able to make his return to practice on Thursday. He was sidelined for a little while after suffering a hamstring injury, but it seems that he is progressing well with his recovery, as the team is now letting him practice in a limited capacity. At this rate he will be ready to play in time for the team's season opener, barring any setbacks with his recovery.

news.head: Pat Bryant held without a catch in Week 2
news.body: Pat Bryant was unable to catch his lone target in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2. He did add a 16-yard rush in the win.
news.impact: Bryant was shut out just one week after leading the Broncos in receiving. Such is life as a complementary option in a Sean Payton offense. Bryant will be a boom/bust flex option in fantasy heading into Week 3 against the Rams.

news.head: Pat Bryant leads team in receiving Monday
news.body: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-6 targets for 42 yards in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Bryant was one of the few Broncos who had a respectable showing on Monday night. He looked great at the start of the game but tapered off as it went on and as Denver continued to fall further and further behind on the scoreboard. He was the best out of Denver's receivers in this bad matchup, however, so the breakout potential seems to be there for the second-year wideout this season.

news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) off injury report Sunday
news.body: Pat Bryant is off the injury report for Sunday's AFC Championship game against the Patriots.
news.impact: Bryant closed the week with two straight full practices. He'll be a full-go heading into Sunday.

news.head: Pat Bryant (concussion) limited Wednesday
news.body: Broncos WR Pat Bryant was a limited participant on Wednesday ahead of the AFC Championship.
news.impact: Bryant caught fire early in last week’s Divisional Round, hauling in three receptions in the opening quarter before suffering a concussion. Denver hopes the rookie can clear protocol ahead of Sunday.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson catches three passes in Week 2 win
news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught three of his four targets for 29 yards in the Vikings' 9-3 Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Hockenson has made the most of modest involvement in the Minnesota passing attack to begin the season, recording three of more receptions in each of the first two games. The tight end remains one of the more risky pass-catching options for fantasy managers ahead of a Week 3 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.body: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards in the Vikings 39-22 win over the Packers.
news.impact: Hockenson caught one of the three touchdowns thrown by Carson Wentz. He could be on the TE1 radar in a favorable matchup next week against the Bears.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson restructures contract with Vikings
news.body: The Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
news.impact: Hockenson is coming off one of the worst seasons of his career. He'll now be two years removed from a knee injury he suffered in 2024. The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings.

news.head: T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) ruled out for Week 18
news.body: T.J. Hockenson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.
news.impact: The season is officially over for Hockenson. He had a down year this season when he was healthy compared to his standards. It is unclear what his future looks like in Minnesota.

news.head: Keon Coleman totals 63 yards in win Thursday
news.body: Keon Coleman caught six passes for 63 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.impact: Coleman was able to capitalize on Buffalo's momentum on Thursday night. He finished the game with 63 yards in a win over the Lions, which is the highest total that he has accumulated since Week 1 of last season. He may see more work than usual for a few weeks if DJ Moore (shoulder) has to miss any time.

news.head: Keon Coleman quiet in big win over Houston
news.body: Keon Coleman caught his only target for a yard in the Bills’ 36-31 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.impact: Coleman was very quiet in a game where Josh Allen threw for over 300 yards. He’s off of fantasy radars right now, and will need to show some signs of life before being brought back into fantasy lineups.

news.head: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) without injury designation for Sunday
news.body: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
news.impact: Coleman's foot and toe injuries are no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of the team's season opener on Sunday. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

news.head: Keon Coleman diagnosed with sprained foot/toe
news.body: Bills WR Keon Coleman was diagnosed with a sprained foot/toe in the team's preseason opener.
news.impact: Coleman was seen in a walking boot on Tuesday. Bills head coach indicated he didn’t have much concern.

news.head: Evan Engram hauls in 17-yard pass in Week 2
news.body: Evan Engram caught his lone target for a 17-yard gain in a 20-13 win over the Jaguars in Week 2.
news.impact: Engram was quiet in the comeback win after posting a productive outing back in Week 1. The veteran tight end has now caught five passes for 60 yards and a touchdown through two games. He will be a low-end TE2 in fantasy for Week 3 against the Rams.

news.head: Evan Engram hauls in touchdown Monday
news.body: Evan Engram caught 4-f-5 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 31-10 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.impact: Engram was one of Denver's lone bright spots on offense on Monday night. He caught all but one of his targets against the Chiefs, including one that accounted for the Broncos' lone touchdown in this matchup. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant moving forward, however, and should remain on the waiver wire in most leagues.

news.head: Evan Engram could take on bigger role next season per Broncos GM
news.body: Broncos GM George Paton said the team wants to add to TE Evan Engram’s workload next year.
news.impact: It is also worth noting that Denver has been linked to the top tight end prospects in next week's draft. That will need to be monitored to get a better idea of Engram's role heading into next season.

news.head: Evan Engram leads team in receiving Sunday
news.body: Evan Engram caught 3-of-4 targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 19-3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: The veteran finished as the team's leading receiver on Sunday, despite only racking up a modest 45 yards over the course of the game. He should continue to be an important part of Denver's offense as they now head into the postseason.

news.head: Jalen Nailor quiet in win Sunday
news.body: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.impact: Nailor was a non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass against the Chargers and wasn't able to do much of note with it. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option moving forward, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) set to return to the lineup in the very near future.

news.head: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
news.body: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
news.impact: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.head: Jalen Nailor signs three-year deal with Raiders
news.body: The Raiders agreed to terms with WR Jalen Nailor on a three-year, $35 million contract.
news.impact: Nailor will receive $23 million in guaranteed money. He is looking to step into a bigger role after playing in a limited role in Minnesota. He will be a late-round flier in drafts for now.

news.head: Jalen Nailor expected to have 'robust market' in free agency
news.body: WR Jalen Nailor is expected to have a "robust market" in free agency.
news.impact: Nailor posted a 26/395/4 receiving line last season in Minnesota. His projected market value is $4.7M per year, and he's in line for a multi-year deal. He'll likely seek a WR3 role with another team.

news.head: Mike Gesicki not targeted Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki did not see a target in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
news.impact: Gesicki was coming off a big Week 1 performance. He remains a touchdown dependent TE2 week-to-week.

news.head: Mike Gesicki explodes to open season
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-7 targets for 78 yards with a touchdown in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
news.impact: While Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were fairly quiet on Sunday, it was Gesicki who led the team in receiving. Despite his big Week 1 performance, he still isn't a reliable weekly start yet.

news.head: Mike Gesicki catches two passes in loss
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bengals' 20-18 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Gesicki failed to get much going in this game with the passing attack of Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown taking most of the work. Between the trio of Gesicki, Drew Sample, and Noah Fant, there's just not enough to go around.

news.head: Mike Gesicki totals 47 yards Sunday
news.body: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 47 yards in the Bengals 37-14 win over the Cardinals.
news.impact: Gesicki had a big catch of 32 yards. He will continue to split snaps with Noah Fant in Week 18 against the Browns.

news.head: Braelon Allen reaches end zone in Week 2 loss to Packers
news.body: Braelon Allen rushed five times for seven yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for eight yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.impact: Allen made the most of a forgettable performance as part of an underperforming backfield attack Sunday, scoring his first touchdown of the season in a losing effort. The running back remains more of a complementary option behind No. 1 running back Breece Hall for head coach Aaron Glenn, with a favorable Week 3 contest against the Detroit Lions up next.

news.head: Braelon Allen sees 10 carres in backup role in Week 1
news.body: Braelon Allen carried the ball 10 times for 40 yards and failed to corral his lone target in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
news.impact: Allen mixed in as the backup behind Breece Hall, who handled 22 carries and caught two passes. The Jets will continue to utilize Allen to spell Hall throughout the season, but the former only has fantasy value as a handcuff for the time being. He will take on the Packers at home in Week 2.

news.head: Braelon Allen 'looks spry' in practice Thursday
news.body: Jets reporter Ryan Dunleavy said Braelon Allen "looked spry" in practice on Thursday.
news.impact: Dunleavy added that Allen bounced a couple long runs to the outside. He is working his way back from a season-ending injury and figures to remain in his 1B/backup role behind Breece Hall.

news.head: Braelon Allen (knee) to miss 8-12 weeks
news.body: Braelon Allen (knee) will be out at least eight weeks.
news.impact: The news gets worse regarding Allen's prognosis after he was placed on IR earlier this week. The second-year running back suffered an MCL sprain while returning a kick this past Monday night in Miami, and it was announced Friday morning that he will be out of action for multiple months. Isaiah Davis will likely step into the top backup role behind starting RB Breece Hall for the Jets.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson plays well in win Monday
news.body: Terrance Ferguson caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
news.impact: Ferguson looked great on Monday night. He saw more work than usual with Puka Nacua (hip) out of the lineup for Los Angeles, and he was able to capitalize by putting up 54 yards and scoring a touchdown against the Giants. He has shown his talent and could continue to have week-to-week upside moving forward, although good games will be hard to predict when Nacua makes his return to the lineup.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson quiet in loss to 49ers
news.body: Terrance Ferguson failed to catch his lone target in the Rams' 27-7 blowout loss to the 49ers.
news.impact: The hopeful breakout for Ferguson came to a screeching halt on Thursday, with the tight end failing to garner a target until late in the game, and failing to bring it in at that. However, the entire Rams offense was dysfunctional; no one had a great day for fantasy aside from maybe Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua, depending on your criteria. And second, Ferguson was present on most of the snaps when the starters were in, a big increase from his part time role in 2025. Hopefully, with his snaps now increased, the targets will come. We may just have to wait a week for the Rams to figure out what happened to them and get back on track.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) off injury report for Divisional Round
news.body: Terrance Ferguson is off the injury report for Sunday's Divisional Round game against the Bears.
news.impact: Ferguson is set to return after practicing in full all week. He'll return in his 13 personnel role with the Rams offense.

news.head: Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) practices fully Thursday
news.body: Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson was a full participant in practice on Thursday ahead of the Divisional Round matchup with the Chicago Bears.
news.impact: Ferguson logged consecutive full participations, a strong sign of his ability to play against Chicago. There was previously optimism for his status, and an official designation will be given on Friday.

news.head: Emmett Johnson expected to continue to see more snaps
news.body: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson will continue to get more and more snaps.
news.impact: Reid added that Johnson will see more snaps and take some of the workload off of Kenneth Walker. The rookie has flashed in a limited role over the first two weeks of the season. He remains a solid stash for fantasy managers in his current role.

news.head: Emmett Johnson a non-factor Sunday
news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball two times for 25 yards and caught two passes for 20 yards in Sunday's 33-30 OT win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.impact: The Chiefs didn't give Johnson much work in their close overtime win on Sunday night. He saw just four touches over the course of the game, but he was still able to turn that into an efficient 35 yards. He shouldn't be considered much more than a handcuff fantasy option at this point in the season.

news.head: Emmett Johnson totals 68 yards in NFL debut Monday
news.body: Emmett Johnson rushed the ball eight times for 24 yards and caught two passes for 44 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.impact: The rookie looked good in his NFL debut on Monday night, totaling 68 yards on ten opportunities against one of the NFL's best defensive fronts. Kenneth Walker III is clearly the bellcow running back on this offense, but it looks like Johnson has solidified himself as the RB2 and will continue to play an important depth role for the Chiefs over the course of the season.

news.head: Emmett Johnson signs rookie contract with Chiefs
news.body: The Chiefs signed RB Emmett Johnson to his rookie deal.
news.impact: Johnson was a fifth-round pick of Kansas City. He will compete for a depth role in the Chiefs backfield.

news.head: Brenton Strange catches two balls in Week 2
news.body: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.impact: Strange was quiet in a game where the defenses led the way. The veteran tight end has now caught four of his five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown over two games. He will be on the TE2 radar in fantasy for his Week 3 matchup against the Patriots.

news.head: Brenton Strange grabs touchdown in win over Browns
news.body: Brenton Strange caught two of three targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
news.impact: Strange was among ten other targeted receivers who were trying to feast off of an extremely small pie of 21 total targets. And he was one of the lucky ones with a touchdown. He should continue to see work as the top tight end for the offense, but things are so spread out that it might be hard to rely on him on a weekly basis.

news.head: Brenton Strange signs three-year extension with Jaguars
news.body: The Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
news.impact: The deal is worth “up to” $48 million with $25 million guaranteed. Strange missed five games last season, but emerged as a top threat in the passing game when he was healthy for Trevor Lawrence last season. Strange profiles as a borderline TE1 for fantasy managers with Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol competing for snaps behind him.

news.head: Brenton Strange could be offense’s most important player’ behind Lawrence
news.body: Brenton Strange could the the Jags ‘“most important player” aside from Trevor Lawrence, according to Jags beat John Shipley. Shipley notes than despite missing five games last year, Strange still finished third in routes run.
news.impact: Strange is far and away the Jags TE1, and it doesn’t seem anyone is taking that job away from him. Tanner Koziol is next up as a pass catcher, but the rookie out of Houston is the TE3 at the moment and unlikely to impact Strange’s workload.

news.head: Ryan Flournoy hauls in five passes in Week 2
news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 5-of-6 targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.impact: Flournoy continues to operate as the WR3 in the Cowboys' offense. Fantasy managers could view him as a flex play in deeper leagues heading into Week 3.

news.head: Ryan Flournoy totals 22 yards Sunday
news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in Sunday's loss to the New York Giants.
news.impact: Flournoy wasn't able to contribute much on Sunday night, being held to just 22 yards in the team's upset loss at the hands of the Giants. He won't have enough opportunities to be a relevant fantasy option anytime soon.

news.head: Ryan Flournoy agrees to one-year, $6 million extension with Dallas
news.body: Ryan Flournoy has agreed to a one-year extension with the Dallas Cowboys worth $6 millloon.
news.impact: Flournoy flashed at times last year and is expected to take on a larger role in 2026. He’s coming off of a great second season in the league that saw him snag 40 passes for nearly 500 yards and four touchdowns, including two games with more than 110 yards.

news.head: Ryan Flournoy seeing more work in slot this offseason
news.body: Ryan Flournoy has reportedly "worked in the slot more” this offseason.
news.impact: Flournoy appears to be the favorite to be the WR3 for the Cowboys heading into training camp. He caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season. He is still likely to be off the fantasy radar as part of a deep offense.

news.head: Antonio Williams hauls in three passes in Week 2
news.body: Antonio Williams caught all three of his targets for 24 yards in the Commanders loss to the Cowboys.
